p:NGA: The Central Bank of Nigeria issues the naira (NGN). Its exposure score is 41 of 100, where 0 means shielded from outside influence and 100 means fully exposed; that is more exposed than 84% of the 194 places with a figure. Of six documented cases, the main ones involve former governor Godwin Emefiele, whom the EFCC (Nigeria's anti-corruption agency) charged in 2024 over banknote printing and foreign exchange allocations. He pleaded not guilty to a separate 20-count charge, and none of these is a verdict. President Tinubu suspended him on 9 June 2023, and President Jonathan suspended governor Sanusi in February 2014. Reuters described Olayemi Cardoso, nominated governor on 15 September 2023, as the former head of Citibank in Nigeria. A swap line, an agreement to borrow another central bank's currency, links it to China: CNY 15 billion against NGN 3.28 trillion, dated 27 December 2024.
p:IDN: Bank Indonesia is the central bank of Indonesia and issues the rupiah, printed by Perum Peruri, the state banknote printing firm, at Karawang in West Java. The country scores 32 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. In October 2011 Securency and Note Printing Australia, both subsidiaries of the Reserve Bank of Australia, pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court of Victoria to conspiring to provide benefits to foreign public officials to win the banknote business of Indonesia's note-issuing authority between 1999 and 2001; the officials are not named. Governor Syahril was released in December 2000 after six months in detention, while the administration was pushing to remove him and install its own candidates; he was sentenced to three years in 2002 over the 546 billion rupiah Bank Bali scandal, and in 2004 the Supreme Court acquitted him on all charges. In October 2008 the Corruption Court sentenced former governor Burhanuddin Abdullah to five years for approving 100 billion rupiah of the bank's funds in 2003 to pay officials' legal fees and bribe legislators over an amendment to the bank's law. In July 2014 the anti-corruption court sentenced Budi Mulya to 10 years over a 689.39 billion rupiah loan to Bank Century. In August 2025 the anti-corruption commission named two members of the House as suspects over alleged misuse of the bank's money for social projects; that is unproven.
p:PHL: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas issues the Philippine peso, and the Philippines scores 36 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. Six cases are recorded. In 2005 an internal audit found 5.955 million pesos missing from the Bacolod City branch, and the Ombudsman, the body that investigates officials, found the manager guilty of dishonesty and dismissed him. An examiner who had audited the Rural Bank of Sapang Dalaga took 103,500 pesos in fees from it through another firm, and the anti-graft court, the Sandiganbayan, upheld his conviction and six to seven years in prison. A former supervision officer took a loan from the Rural Bank of Kiamba in 2006; the Ombudsman cleared him in 2011, but the Supreme Court reversed that and ordered charges, which remain unproven. A 2013 complaint that former governor Amando Tetangco Jr and Monetary Board members favoured Allied Bank in its merger with Philippine National Bank was still pending in September 2025, so it is unproven, as is a January 2021 graft complaint against Governor Benjamin Diokno and six officials over a 1.75-billion-peso identity card contract. Four staff were dismissed in July 2024 for falsifying attendance records, and in August 2025 two supervisors drew the maximum penalties. In December 2016 President Rodrigo Duterte told Tetangco he would give him a whack and threatened criminal charges against the Anti-Money Laundering Council that Tetangco chaired, accusing it of not tracking drug money but giving no details; Deputy Governor Diwa Guinigundo said the bank was independent. The notes are produced at the bank's Security Plant Complex, and Note Printing Australia says it has supplied polymer banknotes to the bank.
p:BRA: Brazil's money is the real, issued by the Central Bank of Brazil. On 3 October 2019 the Federal Police and federal prosecutors in Sao Paulo opened Operation Estrela Cadente into leaks of the bank's interest-rate decisions in 2010, 2011 and 2012, said to have benefited a fund of the bank BTG Pactual; the investigation covered corruption, inside information and money laundering and is still open, so nothing is proven. On 21 June 2024 President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva called the bank's president, Roberto Campos Neto, his political and ideological adversary and said Brazil would return to normality once he could replace him. Three leaders crossed between the bank and private finance: Meirelles, president from 2003 to 2010, held posts at BankBoston, FleetBoston and Lazard Americas; Ilan Goldfajn, governor from May 2016 to February 2019, at Banco Itau Unibanco and Credit Suisse Brazil; and Campos Neto came from Santander and was to join Nubank as vice chairman on 1 July 2025, after a legally required six-month wait. Its notes come from Casa da Moeda, contracted on 13 April 2017 for 980 million notes worth 279.14 million reais. Brazil scores 27 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:LUX: Luxembourg uses the euro, so the Central Bank of Luxembourg does the country's central banking while the European Central Bank sets interest rates for the 21 euro countries. Its books are checked by outside accountants on fixed terms: Ernst & Young SA covered the financial years 2019 to 2023, and KPMG Audit S.à r.l. was approved on 12 March 2024 for the years 2024 to 2028. Both cases on file belong to the European Central Bank. The European Ombudsman found maladministration and recommended in January 2018 that ECB president Mario Draghi suspend his membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum that mixes central bankers with private bankers; the ECB declined and he did not. On 18 May 2015 Cœuré told a private evening event in London that the ECB would bring asset purchases forward, and the speech was published only the next morning, which the ECB put down to an internal procedure error. Luxembourg scores 19 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:FIN: Finland uses the euro, so the Bank of Finland does not set interest rates by itself; the European Central Bank sets them for the 21 countries on the currency. The Finnish bank scores 16 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed, and no case is recorded against it. Both findings sit at the European Central Bank. The European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, found maladministration and in January 2018 recommended that president Mario Draghi suspend his membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum of central bankers and private financiers, saying it did not fit the bank's independence; the bank declined and he did not. On 18 May 2015 board member Benoit Coeure told a private evening event in London that the bank would front-load asset purchases, and the speech was published only the next morning, which the bank called an internal procedure error, Draghi saying nothing market-sensitive was revealed. Finland's gold is stored for it by other central banks rather than managed by them: as of 30 October 2013, 51 per cent at the Bank of England, 20 per cent at Sveriges Riksbank, 18 per cent at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and 7 per cent at the Swiss National Bank. PricewaterhouseCoopers Oy audits the accounts for 2026 to 2031.
p:ZAF: South Africa's money, the rand, is issued by the South African Reserve Bank, which is unusual in having private shareholders: 2,000,000 shares held by just over 800 holders, no holder allowed more than 10,000 shares alone or with associates, voting confined to South African residents at one vote per 200 shares, and no shareholder role in monetary policy, financial stability or regulation. A shareholder list as at 30 June 2022, reported secondhand, names the South African Mutual Life Assurance Society at 20,000 shares and the SA Police Widows' and Orphans' Fund at 10,520, both above that cap, with Absa Bank, Discovery, FirstRand, First National Nominees, Beluga Trust and several other companies, trusts and funds at 10,000 each. An Economic Freedom Fighters bill to have the state buy the shareholders out reached parliament's Standing Committee on Finance, where at public hearings on 2 July 2025 the National Treasury called it a forced takeover; no vote or enactment has followed. The one case against the bank ended with the finding thrown out: in June 2017 the Public Protector ordered the bank Absa to repay 1.125 billion rand over an apartheid-era rescue loan the Reserve Bank had made to Bankorp, and on 16 February 2018 the Pretoria High Court set aside that report and its remedy and ordered the Public Protector to pay part of the Reserve Bank's costs herself. Gill Marcus went from chairing Absa Group to governor from 9 November 2009, having been a deputy governor from 1999 to 2004, and former governor Tito Mboweni joined Goldman Sachs as an international adviser in 2010 and again, as a regional adviser, in February 2022; no ethics finding attaches to either move. Its banknotes are printed by the South African Bank Note Company, which the bank says is its own subsidiary, and a parliamentary reply reported in June 2016 said a large share of the country's gold is stored in the vaults of the Bank of England and other offshore bullion centres, then four million ounces, which is storage rather than management. It scores 34 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:LBN: Banque du Liban issues Lebanon's currency, the Lebanese pound. Riad Salameh ran it for three decades until 2023, arriving from Merrill Lynch, where he worked from 1973 to 1993 and managed the personal portfolio of Rafic Hariri, the prime minister who then appointed him governor. A 2023 forensic audit by Alvarez & Marsal found the bank's foreign-currency position swung from a 7.2 billion US dollar surplus at the end of 2015 to a 50.7 billion dollar deficit at the end of 2020 with no loss shown on the balance sheet, and that Salameh set the accounting standards that concealed the losses and decided which banks benefited from financial engineering, unchallenged by the Central Council. The 2018 accounts, signed off with qualifications by EY and Deloitte, carried a 6.82 billion dollar asset called seigniorage on financial stability while the bank helped fund a widening government deficit. On 18 May 2020 the prosecutor Ali Ibrahim charged Mazen Hamdan, the bank's director of cash operations, with illegally manipulating the exchange rate; that charge is unproven. In May 2023 French prosecutors issued an arrest warrant for Salameh over illicit enrichment and alleged laundering of 330 million dollars, and Germany issued a second a week later; he called the French warrant a violation of the law. Arrested in Beirut in September 2024, held about thirteen months and released in September 2025 on bail of more than 14 million dollars, he was indicted with two lawyers in January 2026 over 44.8 million dollars allegedly taken from a consultancy account. He is also under investigation over allegations that more than 300 million dollars was siphoned off between 2002 and 2015 through Forry Associates, a company controlled by his brother Raja. All of it is unproven, and both brothers deny wrongdoing. The bank holds 286.8 tonnes of gold, 74.5 percent of its reserves, and scores 44 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. Press reporting says KPMG was appointed in 2020 to audit the bank's accounts and that its findings have not been made public; this rests on a news report rather than a Banque du Liban document.
p:BEL: Belgium uses the euro, and the European Central Bank sets monetary policy for all 21 countries that use it; the National Bank of Belgium is the country's own central bank. Its 400,000 shares are split evenly: 200,000 registered shares are held by the Belgian State, fixed by law since 1948 and not transferable, and the other 200,000 trade on the Euronext Brussels stock exchange. Belgium scores 28 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. Two findings stand against the European Central Bank. The European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, found maladministration and in January 2018 recommended that its president, Mario Draghi, suspend his membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum whose members include private bankers; the bank declined and Draghi did not suspend it. On 18 May 2015 board member Benoît Cœuré told a private evening event in London that the bank would front-load its asset purchases, and the speech was published only the next morning, which the bank put down to an internal procedure error; Draghi said no market-sensitive information was revealed. Seven career moves between the bank and private finance are recorded, among them Tom Dechaene, who came from Deutsche Bank and the London merchant bank Morgan Grenfell and was made a director by a royal decree of 13 December 2014; those are job changes, not accusations. Most of the bank's 227,402.4 kilograms of gold is stored at the Bank of England, a much smaller portion at the Bank for International Settlements and the Bank of Canada, and a very limited quantity in the bank's own premises — storage, not management of the holding.
p:KEN: The Central Bank of Kenya is the country's central bank and issues its money. Three cases are on file. In the Goldenberg scandal, the government paid cash subsidies for fictitious gold and diamond exports under President Daniel arap Moi. In March 2006 prosecutors indicted five people, including former governor Kotut and former deputy governor Riungu. They are charged, which is unproven. On 23 March 2006 governor Andrew Mullei was charged with four counts of abuse of office, including hiring his son as a consultant. He denied awarding Sh9 million in contracts irregularly, and no court outcome was found. From 2015 to 2018, Kenya's anti-corruption commission investigated current and former officials over the collapse of Imperial Bank, whose directors said bank officers helped embezzle Sh34 billion. That is under investigation and unproven. Kenya scores 37 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:ARG: Argentina's money is the peso, issued by the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic, which scores 39 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. Luis Caputo, its president from June 2018 until he resigned on 25 September 2018, had headed bond and equity trading at JP Morgan Argentina in the 1990s and presided over Deutsche Bank in Argentina from 2003 to 2008. In January 2010 the government called on governor Martin Redrado to resign after he refused to back a decree releasing 6.6 billion dollars of reserves, then fired him; he resigned that month, the reserves stayed frozen and a court held that the full Congress had to approve their use. Fifteen people, among them Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner and economy minister Axel Kicillof, were tried over the bank's 2015 dollar-futures sales, and the case against all of them was dismissed on 13 April 2021. In May 2023, an election year, the bank advanced a further 140 billion pesos to the Treasury, using 99.2 per cent of the limit agreed with the International Monetary Fund. It is examining at least 900 million dollars bought at the official rate in 2022 and 2023 that allegedly reached the parallel market; the firms deny it and nothing is proven. Its notes have moved around: the state mint, Casa de Moneda, printed 1,000- and 2,000-peso notes under contracts of November 2021, September 2022 and February 2023, the bank partly cancelled them and the mint stopped printing at 10pm on 28 October 2024. Production of the 2,000-peso note had gone to Spain's Fábrica Nacional de Moneda y Timbre, and 20,000-peso notes were imported from China. In July 2026 President Javier Milei announced a bill to bar the bank from funding the state.
p:MEX: Mexico's money is the Mexican peso, and its central bank is the Bank of Mexico, known as Banxico, one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements. Mexico scores 28 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. On 23 March 2022 President Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador announced the bank's unanimous rate rise, from 6 to 6.5 per cent, before the bank published it; on 25 March he said finance minister Rogelio Ramirez de la O, who sits in on board meetings, had told him the evening before, and he apologised to the governor and accepted that the Bank of Mexico law had been violated. Deputy governor Gerardo Esquivel called it an error rather than a leak. People also move between the bank and private finance: Agustin Carstens came from deputy managing director of the International Monetary Fund to be governor from 1 January 2010 to 31 December 2015, and former governor Guillermo Ortiz became chairman of BTG Pactual's Mexico business from 1 January 2016. The bank makes its own notes in every denomination, at two factories of its own in Mexico City and El Salto, Jalisco; the notes it first circulated in 1925 were made by the American Bank Note Company of New York, and printing moved in-house in 1969. Note Printing Australia also says it has supplied the bank with polymer banknotes.
p:IND: India's money is the rupee and its central bank is the Reserve Bank of India, which scores 29 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. One case is recorded and unproven: in December 2016, while 500 and 1,000 rupee notes were being withdrawn from circulation, the Central Bureau of Investigation arrested bank official K. Michael in Bangalore and charged him with converting 15 million rupees of withdrawn notes into 100 rupee notes without legal documentation, with a state bank employee. On 10 December 2018 governor Urjit Patel resigned, giving only personal reasons; media reports said he was annoyed by repeated government efforts to influence policy after a public spat. In September 2010 banknote paper supplier De La Rue said some employees had deliberately falsified paper test certificates, which was reportedly followed by suspension of supply to the bank. Three leaders came from elsewhere: Duvvuri Subbarao, governor from 2008 to 2013, had been a lead economist at the World Bank; Raghuram Rajan was the International Monetary Fund's chief economist from 2003 to 2006 before his appointment in 2013; and Patel arrived as deputy governor in January 2013 from the Fund, Reliance Industries and Boston Consulting Group. Part of India's gold is kept in safe custody with the Bank of England and the Bank for International Settlements, which is storage, not management of the money.
p:EST: Estonia uses the euro, so interest rates are set not by the Bank of Estonia but by the European Central Bank, for the 21 European Union countries that use the currency. The one Estonian case ended in acquittal: on 5 March 1999 the Tallinn City Court found Siim Kallas, a former head of the bank, and Kaju not guilty of abuse of power and of submitting false information over the loss of 10 million US dollars from the North Estonian Bank, a charge of preparing to embezzle having been dropped two weeks earlier; the prosecutor, Jaan Naaber, appealed ten days later. Two findings concern the European Central Bank. In January 2018 the European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, found maladministration and recommended that President Mario Draghi give up his membership of the Group of Thirty, a private forum of central bankers and bank executives; the bank declined and he kept it. And on 18 May 2015 board member Benoît Cœuré told a private London event that the bank would front-load its asset purchases, the speech appearing only the next morning, which the bank put down to an internal procedure error. Six career moves between that bank and private finance are recorded, among them Jorg Asmussen going to the bank Lazard; a job move is not an accusation. The Estonian bank's other ties are to the auditors Ernst & Young Baltic AS and Forvis Mazars and the fund manager BlackRock. It scores 17 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed.
p:MLT: Malta uses the euro, so its interest rates are set by the European Central Bank, in which the Central Bank of Malta takes part. Its books have been checked from outside by two firms: KPMG under an approved term covering the financial years 2019 to 2025, and Deloitte Audit Ltd under a term covering 2023 to 2027. Its own case concerns governor Scicluna, a former finance minister: on 29 May 2024 he pleaded not guilty to fraud over the government's handling of a private hospital contract, the Vitals concession, while he was minister. He stepped aside in July 2024 and was reinstated in July 2025 after the European Central Bank was consulted and raised no objections; the charges remain unproven. Two findings sit at the European Central Bank: the European Union's complaints office found maladministration over president Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a club of central bankers and private bankers, and recommended in January 2018 that he suspend it, which the bank declined and he did not; and a speech of 18 May 2015 to a private London event was published only the next day. Malta scores 26 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed.
p:JPN: The Bank of Japan issues the yen and has capital of 100 million yen, of which the government holds 55 percent and private investors 45 percent through subscription certificates traded on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Those holders have no say in running it, and the bank does not name them. One case is on file: in June 2006 governor Fukui apologised and took a 30 percent pay cut for six months after disclosing that he had kept a 10 million yen investment, made in 1999, in a fund run by Yoshiaki Murakami, who was arrested for insider trading; by then the stake was worth 22 million yen. The bank said he broke no law or internal rule, and he did not resign. Nine people have moved between its Policy Board and private finance, among them Atsushi Mizuno, who joined Credit Suisse the month after his term. Japan scores 35 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:BGR: Bulgaria's central bank is the Bulgarian National Bank. On 1 January 2026 the country swapped the lev for the euro at 1.95583 lev to the euro and joined the Eurosystem, the group of national central banks that works with the European Central Bank, so its governor now sits on the body that sets interest rates. Its own large case concerns Corporate Commercial Bank, Corpbank, which collapsed in June 2014: prosecutors charged two former deputy governors responsible for supervision with failing, from February 2010, to take the measures the law required against the bank, allegedly to benefit its shareholders. Gounev was charged in June 2014 and removed from office by court order that December, and Simeonov about ten months later; neither charge is proven, and the accusation that Corpbank's majority owner embezzled 206 million leva is likewise unproven. The state's Bulgarian National Audit Office checks the books under a continuing legal mandate, Oberthur Fiduciaire AD has handled banknote production since 2014, and Louisenthal supplied the thread, foil and watermark for the 100-lev note that became legal tender on 28 December 2018. The bank is one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements, and belongs to the World Bank Treasury's Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership, which offers advice, training or asset management without the page saying which Bulgaria uses. About 60 per cent of its 41 tonnes of gold sits outside its own vaults, stored at the Bank of England, which stores the metal rather than managing it. Two findings sit at the European Central Bank: the European Ombudsman found maladministration over President Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum whose members include private bankers, and recommended in January 2018 that he suspend it, which the ECB declined; and a speech by Coeure to a private London event on 18 May 2015 about front-loading asset purchases was published only the following morning, which the ECB called an internal procedure error. Kalin Hristov, long a member of the Governing Council and deputy governor for the Issue Department, joined the supervisory board of the commercial DSK Bank in August 2025; no ethics finding is recorded. Bulgaria scores 28 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:AUT: Austria uses the euro: the European Central Bank sets its interest rates, for the 21 euro countries together, with the Oesterreichische Nationalbank taking part; the ECB is one of 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements. The national bank owns its banknote printer, OeBS, which cooperates with two other central-bank-owned printers. Managers of OeBS paid kickbacks to win orders, overcharging Azerbaijan's central bank by 20 percent and Syria's by 14 percent, about 14 million euros. Seven were convicted in October 2014; after a retrial, a Vienna court in February 2018 gave Wolf and Miller 18-month suspended sentences and Meyer 21 months suspended, and acquitted former deputy governor Duchatczek. In January 2018 the European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, ruled that ECB president Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a club of central bankers and private bankers, was maladministration; the ECB declined to drop it. In 2015 a speech by board member Coeure on front-loading asset purchases reached a private London audience the evening before publication; the ECB called this an internal procedure error. BDO Assurance, elected on 23 March 2023, audited the bank's 2025 accounts. Austria scores 22 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:IRL: Ireland uses the euro, so its interest rates are set not by the Central Bank of Ireland but by the European Central Bank, for the 21 European Union states that use the currency. The Irish bank's books are checked from outside by Grant Thornton Ireland, under a term covering 2023 to 2027, and its gold bars are held at the Bank of England, which stores them rather than manages them; the remaining coin stocks stay at the Central Bank of Ireland. In 2008 and 2009 the financial regulator, Neary, said he would retire early over the regulator's handling of 87 million euros in secret directors' loans at Anglo Irish Bank; an internal committee found the matter, discovered in January 2008, was not pursued, partly because a letter from Anglo went missing, and Neary said he was not told until the finance minister raised it in December 2008. Two further findings sit at the European Central Bank. The European Ombudsman found maladministration and in January 2018 recommended that president Mario Draghi suspend his membership of the Group of Thirty, a club of central bankers and private bankers; the bank declined and he kept it. And a speech of 18 May 2015, in which Coeure told a private London event that the bank would front-load asset purchases, was published only the next morning, which the bank put down to an internal procedure error; Draghi said no market-sensitive information was revealed. Seven career moves run between these banks and private finance, among them Matthew Elderfield, the Irish deputy governor and financial regulator, hired by Lloyds Banking Group as director for conduct and compliance from October 2013. Ireland scores 21 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:LTU: Lithuania uses the euro, so the Bank of Lithuania does not set interest rates itself: the European Central Bank sets them for the 21 countries that share the currency, a group Bulgaria joined on 1 January 2026. Lithuania's own case ended in acquittal. An official who monitored the commercial bank Snoras was sacked in November 2011 and charged with letting Snoras keep information from the bank's leadership, including on assets in Swiss banks; a guilty verdict in March 2014 was annulled by a Vilnius court, which found that no crime had been committed, and that ruling can still be appealed to the Supreme Court. Two further cases sit at the European Central Bank. In case 1697/2016/ANA the European Ombudsman found maladministration and in January 2018 recommended that president Mario Draghi suspend his membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum where central bankers sit alongside private financiers such as Citi's chief executive Jane Fraser, saying it was not in keeping with the bank's independence; the bank declined, and Draghi did not suspend it. On 18 May 2015 one of its officials, Cœuré, told a private evening event in London that the bank would bring forward its asset purchases, and the speech was published only the next morning, which the bank put down to an internal procedure error; Draghi said no market-sensitive information had been revealed. Six of that bank's officials have moved to or from private finance, among them Otmar Issing, its former chief economist, who in 2006 took what he called a loose advisory position with Goldman Sachs, and Luis de Guindos, who headed Lehman Brothers and Nomura Securities in Iberia from 2006 to 2008 and became vice-president in 2018. Lithuania's 5.8 tonnes of gold, 466 bars, are all stored at the Bank of England as custodian, none of it at home. UAB Ernst & Young Baltic audited its accounts for 2018 to 2021, UAB ROSK Consulting for 2022 to 2024. It scores 20 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:HRV: Croatia uses the euro, so the European Central Bank sets its monetary policy, for 21 countries in all; the ECB is also one of 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements. The country's own central bank is the Croatian National Bank. In January 2022, after media reports, the Zagreb prosecution and the financial regulator HANFA opened inquiries into whether senior bank officials had traded securities of commercial banks they supervise on inside information. The bank said its executives sold shares before the ban took effect and that trading bonds was not prohibited; the inquiries remain open and nothing is proven. Two further cases concern the ECB: between 2016 and 2018 the European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, found maladministration over ECB president Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a private forum of bankers, and the ECB declined its recommendation that he give it up; and in 2015 a speech on asset purchases was published only the morning after a private London event, which the ECB called an internal procedure error. Ernst & Young d.o.o. audits the Croatian bank's accounts for 2025 to 2027. Croatia scores 28 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:SVK: Slovakia uses the euro, so the National Bank of Slovakia does not set interest rates; the European Central Bank does that for the 21 euro countries. The Slovak bank is also one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements, whose capital is held by central banks alone. Slovakia's own case ended in a conviction: on 29 May 2025 the Specialised Criminal Court found the sitting governor, Kazimir, guilty of paying a 48,000 euro bribe in 2017 and 2018, while he was finance minister, to the head of the tax office in connection with audits of private companies, and fined him 200,000 euros. He denied wrongdoing and said he would appeal, and the offence predates his central bank post. Two findings concern the European Central Bank. The European Ombudsman found maladministration over president Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a private forum of central bankers and bank executives, and recommended in January 2018 that he suspend it; the ECB declined and he did not. And Coeure's remark to a private London event on 18 May 2015 that the ECB would front-load asset purchases was published only the next morning, which the ECB put down to an internal procedure error. The Slovak bank owns 31.694 tonnes of gold in bars, stored for it by the Bank of England as depositary, which safekeeps rather than manages it. Deloitte Audit s.r.o. audited its accounts and Grant Thornton Audit, s.r.o. is the approved auditor for 2024 to 2027. Slovakia scores 23 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:LVA: Latvia uses the euro, so policy is set by the European Central Bank for the 21 countries on the currency, and the Bank of Latvia takes part in it; the Latvian bank is one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements, the bank central banks use among themselves. Former governor Ilmars Rimsevics was convicted of taking a bribe and other material inducements by the Riga District Court on 20 December 2023, sentenced to six years in prison with a five-year ban on public office, and lost about 25,000 euro and several properties to confiscation; he was tried alongside the businessman Maris Martinsons. Two further matters concern the European Central Bank. From 2016 to 2018 the European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, found maladministration and in January 2018 recommended that president Mario Draghi suspend his membership of the Group of Thirty, a private forum of central bankers and bank executives; the bank declined and he did not. On 18 May 2015 Cœuré told a private London event the bank would front-load asset purchases, and the speech appeared only the next morning, which the bank called an internal procedure error; Draghi said no market-sensitive information was revealed. Six officials have moved between that bank and private finance, among them Otmar Issing, who became an international adviser to Goldman Sachs in 2006, with no ethics finding attached. Latvia's gold is stored at the Bank of England, which is custody of a reserve asset rather than management of money, and the bank manages its yen share of euro reserves jointly with the Oesterreichische Nationalbank. SIA Ernst & Young Baltic audited its accounts from 2020 to 2024; Forvis Mazars audits the European Central Bank for 2025 to 2029, where BlackRock was also hired to help design asset-backed securities purchases. Latvia scores 22 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed.
p:SVN: Slovenia uses the euro, so the Bank of Slovenia does not set interest rates itself; the European Central Bank sets them for the 21 countries using the euro. Both are among the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements. The main local matter is the 2013 bank bailout, in which a 960 million euro bail-in, meaning losses forced on investors, hit about 100,000 junior bondholders and shareholders. Police have filed a second criminal complaint alleging abuse of office over it, after a 2016 attempt hit a dead end over procedural errors; the specialised prosecutor has asked the court to investigate, so nothing is proven. That inquiry included a search of the bank's premises on 6 July 2016, over which the European Central Bank's President wrote to Slovenia's prosecutor general and to the European Commission about information seized. Two findings concern the European Central Bank itself: on 18 May 2015 Benoit Coeure told a private London event it would front-load asset purchases before the speech was published; and in January 2018 the European Ombudsman found maladministration and asked Mario Draghi to suspend his membership of the Group of Thirty, a private forum of central bankers and financiers, which the bank declined. Six career moves are recorded between that board and private finance, among them Otmar Issing advising Goldman Sachs and Lorenzo Bini Smaghi leaving to chair Societe Generale, with no ethics finding on them. Slovenia scores 21 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:MYS: Bank Negara Malaysia is the country's central bank and issues the ringgit. Malaysia scores 29 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. Two bribery cases are recorded, both from banknote printing. In July 2011 the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission charged former official Mohamad Daud with taking two bribes of 50,000 ringgit in 2004 and 2005 over a 95 million ringgit contract for the five-ringgit polymer note, won by Note Printing Australia; the court acquitted him on 6 December 2015 and the Attorney-General withdrew the appeal in February 2016. In October 2011 Securency and Note Printing Australia, both belonging to the Reserve Bank of Australia, pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court of Victoria to conspiring to provide benefits to foreign public officials to win banknote business with Malaysia's note-issuing authority between October 2001 and December 2003; no Malaysian official was named, and they paid 19,809,772 and 1,856,710 Australian dollars. Zeti Akhtar Aziz, governor for 16 years until 2016, became group chairman of the fund manager Permodalan Nasional Bhd.
p:HUN: The Magyar Nemzeti Bank issues Hungary's forint and owns outright the company that prints the notes. Hungary scores 32 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. In July 2010 the cabinet went ahead with a bill cutting governor Andras Simor's monthly pay by 75 percent, from about 8 million to 2 million forints, under a cap on all public pay; the European Central Bank said such changes should apply only to future appointments. In December 2011 parliament's constitutional committee tabled an amendment merging the bank with the financial regulator under a head appointed by President Pal Schmitt on Prime Minister Viktor Orban's nomination, cutting Simor to deputy, and Simor said he refused what he called bullying. On 12 March 2024 the bank said a proposed law widening its supervisory board's control could erode its independence. The Constitutional Court ruled on 31 March 2016 that the foundations the bank endowed in 2014 with over 267 billion forints were managing public money, and the Public Procurement Board fined six of them 200,000 forints each. In March 2025 the State Audit Office found mismanagement and losses of hundreds of billions of forints there and filed a criminal complaint. On 21 October 2026 former governor Gyorgy Matolcsy was detained on suspicion of economic fraud and use of a forged private document, which is unproven.
p:GRC: Greece uses the euro, so its interest rates are set by the European Central Bank. The Bank of Greece is unusual in being a listed company: 19,864,886 of its shares trade in Athens. The Greek State holds 1,774,088 of them, 8.93 percent, after taking over 1,309,210 shares from DEKA S.A. when that body was dissolved under a law of 2011. A social security fund, e-EFKA, is listed at 12.4402 percent as of 7 August 2020, but that figure comes from Wikipedia and is not confirmed in a filing by the bank. The bribery case against the governor collapsed: on 29 August 2019 Greek prosecutors dropped charges that Stournaras had taken bribes from the drug company Novartis while he was finance minister, along with charges against six other former senior officials; the allegations reached back to 2001 and predated his central bank post. Two findings concern the European Central Bank, where the European Ombudsman found maladministration and recommended in January 2018 that President Mario Draghi give up his membership of the Group of Thirty, a private forum of central bankers and bank executives, which the bank declined to do, and where a speech of 18 May 2015 told a private London audience about front-loaded asset purchases before it was published. Georgios Provopoulos, governor from June 2008 to 2014, came straight from Greek private banking, having advised Alpha Bank from 1993, held a management role at Emporiki Bank from 2004 and been vice president and chief executive of Piraeus Bank from 2006 to 2008. Greece scores 30 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:TUR: Turkiye's money is the Turkish lira, issued by the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkiye, which has shareholders: at the end of 2025 the Ministry of Treasury and Finance held 55.12 per cent, a share the law bars from falling below 51, the state-owned Ziraat Bankasi 19.22 per cent and Mervak Ic ve Dis Ticaret 5.12 per cent. Four governors have been removed by presidential decree: Murat Cetinkaya in July 2019, after the bank held its rate at 24 per cent; Murat Uysal on 7 November 2020, after the lira lost 30 per cent of its value that year; Naci Agbal on 20 March 2021, four months in and after a rate rise; and Sahap Kavcioglu on 8 June 2023, having cut rates from 19 to 8.5 per cent. His replacement, Hafize Gaye Erkan, joined Goldman Sachs in 2005, was a managing director by 2011 and went to First Republic Bank in 2014, becoming co-chief executive in 2021. Government pressure was reported in 23 of 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018, all of it for lower rates and 21 of those quarters in election periods. In October 2025 Istanbul prosecutors took former deputy governor Sener and six others into custody and arrested him, in an investigation into corruption and tender-rigging in two 2023 tenders at the Interbank Card Center, the national payment network the bank majority-owns; that investigation is open and nothing is proven. The notes are printed at the Banknote Printing Plant, which operates under the bank itself. About 34 tonnes of its gold sit in its own vaults, about 382.9 tonnes are stored at the Turkish exchange company Borsa Istanbul and about 119.2 tonnes at the Bank of England, all safekeeping rather than management. It scores 46 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:BGD: Bangladesh Bank issues the taka, printed at Gazipur by the Security Printing Corporation (Bangladesh) Ltd, known locally as Takshal. On the night of 4 February 2016 attackers used the bank's access to SWIFT, the network banks use to send payment instructions, to take reserves from its account at the New York Federal Reserve: 101 million dollars by The Daily Star's figure, 81 million extracted by Prothom Alo's. A government inquiry's final report of 30 May 2016 hinted that central bank officials were involved, but it was never published and no one had been punished as of 2019. Governor Atiur Rahman resigned on 15 March 2016, having been criticised for not telling Finance Minister Abul Maal Abdul Muhith, who called the bank's handling very incompetent. The Anti-Corruption Commission prosecuted Atiur in February 2025 over the AnonTex loan scam and in June 2025 opened an investigation into him over alleged abuse of power and the Hallmark and S Alam Group frauds; former deputy governor SK Sur was arrested on 14 January 2025 for failing to submit an asset statement, after a 2022 investigation into allegations he helped and gained from PK Halder's loan scam. Neither is proven. Governor Abdur Rouf Talukder resigned on 9 August 2024 citing health, three days after more than a hundred of the bank's own staff stormed his office demanding he go. Its gold is stored abroad rather than managed for it: the Bank of England holds about 188,927 troy ounces, used in lending, Standard Chartered 92,739 ounces and HSBC 93,535. Bangladesh scores 41 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed. Bangladesh Bank's own accounts are audited by two Dhaka firms together, Howladar Yunus & Co. and ACNABIN, whose joint report for 2024-2025 was signed on 26 August 2025 and is addressed to the Government rather than to the bank's board.
p:CYP: Cyprus uses the euro, so interest rates for the Central Bank of Cyprus are set by the European Central Bank, for the 21 countries on the currency. It scores 28 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. Former governor Christodoulos Christodoulou and five others were charged with corruption, money laundering and abuse of office over a payment of 1 million euros made in 2007 by a Greek businessman through Focus Maritime Corporation; on 31 July 2020 judges dismissed the case, ruling he should not be tried twice, and he said he was not bribed. In 2014 he pleaded guilty to six tax offences over the undeclared payment and was jailed for five months, and he faced 29 further charges, none proven, over a payment said to have been made so he would overlook Andreas Vgenopoulos and Marfin Investment Group taking control of Laiki Bank. Governor Panicos Demetriades resigned in March 2014, giving no reason, after the President of Cyprus said he would start proceedings to remove him for not doing his job properly; PricewaterhouseCoopers Limited checked the accounts from outside for 2018 to 2022, and Baker Tilly Klitou and Partners Limited holds that work for 2023 to 2027.
p:NLD: The Netherlands uses the euro, whose rates the European Central Bank sets for the 21 countries on it, and De Nederlandsche Bank is the Dutch central bank inside that system; it scores 22 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. In June 2010 the Scheltema committee, set up by finance minister Wouter Bos, found that the bank had fallen seriously short in supervising DSB bank, missing flaws when licensing DSB in 2005 and being too patient afterwards, though it thought a different approach probably would not have prevented DSB's collapse. Two further findings sit at the European Central Bank: the European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, found maladministration over president Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum of central bankers and private financiers, and in January 2018 recommended he suspend it, which the bank declined and he did not; and a board member's 18 May 2015 remarks in London that the bank would front-load asset purchases were published only the next morning, which the bank put down to an internal procedure error. Wim Duisenberg joined the Dutch bank in 1981 and became chairman in 1982, after three years at the International Monetary Fund and a seat on Rabobank's board. Most of its gold is stored for it rather than managed: 32 per cent at the Bank of England, 18.5 per cent at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and 18.5 per cent at the Royal Canadian Mint in Ottawa. EY Accountants B.V. audits the accounts for 2026 to 2032.
p:FRA: France uses the euro, so the Bank of France does not set rates on its own; the European Central Bank does that for the 21 countries using the currency. France scores 20 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. Jean-Claude Trichet, while governor, was charged with spreading false information and publishing inexact accounts of the state-owned bank Crédit Lyonnais for 1991 to mid-1993, and prosecutors asked for a ten-month suspended sentence; in June 2003 judges cleared him, writing that he had only imprecise or incorrect information about the losses. Jacques de Larosière, a Banque de France governor at the time, was accused alongside him, and the verdict for him is not stated. Two findings stand against the European Central Bank: the European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, found maladministration and in January 2018 recommended that Mario Draghi suspend his membership of the Group of Thirty, which the bank declined and he did not do; and on 18 May 2015 Benoît Cœuré told a private London event that the bank would front-load asset purchases, the speech appearing only the next morning, which the bank called an internal procedure error and which Draghi said revealed nothing market-sensitive. François Villeroy de Galhau was chief operating officer of the BNP Paribas group until 1 May 2015 and took office as governor on 1 November 2015, a career move and not an accusation. The bank prints more than 2.5 billion notes a year at its own works at Chamalières, and stores its gold, 2,436.8 tonnes at the end of May 2023, mainly in its own vault 27 metres underground.
p:LKA: The Central Bank of Sri Lanka issues the rupee. It scores 34 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed, its weakest side being corruption and secrecy around it, at 63. On 14 November 2023 a majority of a five-judge Supreme Court bench ruled that the three Rajapaksa brothers, former governors Cabraal and Lakshman and members of the bank's Monetary Board violated the public trust in their handling of the economy, leading to the 2022 crisis. In June 2019 the Attorney General filed a 23-count indictment against former governor Arjuna Mahendran and nine others over a February 2015 treasury bond auction; these are charges, not findings. Mahendran's term ended on 30 June, and he told the Monetary Board he would not seek reappointment until the parliamentary committee COPE finished its bond inquiry. President Maithripala Sirisena, who had said in June 2015 that he should resign, tweeted that he would name a new governor within hours; Prime Minister Ranil Wickremesinghe said Mahendran could not be removed because the charges had never been proved, and nobody was named that day. Sirisena said in 2017 that he personally removed him, and the Auditor General found a loss of 1.6 billion rupees. The notes are printed at De La Rue Lanka Currency & Security Print (Pvt) Ltd in Biyagama, and Note Printing Australia says it has supplied polymer banknotes to the bank.
p:ITA: The Bank of Italy is Italy's central bank, and because Italy uses the euro its interest rates are set by the European Central Bank. It has shareholders: capital of 7.5 billion euro in 300,000 quotas of 25,000 euro each, held by Italian banks, insurers, social security bodies, pension funds and banking foundations, 173 holders on 30 April 2026, with no holder allowed above 5 per cent since 1 January 2022, up from 3 per cent under Law 5/2014. UniCredit sits at that cap with 15,000 quotas, the pension bodies INARCASSA, ENPAM and Cassa Forense hold 14,800 each, Intesa Sanpaolo 14,736, CNPADC 11,000 and BPER Banca 9,765. On 28 May 2011 a Milan court sentenced former governor Antonio Fazio to four years and a 1.5 million euro fine for market rigging in the 2005 attempt by Banca Popolare di Lodi to take over Antonveneta, prosecutors arguing he had favoured Gianpiero Fiorani's bank over ABN Amro; the appeal court cut that to two years and six months on 28 May 2012, and the Court of Cassation made the conviction final on 28 November 2012. Over Unipol's attempted takeover of BNL he was sentenced to three and a half years in October 2011 and then acquitted, with twelve other defendants, on 30 May 2012. Two findings concern the European Central Bank: the European Ombudsman found maladministration and in January 2018 asked Mario Draghi to suspend his membership of the Group of Thirty, a private forum of central bankers and bank executives, and the ECB declined, so he kept it; and Coeure's remark to a private London event on 18 May 2015 that the ECB would front-load asset purchases was published only the next morning, which the ECB put down to an internal procedure error. Draghi was vice chairman and managing director of Goldman Sachs International from 2002 to 2005 before becoming governor in 2006. Of its 2,452 tonnes of gold, 1,100 tonnes are stored in the bank's own security rooms at Via Nazionale. Deloitte audits the accounts. Italy scores 32 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:POL: Poland's money is the zloty, issued by the National Bank of Poland. Six matters are recorded. In the ArtB cheque-float affair of 1991, those arrested after the company's owners fled included the bank's president, Grzegorz Wojtowicz, who was charged with unintentionally causing bank losses of about 72 billion old zloty; the court acquitted him. In February 2009 the Central Anti-Corruption Bureau detained eight people in a case against the head of a division in the bank's IT and telecommunications department, accused of taking at least 350,000 zloty in bribes to rig tenders between 2001 and 2008; he was charged and nothing is proven. Warsaw's district prosecutors are investigating the disclosure of material classified as secret from the closed part of a Monetary Policy Council meeting on 8 September 2023, and on 12 June 2025 secured documents at the bank's head office after it had twice refused to hand them over. In March 2024 ruling-coalition members of parliament filed a motion to bring the bank's president, Adam Glapinski, before the State Tribunal, the court that hears cases against senior officials, on eight charges, among them bond purchases in 2020 and 2021 said to have indirectly financed the budget deficit by at least 144 billion zloty, and breaching the bank's political neutrality. On 20 August 2024 the Constitutional Tribunal dismissed that attempt, ruling the enabling law unconstitutional; it had earlier held, on 12 January 2024, that a three-fifths majority was needed, where the coalition held 241 of 460 seats against a threshold of 276. A Sejm committee then upheld all eight charges on 9 October 2026, with the full vote still to come in the second half of November 2026; Glapinski and the bank call the accusations groundless, and nothing is proven. Dariusz Filar went from chief economist of Bank Pekao to the Monetary Policy Council, with no ethics finding recorded. The notes are made to the bank's order by Polska Wytwornia Papierow Wartosciowych, and of the 448 tonnes of gold held at the end of December 2024 about three quarters sits abroad, in roughly similar portions in the vaults of the Bank of England and the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, which store the bars rather than manage the holding. It scores 28 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:AUS: The Reserve Bank of Australia issues the Australian dollar, which floats freely. It scores 22 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed, and no government pressure was reported from 2010 to 2018. Its one case came out of its own banknote businesses: in October 2011 the subsidiaries Securency and Note Printing Australia pleaded guilty to conspiring to bribe foreign officials to win banknote work from the note-issuing authorities of Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam and Nepal, paying proceeds-of-crime penalties of 19.8 million and 1.86 million Australian dollars and fines of 480,000 and 450,000. Securency's former chief financial officer got a suspended six-month sentence for false accounting in 2012, the agent Radius Christanto a suspended two-year sentence in 2013. Three governors went into private finance on leaving: Ian Macfarlane to the ANZ board in 2007, Glenn Stevens to Macquarie Group in 2017 and Philip Lowe to Barrenjoey in 2024. Almost all its gold, 80 tonnes as at 30 June 2026, sits at the Bank of England, which holds it as bailee: storage, not management, with title staying with the Reserve Bank.
p:ISR: Israel's money is the shekel and its central bank is the Bank of Israel. It scores 25 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and no government pressure was reported between 2010 and 2018. On 29 April 2002 State Comptroller Eliezer Goldberg reported that former governor Jacob Frenkel unlawfully received hundreds of thousands of shekels when he resigned, approved by a senior official who reported to him; Goldberg did not say whether the money should be demanded back. On 3 February 2009 Globes reported that a draft comptroller report alleged flaws in the bank's supervision of Bank Hapoalim's sub-prime investments, on which Hapoalim wrote off 1.5 billion dollars; the bank said it had responses to all the points, and this is unproven. A comptroller report on 17 October 2012 found supervision of the bank's reserves dealing deficient as those reserves grew from 28 to 75 billion dollars; the bank said some issues had been corrected during the audit. Frenkel, governor from 1991 to 2000, came from the International Monetary Fund and later chaired Merrill Lynch International; he sits in the Group of Thirty alongside private-sector members such as Jane Fraser of Citi and Philipp Hildebrand of BlackRock. Stanley Fischer, governor from 2005 to 2013, came from the World Bank, the IMF and Citigroup. The bank is also one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements.
p:ESP: Spain uses the euro, so the Bank of Spain follows interest rates set by the European Central Bank for 21 countries. It owns four fifths of Imprenta de Billetes S.A., or IMBISA, which prints the euro notes allotted to Spain. In 2002 a Madrid court sentenced De la Concha to six years in prison for falsifying public documents linked to a securities account of former governor Mariano Rubio; a wound-up company, NALVI, had hidden Rubio as the investor from at least 1986, and the ruling could be appealed. On 15 September 2017 the National Court decided not to prosecute the former governor over the 2012 failure of the commercial bank Bankia, and the case was dismissed, a decision described as final. Two further cases sit at the European Central Bank: the European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints watchdog, found maladministration and recommended in January 2018 that Mario Draghi give up his membership of the Group of Thirty, which the bank declined and he did not; and a speech by Benoit Coeure to a private London event on 18 May 2015 was published only the next morning. Spain scores 23 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:PRT: Portugal uses the euro, so interest rates are set by the European Central Bank for all 21 European Union countries on the currency rather than by the Banco de Portugal, which has its notes printed by Valora S.A., a printer it owns. It scores 27 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. A 600-page report by a committee the bank itself appointed, with technical support from Boston Consulting Group, pointed to failures in its supervision of Banco Espirito Santo going back to the start of the previous decade, and said information on the Espirito Santo group and on the bank's operations in Angola was reportedly not used; the Banco de Portugal twice refused parliament's request for the report. On 20 July 2021 Fernando Anastacio, rapporteur of parliament's inquiry into losses at Novo Banco, presented a draft report saying supervision had failed across the board, which remained a draft that the PSD said its deputies would vote against. The committee approved its final report on 27 July 2021, concluding that the rescue of Banco Espirito Santo and the first capitalisation of Novo Banco, of 4,900 million euros, were a political fraud, with criticism of the Banco de Portugal and the European Commission and no officials named. In April 2019, after an EY audit of the management of Caixa Geral de Depositos, the bank's ethics committee examined governor Carlos Costa's request to be excused from matters concerning that bank, where he had been a board member from 2004 to 2006; no conclusion was published. Two findings concern the European Central Bank itself: the European Ombudsman found maladministration over President Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum that includes private financiers, and recommended in January 2018 that he suspend it, which the bank declined; and a speech by Coeure to a private London event on 18 May 2015, saying asset purchases would be front-loaded, was published only the next morning, which the ECB put down to an internal procedure error. Vitor Constancio was governor from 1985 to 1986, an executive director of Banco Portugues de Investimento from 1995 to 2000, governor again until May 2010 and then ECB Vice-President, with no ethics finding recorded. PricewaterhouseCoopers & Associados audits the accounts for 2022 to 2026. Of 382.7 tonnes of gold, about 45 per cent was kept in the bank's own vaults in 2023, 49 per cent at the Bank of England, 5 per cent at the Bank for International Settlements and 1 per cent at the Banque de France; those institutions store the metal, they do not manage it.
p:RUS: The Bank of Russia issues the ruble, and is one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements, the central banks' own bank. It scores 38 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, its weakest side being corruption and secrecy around it. Government pressure was reported in 5 of 37 quarters between 2010 and 2018, every time to cut rates or loosen policy. In October 1994 President Boris Yeltsin fired chairman Viktor Gerashchenko over his part in the Black Tuesday ruble crash and named Tatyana Paramonova in his place; the State Duma rejected her by secret ballot, 107 to 127, opponents saying the constitution barred hiring or firing the bank's chief without the Duma's approval. On 19 October 2005 the Moscow prosecutor's office indicted Alexei Mishin, chief legal expert at the bank's Moscow directorate, and a deputy department head of the tax service, for taking a bribe of 1 million US dollars; at the Moscow City Court on 17 April 2007 prosecutors asked for 15 years for Mishin and 12 years for the tax official Oleg Alekseev, but the verdict is not known, so nothing is proven. After Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Western countries immobilised the bank's assets held in their jurisdictions, put at around 300 billion euros worldwide, and on 12 December 2025 the European Union agreed to freeze 210 billion euros of them indefinitely, replacing six-monthly renewals that Hungary or Slovakia could veto. It holds 2,283 tonnes of gold and has swap lines, standing arrangements to lend each other currency, with China and with Kazakhstan, the latter signed on 28 May 2026 for up to three years. Oleg Vyugin, a First Deputy Chairman of the bank, also held private finance posts at Troika Dialog, Morgan Stanley Bank, MDM Bank, Binbank and Safmar Financial Investments; the CV listing them gives no dates, so the order of the moves is not established, and no ethics finding is recorded. Its accounts are audited by B1 - Audit LLC and by the Accounts Chamber of the Russian Federation. Goznak, owned entirely by the federal government under the Ministry of Finance, prints Russian money, though the page describing it does not name the bank as its customer.
p:PAK: The State Bank of Pakistan is the country's central bank. It scores 29 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. One case from 2025 is alleged and unproven. In August 2025 Pakistan Observer reported, citing internal memos and cash slips, that senior officials including an executive director issued bulk fresh banknotes directly to private brokers, who resold them at premiums, with each transaction netting officials at least 2 million rupees in kickbacks. It said no probe had been opened. In January 2014 governor Yaseen Anwar resigned; the Finance Ministry spokesman said he cited personal reasons, while unnamed senior officials said it covered differences with Finance Minister Ishaq Dar over inflation and reserves. Two governors came from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund: Ishrat Husain, appointed in December 1999, and Reza Baqir, appointed in May 2019 after leading the IMF's Debt Policy Division. KPMG and BDO audit its accounts.
p:CHL: Chile's central bank is the Central Bank of Chile, which issues the Chilean peso. It scores 22 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and no government pressure was reported between 2010 and 2018. Two cases are recorded, both still under investigation. On 24 July 2012 three staff allegedly tried to take about 38 million pesos in banknotes being processed for destruction, and a fourth was detained the next day; the bank told the police economic crimes unit and began legal action. In March 2022 someone posing as the finance chief of the US firm RVK sent a false invoice for 205,000 dollars from an address one letter off the real one, and the bank paid. It complained to prosecutors in May 2022, said no official appeared to have taken part deliberately, and dismissed its accounting management head that June; he sued in December, seeking 267 million pesos. Part of the state's sovereign wealth funds is run by outside firms the bank picks and supervises, BlackRock holding the high yield and corporate bond portfolios and Nomura Asset Management part of the high yield bonds. KPMG audits the accounts.
p:ZWE: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe issues the ZiG, which circulates alongside foreign currency. From 2003 to 2013, under governor Gideon Gono, it ran quasi-fiscal activities, handing out cash and farm equipment at events presided over by President Mugabe and raiding private foreign-currency accounts to fund state operations, leaving debts of close to 1.3 billion dollars that a 2014 government bill moved onto taxpayers. In 2009 the Movement for Democratic Change demanded Gono be replaced, saying Western donors would not fund reconstruction until he went; Mugabe said he would stay, and he was not removed. At a parliamentary Public Accounts Committee hearing in September 2019, deputy governor Mlambo confirmed the bank had issued 663.8 million US dollars in Treasury Bills in 2017 and 2018 to Sakunda Holdings, owned by presidential ally Kudakwashe Tagwirei, on Finance Ministry instruction; the committee also cited a 1.37 billion dollar overdraft issued without parliamentary approval. Both matters stand as official findings. Government pressure was reported in 8 of 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018, always to ease policy. Zimbabwe scores 34 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:DEU: Germany uses the euro, and its central bank, the Deutsche Bundesbank, applies the interest rates the European Central Bank sets for the 21 countries using the currency. Bundesbank president Ernst Welteke resigned on 16 April 2004 after criticism for accepting a free New Year stay at Berlin's Hotel Adlon, paid two years earlier by the commercial bank Dresdner Bank, which the Bundesbank supervises; prosecutors and the Bundesbank both opened inquiries. Two further matters concern the European Central Bank. The European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, found maladministration and in January 2018 recommended that president Mario Draghi suspend his membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum including private bankers; the ECB declined and he did not. And on 18 May 2015 board member Cœuré told a private London event the ECB would bring forward asset purchases, in a speech published only the next morning, which the ECB called an internal procedure error. Leaders have moved into private finance: Axel Weber to the chairmanship of UBS, Jens Weidmann to chairman of Commerzbank's supervisory board in May 2023. Most of the gold is stored abroad rather than managed by others: of 3,381 tonnes at the end of 2015, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York held 1,347.4 tonnes, the Bank of England 434.7 and the Banque de France 196.4. Germany scores 22 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:LBY: The Central Bank of Libya issues the dinar, and Britain's De La Rue prints the notes. The bank has signed a cooperation agreement under the World Bank Treasury's Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership; it describes an exchange of expertise and capacity building, not handing its reserves over to be managed. The Misrata Criminal Court convicted two people over a scheme to seize 128 million US dollars and 5 million euros from the Sirte branch in 2013, with sentences of 15 and 13 years. In November 2022 the bank accused its deputy governor, Ali al-Hibri, of signing forged 50-dinar notes printed in Russia, and Governor Saddek Elkaber asked the Attorney-General to pursue a complaint; that allegation is unproven. Global Witness reported on 19 February 2021 that senior officials hold paid directorships abroad and that Elkaber chairs a London bank the central bank indirectly owns, calling this a conflict of interest while alleging no lawbreaking. On 18 August 2024 the Presidential Council decreed that the governor be replaced; a delegation from the Dbeibah government then took over his office, al-Kabir said he had fled over militia threats, and banking operations were suspended. Libya scores 50 of 100 for exposure to outside influence. Libya's central bank publishes no annual auditor's report, but Deloitte audited both of the branches it split into in 2014, covering September 2014 to June 2020. The Presidency Council commissioned that review with United Nations support, and the final reports were handed over in Tripoli on 8 July 2021.
p:CHE: Switzerland's money is the Swiss franc, issued by the Swiss National Bank, a joint-stock company listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange with 100,000 shares and 25 million francs of capital. At the end of 2025 the 26 cantons held 38.995 per cent, 24 cantonal banks 11.966 per cent, 19 municipalities 0.265 per cent and private shareholders 48.774 per cent; the largest single holders were the Canton of Berne with 6.63 per cent, the Canton of Zurich with 5.23 per cent and one private holder, Theo Siegert, with 5.01 per cent. Holders outside the public sector may vote no more than 100 shares each, and the Confederation owns none. Orell Fussli Security Printing prints the notes, KPMG has audited the accounts since 2015, and the bank part-owns the Bank for International Settlements. About 70 per cent of its gold is stored in Switzerland, some 20 per cent at the Bank of England and roughly 10 per cent at the Bank of Canada; those two store the gold and do not manage its money. It scores 30 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. One case is recorded: chairman Philipp Hildebrand resigned on 9 January 2012 after reports that dollar trades made in 2011 from a joint account with his wife, Kashya Hildebrand, earned tens of thousands of dollars while the bank was acting to weaken the franc. He said the trades broke no rules but that he could not prove he was unaware of them, and he gave the profits to charity; he joined BlackRock as vice chairman in 2012. Jean-Pierre Roth, chairman of the Governing Board from 2001 to 2009, was elected to the board of the reinsurer Swiss Re in 2010. Neither move carries an ethics finding.
p:SWE: Sveriges Riksbank is Sweden's central bank and issues the krona. It scores 13 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, less exposed than 99 per cent of the 194 places with a figure. Two linked cases run from 2020 to 2021. On 18 June 2021 the Riksbank said a routine check of staff securities dealings had found a few employees making transactions that did not fit its ethics rules, including share trades close to monetary policy decisions and trades in companies whose corporate bonds it was buying; it called this inappropriate, held talks with those involved and began revising the rules. After media reports that Stefan Ingves and Skingsley had conflicts of interest from shares they held while deciding on corporate bond purchases, the bank's General Council reviewed the matter and on 17 December 2021 concluded the link was too weak to amount to a conflict of interest, finding no shortcoming in their conduct. Ingves was appointed governor in October 2005, having headed a department at the International Monetary Fund since 1999; that move is not an accusation. Its 125.7 tonnes of gold sit partly at the Riksbank and partly abroad, 61.4 tonnes at the Bank of England, 33.2 at the Bank of Canada, 13.2 at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and 2.8 at the Swiss National Bank, which is storage of the gold and not management of its money. Crane AB printed the notes at Tumba until the Riksbank gave notice to end the contract on 19 June 2018 because Crane was moving printing to Malta; De La Rue replaced it under an agreement announced on 19 September 2018.
p:GHA: The Bank of Ghana issues the cedi, and Ghana scores 32 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. Governors keep being pushed out. In March 2016 the MP Kwasi Ameyaw-Cheremeh said the government had forced out Henry Kofi Wampah; Wampah said he had agreed with President Mahama to leave early, and no government response is reported. Abdul Nashiru Issahaku resigned with effect after 1 April 2017 citing personal reasons, under an agreement with the government that month, after the New Patriotic Party won the 2016 election and the party's Anthony Akoto Osei said he should step down; a governor's four-year term is protected by the 1992 constitution. In December 2017 the government pushed for second deputy governor Johnson Asiama to go; he said he had not resigned, and nothing further was reported. In November 2022 Isaac Adongo, for the Minority in Parliament, called governor Ernest Addison incompetent over the cedi's fall and said he should resign or be sacked, with no answer reported. The bank said in February 2023 that its claims on the government at the end of 2022 included a 37.9 billion cedi overdraft covering auction shortfalls and maturing bonds, 7.2 billion cedis of treasury bonds bought from banks and 8.9 billion cedis of International Monetary Fund money passed on, after government, bank and Fund had adopted zero deficit financing. In February 2020 the Attorney-General charged Kwabena Duffuor, a former finance minister and governor, and seven others with 68 counts over uniBank's collapse: Duffuor with dishonestly receiving 663.28 million cedis and money laundering, Asiama with approving a 300 million cedi unsecured facility from the distressed uniBank to Universal Merchant Bank. Asiama's charges were withdrawn around 30 January 2025 and the case against Duffuor and the others was ended on 22 July 2025 after more than 60 per cent of the funds allegedly lost had been recovered; none of it was proven. Duffuor had gone from governor between 1997 and 2001 to founder and president of HODA Holdings, whose largest holding was uniBank. De La Rue, a security printer in the United Kingdom, prints the notes and charges in British pounds, and KPMG audits the accounts. On the 2020 accounts, gold held with the Bank of England and the US Federal Reserve came to 2.05 billion cedis between them, with 907 million cedis with the Swiss firm UBS Gold Investment and 111.7 million in its own vault: storage of gold, not management of its money.
p:MOZ: The Bank of Mozambique is the country's central bank, and it scores 43 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. Four of its records come out of the 'hidden debts', more than two billion US dollars of loans from Credit Suisse and VTB of Russia. Letters from 2013 shown at a trial in the United States had the bank authorising the company Proindicus to seek 372 million dollars, later 622 million, and Ematum 850 million; board member Silvia de Abreu signed them after an instruction from governor Ernesto Gove, who in 2016 denied responsibility and said he had never heard of Proindicus. That strand is still under investigation, so nothing in it is proven. At the Maputo City Court on 23 November 2021 Gove testified that he had signed on grounds of sovereignty and national security and admitted irregularities, and judge Efigenio Baptista rejected his argument that the law barring such approvals did not apply; the same day the bank's administrator Silvina de Abreu testified that it should not have authorised the loans and that Gove told her to keep technical staff out. Both of those stand as official findings. In April 2023 the daily Noticias reported Gove and two other board members among four people accused in a second trial then being prepared, with no date set and no charges listed, which is unproven. President Filipe Nyusi fired deputy governor Antonio Pinto de Abreu on 26 January 2016 without giving a reason, and on 31 August 2016 replaced Gove with Rogerio Zandamela, an International Monetary Fund official, which is a career move and not an accusation. On 2 September 2026 President Daniel Chapo revoked Waldemar Fernando de Sousa's appointment as governor, citing circumstances he did not specify, and named Felisberto Dinis Navalha; the Attorney General's Office accuses De Sousa over the hidden debts, though he was not tried in the main case. Crane Currency printed its 500-metical note and BDO audited its 2019 accounts.
p:GEO: The National Bank of Georgia issues the lari. Its law scores 0.847 of 1 for independence from government, and it scores 26 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. On 17 July 2015 parliament voted 80 to 19 to move banking supervision out of the bank to a new agency, after Bidzina Ivanishvili blamed the bank and its chairman Giorgi Kadagidze for the lari's fall. In September 2023 the bank unfroze assets tied to Otar Partskhaladze, a former Prosecutor General sanctioned by the US Treasury, arguing that Georgian citizens cannot be sanctioned without a conviction in a Georgian court; acting president Natia Turnava confirmed on 20 September that she had changed the procedure single-handedly, three of the four vice presidents and an adviser resigned, and no court verdict or official finding followed. In 2026 the Prosecutor's Office began investigating Council member Nana Keinishvili over possible unlawful involvement in business, after complaints from the crypto firm Bitexchange LLC, which the bank had fined; it was still open in October 2026 and nothing is proven. The World Bank's Reserves Advisory and Management Partnership advises the bank on its reserves investment strategy and gold policy rather than managing the money. KPMG Georgia LLC audited the bank's accounts for 2020, signing at Tbilisi on 23 April 2021.
p:NPL: Nepal Rastra Bank issues Nepal's rupee and holds it at a fixed rate against India's rupee, and scores 28 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. In 2007 the Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority charged sitting governor Bhattarai and executive director Pradhan with embezzlement over the hiring of American consultants; Bhattarai was suspended, and the Supreme Court later cleared both. In October 2011 Note Printing Australia, owned by the Reserve Bank of Australia, pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court of Victoria to conspiring to provide benefits to foreign public officials to obtain banknote business with Nepal's note-issuing authority between February 2000 and May 2002, and paid 1,856,710 Australian dollars. On 8 April 2022 the government suspended governor Adhikari over charges, still unproven, of leaking sensitive government decisions; the Supreme Court stayed the suspension on 19 April and he returned to work.
p:IRN: The Central Bank of the Islamic Republic of Iran issues the rial, which is in free fall. Its law leaves most power with government, 0.448 of 1 where 1 means the bank holds it. Its notes and coins come from the Security Printing and Minting Organization, a state printing works owned by the bank since 1962; before 1982 the notes were printed abroad. The government replaced governor Valiollah Seif on 25 July 2018 without reason, and dismissed his successor Abdolnasser Hemmati on 30 May 2021 for standing for president. In October 2021 a Tehran court sentenced Seif to ten years, his deputy Araghchi to eight and the intermediary Aghakhani to thirteen over an illegal foreign-currency scheme; the Supreme Court overturned the verdicts in 2023, and the prosecution of Seif and Araghchi was dropped in March 2025. Abroad, Bahrain's High Criminal Court in November 2020 fined the bank and other Iran-owned banks one million Bahraini dinars each; prosecutors said it planned to launder billions of dollars through Future Bank.
