At the Maputo City Court on 23 November 2021, the 49th day of a trial of 19 people, former Bank of Mozambique governor Ernesto Gove testified as a witness that he signed the authorisations on grounds of sovereignty and national security, and admitted irregularities: the requests were handed personally to senior bank officials by Eugenio Matlaba and Antonio Carlos do Rosario rather than submitted at a counter, and the Credit Suisse contracts were already signed. The Foreign Exchange Law regulations bar the bank from authorising foreign loans to private companies whose repayment depends on a state guarantee; Gove said the bar applied only to guarantees obtained after loans were agreed, and judge Efigenio Baptista rejected that reading. Bank administrator Silvina de Abreu testified the same day that the loans should not have been authorised, and that Gove told her to work only with the management group and leave technical staff out.
n:Ministry of Finance of Chile: The Ministry of Finance of Chile, in Santiago, is named alongside a fraud at the Banco Central de Chile. On 11 May 2022 a consultant under contract to the central bank told it that it had not been paid for services provided in 2021. The bank had paid 205,000 US dollars, about 170 million pesos, into the account of someone posing as an international consulting services provider. It complained to prosecutors on 20 May 2022 and investigated possible administrative responsibilities internally, saying nothing indicated any official took part deliberately.
n:Nina Angelovska: Nina Angelovska was finance minister of North Macedonia. An association of Eurostandard Bank depositors said in a press release that the central bank governor had tipped off the finance minister and other large depositors so they could take their money out before the bank was put under administration, and that financial police reports were kept secret so the bank could keep operating. It said Angelovska withdrew more than 200,000 euros months before the central bank acted. No charges have been brought and no official finding made, so none of this is proven.
n:Peter Carter: Peter Carter is a Queen's Counsel, a senior barrister, who appeared at the Commission of Enquiry into the collapse of CL Financial and the Hindu Credit Union in Trinidad and Tobago. On 6 December 2012 he put it to former Central Bank governor Ewart Williams that had the Central Bank intervened in 2006, more than 10 billion Trinidad and Tobago dollars would not have been at risk. Williams had said the bank saw early warning signs at the insurer CLICO in 2006 but held off to avoid a run on it, and intervened in 2009. This was cross-examination, not a finding by the commission.
n:Rajabu Maranda: Rajabu Maranda is a businessman in Tanzania. The Kisutu Resident Magistrate's Court in Dar es Salaam found him and fellow businessman Farijala Hussein guilty of offences related to financial impropriety, forgery and obtaining credit under false pretences, sentenced each to five years in prison, and ordered them to return the money they had taken. A report published on 27 May 2011 describes these as the first court cases heard after the 2008 corruption scandal at the Bank of Tanzania.
n:Srettha Thavisin: Srettha Thavisin was prime minister of Thailand, in Bangkok. Pheu Thai Party leader Paetongtarn Shinawatra criticised the Bank of Thailand's independence, saying the law that keeps the bank separate from the government obstructs solving economic problems. The remarks drew a backlash, and Srettha said he had no plans to remove Governor Sethaput Suthiwartnarueput or to amend the Bank of Thailand Act. A 2008 amendment to that Act makes removing the governor over policy disagreements very difficult.
n:Supreme Court of Thailand, Criminal Di: This division of Thailand's Supreme Court, in Bangkok, tries people who have held political office. It convicted former finance minister Surapong Suebwonglee of malfeasance under Section 157 of the Criminal Code for appointing Sathit Limpongpan, Vijit Supinij and Chaiwat Wibulsawasdi in 2008 to the committee that selects members of the Bank of Thailand's board; all three were representatives of financial institutions under Bank of Thailand supervision. He was given one year in jail, suspended for one year, and a fine of 20,000 baht. The National Anti-Corruption Commission had filed the case on 27 May 2015.
n:Tribunal de Sentencia de Asuncion: The Tribunal de Sentencia de Asuncion is a sentencing court in Paraguay's capital. On 6 June 2006, presided over by Sandra Farias with Gustavo Amarilla and Miguel Said, it sentenced former president Luis Gonzalez Macchi to six years in prison for breach of trust, as the alleged instigator of the diversion of 16 million US dollars to the United States from two private banks, Union and Orienta, which the Banco Central had intervened in and declared bankrupt. Jose Pecci, the bank's former superintendent, got eight years. Gonzalez Macchi said he would appeal; the prosecutor had sought ten years.
n:World Bank Group: The World Bank Group, based in Washington, D.C., lends to governments for development. Adriana D. Kugler was the United States Executive Director there before becoming a governor of the Federal Reserve System, the United States central bank, a post she held from 13 September 2023 to 8 August 2025.
n:Abd Rabbuh Mansur Hadi: Abd Rabbuh Mansur Hadi was Yemen's president, based in Aden. He dismissed the governor of the Central Bank of Yemen and his deputy, according to the state news agency Saba, and Ahmed bin Ahmed Ghaleb Al-Maabq was named governor with Muhammad Omar Banaja as deputy. No reason was given for the removals, which were the fourth such sacking since the country's civil war began.
n:Assembleia da República committee of i: This was a committee of inquiry set up by Portugal's parliament, the Assembleia da República in Lisbon, to examine the bank Novo Banco. On Tuesday 27 July 2021 it approved its final report, with the PS voting against and the CDS-PP abstaining. The report concluded that the winding up of Banco Espírito Santo and the 4,900 million euros put into Novo Banco at the start were a political fraud, and it criticised the Bank of Portugal and the European Commission.
n:Bank of Maldives: The Bank of Maldives is a bank in Malé. It is named in the case of money embezzled from the Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation. An Anti-Corruption Commission report made public in February 2019 found the country's central bank, the Maldives Monetary Authority, negligent over the theft of 1.3 billion rufiyaa from that company: its Financial Intelligence Unit was told in 2014 of a 59 million US dollar cheque to a firm called SOF, and did not examine SOF's large transactions passing through the Bank of Maldives and the Bank of Ceylon.
n:Cambio Nelson: Cambio Nelson is a company in Uruguay. Investigating fraud at the firm, prosecutor Rodrigo Morosoli asked for the formal indictment of Humberto Capote, a former president of the Central Bank of Uruguay, for joint responsibility in a continued crime of misappropriation. Judge Marcelo Souto freed Capote at first instance, finding the evidence insufficient to prosecute him, and the prosecutor appealed in April 2017.
n:Cour des comptes (DRC): The Cour des comptes is a state audit court in Kinshasa, DR Congo, and it has been examining Deogratias Mutombo, a former governor of the Central Bank of the Congo. On 25 October 2023 it was reported that his accounts, and those of Albert Yuma, former board chairman of the mining company Gecamines, had been frozen, and that both men must stay available to the court. The sum at issue is an alleged embezzlement of 25.521 million US dollars, which is unproven.
n:Ematum: Ematum was a Mozambican company whose foreign borrowing, with that of Proindicus and MAM, made up the country's hidden debts: more than two billion US dollars from Credit Suisse and VTB of Russia. At the Maputo City Court on 23 November 2021, former Bank of Mozambique governor Ernesto Gove said he had signed the authorisations on grounds of sovereignty and national security, and admitted irregularities in how the central bank granted them. Bank administrator Silvina de Abreu testified the same day that it should not have approved the loans, which included 850 million dollars for Ematum in August 2013.
n:First Labour Court of Santiago: The First Labour Court of Santiago in Chile hears employment disputes. In March 2022 someone posing as the chief financial officer of the US firm RVK emailed the Central Bank of Chile a false invoice for 205,000 US dollars, from an address one letter different from the real one, and asked for payment to a new account; the bank paid. It complained to prosecutors in May 2022 and dismissed the head of its accounting management department on 23 June 2022 over the payment. In December he sued in this court, calling the dismissal abusive and seeking 267 million Chilean pesos.
n:Jaan Naaber: Jaan Naaber was a prosecutor in Estonia. A Tallinn court had acquitted Siim Kallas, a former president of the Bank of Estonia, of charges tied to a failed investment deal made during his time at the central bank. On 15 March 1999 Naaber appealed against that acquittal, asking a district court to convict Kallas and an unnamed co-defendant over their role in the deal.
n:Luis Gonzalez Macchi: Luis Gonzalez Macchi was a president of Paraguay. On 6 June 2006 a sentencing court in Asuncion presided over by Sandra Farias gave him six years in prison for breach of trust as the alleged instigator of the diversion of 16 million US dollars to the United States from two private banks, Union and Orienta, which the Central Bank of Paraguay had taken over and declared bankrupt. Jose Pecci, a former superintendent at the central bank, was sentenced to eight years. Gonzalez Macchi said he would appeal; the prosecutor, Victoria Acuna, had asked for ten years.
n:Maputo City Court: The Maputo City Court in Mozambique heard the hidden debts trial of 19 people, over loans of more than two billion US dollars from Credit Suisse and VTB of Russia to Proindicus, Ematum and MAM. Giving evidence on 23 November 2021, former Bank of Mozambique governor Ernesto Gove said he had signed the authorisations on grounds of sovereignty and national security, and admitted irregularities: the requests were handed to senior bank officials in person rather than filed at a counter, and the Credit Suisse contracts were already signed. Judge Efigenio Baptista rejected his reading of the rule barring such loans.
n:Mswati III: Mswati III is the king of Eswatini. In 2017 an evaluations team at the Central Bank of Eswatini recommended refusing a commercial banking licence to Farmers Bank. A conditional licence was issued in September 2018 after a royal command from the king. It was revoked in October 2020 because Farmers Bank could not prove where its seed capital came from, and an appeal chaired by commerce minister Manqoba Khumalo reinstated it in January 2021. A 2022 report by Kroll said outside parties had probably told the bank to proceed, and that 89 million rand of the seed capital had gone from 2019 into silver bullion the bank could not verify existed.
n:Note Printing Works, Bank of Thailand: The Note Printing Works at Nakhon Pathom is the Bank of Thailand's own banknote plant. The bank's history of the works records that the Cabinet authorised the bank to establish it in 1961, and describes the new works as built for the production of Thai banknotes.
n:Petro Poroshenko: Petro Poroshenko was president of Ukraine, in Kyiv. Valeria Gontareva stepped down as governor of the National Bank of Ukraine on 10 May 2017, but by January 2018 parliament had still not voted on her resignation or on a replacement. She had been on unpaid leave since 26 September, saying she would stay away until parliament acted. On 18 January 2018 Poroshenko nominated the acting head, Yakiv Smolii, for the post.
n:RenaissanceRe Holdings: RenaissanceRe Holdings is a reinsurance company based in Pembroke, Bermuda. In November 2024 Loretta Mester joined its board of directors. She had been president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland from 2014 until she retired in 2024, and over those same years sat on the Federal Open Market Committee, the group that sets interest rates in the United States.
n:State Great Khural of Mongolia: The State Great Khural is Mongolia's parliament, in Ulaanbaatar. On 21 November 2019 lawmakers accepted the resignation of the governor of the Bank of Mongolia, Nadmid Bayartsaikhan. He stepped down after the Financial Action Task Force, the international body that sets standards against money laundering, added Mongolia to its grey list over its enforcement. The next day parliament appointed Byadran Lkhagvasuren in his place.
n:Surapong Suebwonglee: Surapong Suebwonglee was Thailand's finance minister. In 2008 he appointed Sathit Limpongpan, Vijit Supinij and Chaiwat Wibulsawasdi to the committee that selects members of the Bank of Thailand's board; all three were representatives of financial institutions that the Bank of Thailand supervises. The National Anti-Corruption Commission filed the case on 27 May 2015, and the Supreme Court's Criminal Division for Holders of Political Positions convicted him of malfeasance in office. He was given one year in jail, suspended for one year, and fined 20,000 baht.
n:Trifun Kostovski: Trifun Kostovski is named in North Macedonia in connection with the failure of Eurostandard Bank. An association of the bank's depositors said the governor of the central bank tipped off the finance minister and other large depositors so they could take their money out before the bank was placed under administration, and that financial police reports were kept secret so it could keep operating. The association said Finance Minister Nina Angelovska withdrew more than 200,000 euros months before the central bank acted, and that over 60 million euros were lost. No charges and no official finding are recorded.
n:Zephyr Management LP: Zephyr Management LP is a private equity firm in New York. Dennis P. Lockhart worked there from 2001 to 2003, after Citibank from 1971 to 1988 and Heller Financial from 1988 to 2001, and then served as president and chief executive of the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta from 1 March 2007 to 28 February 2017.
n:Anthony Akoto Osei: Anthony Akoto Osei is a politician in Accra and a figure in Ghana's New Patriotic Party. After the party won the 2016 election, the position of Bank of Ghana governor Abdul Nashiru Issahaku came under scrutiny, and Osei held that he should voluntarily step down. Issahaku resigned with effect after 1 April 2017, telling Joy Business he was leaving for personal reasons, following an agreement reached with the government earlier that month. A governor's four-year term is protected by Article 183(4)(d) of Ghana's 1992 constitution.
n:BSP Security Plant Complex: The BSP Security Plant Complex is a plant in Quezon City run by Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, the central bank of the Philippines. It is where the country's banknotes are made: a speech by the bank's governor, Benjamin Diokno, published by the Bank for International Settlements, describes the complex as the facility that has housed the Bangko Sentral's currency production since 1978.
n:Belarusian Interbank Settlement Center: The Belarusian Interbank Settlement Center is a company in Minsk, named in a bribery case around the National Bank of the Republic of Belarus. At a trial reported in March 2020, prosecutors charged Feliks Kasperovich, with Andrei Podgorny of the National Bank's information technology directorate, with taking bribes of at least 868,750 US dollars from 2007 onwards. Igor Kudasov, head of the bank's payment systems directorate, was charged over a 30,000 dollar bribe and had been held since 29 December 2018. Kasperovich admitted the charges; the rest are unproven.
n:Cayman Islands Football Association: The Cayman Islands Football Association is the islands' football body. In June 2015 the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority, which acts as the central bank there, said it would review the involvement of local people and financial institutions in the FIFA corruption case, after Caymanian businessman Jeffrey Webb was arrested in Switzerland on 27 May. Managing director Cindy Scotland's husband, former minister Mark Scotland, had worked for the association under Webb and was with him at the arrest. Chairman George McCarthy said Scotland would remain and that no Cayman bank was shown to have done wrong.
n:Criminal Court of the Maldives: The Criminal Court of the Maldives sits in Male. In February 2020 prosecutors charged Ibrahim Athif Shakoor, former head of the Financial Intelligence Unit at the Maldives Monetary Authority, with negligence over the MMPRC case, in which state funds were moved to private accounts. He denied the allegations, saying he had told the then governor, Azeema Adam, about the illegal transactions. At a hearing in September 2020 he sought a deal waiving prison in exchange for admitting a breach of the money laundering law. The charges were later withdrawn.
n:Ernst & Young Audit Services LLC: Ernst & Young Audit Services LLC is an audit firm based in Kyiv. An audit is an outside check of whether an organisation's accounts are accurate. This firm does that work for the National Bank of Ukraine, the country's central bank, and signed the bank's consolidated financial statements for the financial year ending 31 December 2024.
n:Gecamines: Gecamines is a company in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It appears in a case around the Central Bank of the Congo, the country's central bank. On 25 October 2023 Financial Afrik reported that the accounts of former central bank governor Deogratias Mutombo, and those of former Gecamines board chairman Albert Yuma, had been frozen, and that both men must remain available to the Cour des comptes, the state audit court. The sum at issue is alleged embezzlement of 25.521 million US dollars. It is not proven.
n:Jeffrey Webb: Jeffrey Webb is a Caymanian businessman, arrested in Switzerland on 27 May 2015 in the FIFA corruption case. In June 2015 the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority, which acts as the central bank there, said it would review the involvement of local people and financial institutions in that case. Managing director Cindy Scotland's husband, former minister Mark Scotland, had worked for the Cayman Islands Football Association under Webb and was with him at the arrest. Chairman George McCarthy said Scotland would stay as managing director and that no Cayman bank was shown to have done wrong.
n:MAM: MAM is a Mozambican company, one of three state-linked borrowers in the hidden debts case, with Proindicus and Ematum; their loans from Credit Suisse and VTB of Russia came to more than two billion US dollars. At the Maputo City Court on 23 November 2021 former Bank of Mozambique governor Ernesto Gove testified that he signed the authorisations on grounds of sovereignty and national security. Rules bar the bank from authorising such loans when repayment depends on a state guarantee, and judge Efigenio Baptista rejected Gove's argument to the contrary. The bank's own administrator told the court it should not have authorised them.
n:Martin Dlamini: Martin Dlamini was finance minister of Eswatini. The Central Bank of Eswatini rejected Farmers Bank's application for a commercial banking licence in late 2017, and in May 2018 Dlamini told the bank that the king had ordered an investigation into its reluctance to license it. The licence was granted after a royal command in September 2018. The central bank revoked it on 5 October 2020 over the unexplained source of the seed capital, then reinstated it in January 2021, objecting to procedural improprieties, after commerce minister Manqoba Khumalo ruled that Farmers Bank should keep it.
n:National Anti-Corruption Commission (T: The National Anti-Corruption Commission is a state agency in Bangkok that investigates officials. On 27 May 2015 it filed the case in which the Supreme Court's Criminal Division for Holders of Political Positions convicted former finance minister Surapong Suebwonglee of malfeasance. In 2008 he had appointed Sathit Limpongpan, Vijit Supinij and Chaiwat Wibulsawasdi to the committee that selects Bank of Thailand board members, and all three represented financial institutions the bank supervises. He was given one year in jail, suspended for one year, and a 20,000 baht fine.
n:Novo Banco: Novo Banco is a bank in Lisbon, created out of the collapsed Banco Espirito Santo. On Tuesday 27 July 2021 a Portuguese parliamentary committee of inquiry approved its final report on it, with the Socialist Party voting against and the CDS-PP abstaining. The report concludes that the resolution of Banco Espirito Santo and the initial capitalisation of Novo Banco, of 4,900 million euros, were a political fraud, and it criticises the Bank of Portugal, the country's central bank, and the European Commission.
n:Polska Wytwórnia Papierów Wartościowyc: Polska Wytwornia Papierow Wartosciowych S.A. is a security printing firm in Warsaw. It makes Poland's banknotes: the National Bank of Poland, Narodowy Bank Polski, states in its own publication on banknote security features that Polish notes are produced by this firm, which the bank commissions to do the work.
n:Rodrigo Morosoli: Rodrigo Morosoli is a prosecutor in Uruguay. Investigating the Cambio Nelson fraud, he sought the formal indictment of Humberto Capote, a former president of the Central Bank of Uruguay, for co-authorship of a continued crime of misappropriation, which means taking money held in trust. Judge Marcelo Souto freed Capote at first instance, finding the evidence insufficient to prosecute him, and Morosoli appealed that decision in April 2017. Nothing against Capote was established.
n:State Prosecutor General of the Republ: The State Prosecutor General of the Republic of Slovenia heads the country's prosecution service in Ljubljana, and the post was then held by Mr Fiser. Slovenian authorities searched the premises of Banka Slovenije, the central bank, on 6 July 2016 in a pre-criminal investigation procedure, a step in the long-running inquiry into Slovenia's 2013 bank bailout. The central bank then published letters from the President of the European Central Bank to Fiser, and to European Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker, about European Central Bank information seized during the search.
n:Szymon Holownia: Szymon Holownia is a politician in Poland. The ruling coalition accused National Bank of Poland governor Adam Glapinski of breaking several laws and of failing to keep the bank politically independent under the former Law and Justice government, and in March 2024 it moved in the Sejm, the lower house, to bring him before the State Tribunal. On 20 August 2024 the Constitutional Tribunal ruled that legislation unconstitutional; in January 2024 it had also required a three-fifths majority, and the coalition held 241 of 460 seats against a threshold of 276.
n:Valeriu Strelet: Valeriu Strelet was prime minister of Moldova, based in Chisinau. Dorin Dragutanu announced his resignation as governor of the National Bank of Moldova after criticism that he had failed to prevent about one billion US dollars disappearing from three Moldovan banks in 2014. He said he was resigning because of pressure from some politicians, and denied responsibility, saying he had repeatedly warned the authorities. President Nicolae Timofti and Strelet had both said he should be removed.
n:Zhogorku Kenesh: The Zhogorku Kenesh is the parliament of Kyrgyzstan, in Bishkek. Melis Turgunbaev, chairman of the National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic since 26 June 2024, submitted a letter of resignation, and Speaker Marlen Mamataliev announced it in a session of the parliament. It was described as a voluntary resignation.
n:Anti-Corruption Commission of the Mald: The Anti-Corruption Commission of the Maldives is the country's anti-corruption body, in Male. A report it published in February 2019 found the Maldives Monetary Authority negligent over the embezzlement of 1.3 billion rufiyaa from the Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation: the bank's Financial Intelligence Unit, which is meant to spot suspicious money, was told in 2014 of a 59 million US dollar cheque to a firm called SOF but did not investigate it properly or pass the case on. In March 2019 police confirmed that governor Ahmed Naseer was under investigation for obstruction of justice, which is unproven.
n:Banco Orienta: Banco Orienta was a private bank in Paraguay that the Central Bank of Paraguay took over and declared bankrupt. On 6 June 2006 a court in Asuncion sentenced former president Luis Gonzalez Macchi to six years in prison for breach of trust, as alleged instigator of the diversion of 16 million US dollars to the United States from Orienta and another private bank, Union. Jose Pecci, a former superintendent at the central bank, was sentenced to eight years. Gonzalez Macchi said he would appeal; the prosecutor had asked for ten years.
n:Berkshire Hills Bancorp: Berkshire Hills Bancorp is a banking company in Boston. Eric S. Rosengren, president and chief executive of the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston from 2007 until he retired in 2021, joined the boards of Berkshire Hills Bancorp and Berkshire Bank with effect from 5 April 2023. The company announced the appointment in April 2023.
n:Centro para Democracia e Desenvolvimen: The Centro para Democracia e Desenvolvimento, in Maputo, followed Mozambique's hidden-debts trial day by day. On the 49th day, 23 November 2021, Bank of Mozambique administrator Silvina de Abreu testified that the central bank should not have authorised the loans to ProIndicus, EMATUM and MAM, because the Foreign Exchange Law bars approving loans whose payout depends on a state guarantee. She said governor Ernesto Gove told her to work only with the management group and keep technical staff out, as the file concerned state security. ProIndicus was approved 372 million US dollars in March 2013 and EMATUM 850 million that August.
n:D. E. Shaw group: The D. E. Shaw group is a hedge fund manager in New York. Brian Sack, who ran the New York Federal Reserve's Markets Group from mid-2009 to 2012 and had earlier spent six years at the Federal Reserve Board of Governors, joined the firm's macro investing unit as senior vice president and co-director of global economics. Angel Ubide, a former staff economist at the International Monetary Fund, took the same title. The firm announced both hires.
n:Eurostandard Bank: Eurostandard Bank was a commercial bank in North Macedonia that was put under administration, meaning the central bank took over running it. An association of its depositors said in a press release that the governor tipped off the finance minister and other large depositors so they could take their money out first, and that financial police reports were kept secret so the bank could keep operating. It said Finance Minister Nina Angelovska withdrew more than 200,000 euros months beforehand and that over 60 million euros were lost. No charges and no official finding are reported.
n:Government of Bolivia: This is the national government in La Paz. The Central Bank of Bolivia dismissed more than a dozen of its senior managers, among them the manager for international operations, the principal adviser on political economy and subdirectors of several departments. A former governor of the bank said the dismissals were likely influenced by the change of government. The governor himself was not removed.
n:KPMG Auditores Independentes: KPMG Auditores Independentes is an accounting firm in Sao Paulo. It audited the accounts of the Central Bank of Brazil for the financial year that ended on 31 December 2018. An audit is an outside check that the figures an institution publishes are accurate.
n:Maldives Police Service: The Maldives Police Service is the national police force, based in Male. In March 2019 it summoned Ahmed Naseer, governor of the Maldives Monetary Authority, and confirmed he was being investigated for obstruction of justice. Parliament's Financial Committee had questioned him on 5 March about the Anti-Corruption Commission's report on the embezzlement case at the Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation, and about the removal of Abdulla Ashraf as head of the Financial Intelligence Unit. The investigation is unproven.
n:Members of the Jordanian Parliament: These are elected members of Jordan's parliament in Amman. In September 2003 some of them signed a petition urging Prime Minister Ali Abulragheb to remove Umayya Touqan, governor of the Central Bank of Jordan, after Touqan froze all the bank accounts belonging to six leaders of Hamas. The petition was a demand to the prime minister, not a legal step against the governor.
n:National Assembly of Serbia: The National Assembly of Serbia is the country's parliament, in Belgrade. It passed a law giving members of parliament the power to nominate and appoint the top officials of the National Bank of Serbia. Governor Mladjan Dinkic said the law undermined the bank's independence and resigned, as did two of its three deputy governors. Energy Minister Kori Udovicki was nominated to replace him.
n:Office of the Auditor General of Thail: The Office of the Auditor General of Thailand, also called the State Audit Office, is the government body in Bangkok that checks public accounts. It audits the Bank of Thailand and signed the auditor's report on its financial statements for the year that ended on 31 December 2025. An audit is a check that published figures are accurate.
n:Proindicus: Proindicus is a Mozambican company at the centre of the hidden-debts case, in which state-backed loans of more than two billion US dollars were taken from Credit Suisse and VTB of Russia. At the Maputo City Court on 23 November 2021, in the trial of 19 people, former Bank of Mozambique governor Ernesto Gove said he signed the authorisations for the loans to Proindicus, Ematum and MAM on grounds of sovereignty and national security, and admitted irregularities: the requests were handed personally to senior officials rather than submitted at a counter, and the Credit Suisse contracts were already signed. The law bars the bank from authorising such loans when repayment depends on a state guarantee; Gove said that applied only to guarantees obtained afterwards, and judge Efigenio Baptista rejected his reading.
n:SOF Pvt Ltd: SOF Pvt Ltd is a company in the Maldives. An Anti-Corruption Commission report published in February 2019 found the Maldives Monetary Authority negligent in the case in which 1.3 billion rufiyaa was embezzled from the Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation. The bank's Financial Intelligence Unit was told in 2014 of a 59 million US dollar cheque from that corporation to SOF but did not investigate it properly, did not examine SOF's large transactions through Bank of Maldives and Bank of Ceylon, and did not forward suspected money-laundering cases.
n:State Tribunal of Poland: The State Tribunal is the court in Warsaw that tries senior Polish officials for breaking the law in office. In October 2026 the Sejm's Committee on Constitutional Responsibility backed a report supporting the referral of National Bank of Poland president Adam Glapinski to it, and the Sejm Marshal said the full chamber would vote in the second half of November 2026. The motion, begun in May 2024, accuses Glapinski of indirectly financing the budget deficit through asset purchases in 2020 and 2021 and of acting without proper authorisation for those purchases and for currency interventions. He and the bank called the allegations baseless, and nothing is proven.
n:TBC Bank: TBC Bank is a commercial bank in Tbilisi. It and Bank of Georgia had frozen the accounts of Otar Partskhaladze. At a briefing on 20 September 2023, the acting president of the National Bank of Georgia, Natia Turnava, confirmed she had single-handedly changed the procedure for carrying out sanctions regimes, deciding on 19 September with effect from the next day. She said it was within her discretion, that she had told National Bank Council members beforehand, and that the two banks broke no law because the change took effect the day of her briefing. Vice-president Papuna Lezhava resigned.
n:Virabongsa Ramangkura: Virabongsa Ramangkura was chairman of the Bank of Thailand, in Bangkok. During a dispute between the bank and Finance Minister Kittiratt Na-Ranong, he pointed to the cabinet's power under Section 28/19 of the Bank of Thailand Act to remove the governor, who was then Prasarn Trairatvorakul. He stopped short of directly calling for the governor to be removed.
n:i(x) investments: i(x) investments is an investment company in New York. Sarah Bloom Raskin, who had been a governor of the Federal Reserve Board and then Deputy Secretary of the Treasury, was named to its board of directors in an announcement dated 10 August 2017.
n:Antonio Carlos do Rosario: Antonio Carlos do Rosario is named in a documented case in Mozambique involving the Bank of Mozambique, the country's central bank. On 23 November 2021, the 49th day of the hidden-debts trial, bank administrator Silvina de Abreu testified that the central bank should not have authorised the ProIndicus, EMATUM and MAM loans, because the Foreign Exchange Law bars approving loans whose disbursement depends on a state guarantee. She said then governor Ernesto Gove told her to work only with the management group and keep technical staff out.
n:Banco Union: Banco Union was a private bank in Paraguay that the Central Bank of Paraguay took over and declared bankrupt. On 6 June 2006 a sentencing court in Asuncion sentenced former president Luis Gonzalez Macchi to six years in prison for breach of trust, as alleged instigator of the diversion of 16 million US dollars to the United States from Union and the other failed bank, Orienta. Jose Pecci, former superintendent of the central bank, was sentenced to eight years. Gonzalez Macchi said he would appeal.
n:CL Financial: CL Financial was a company in Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago, whose collapse was examined by a commission of enquiry set up in November 2010 under sole commissioner Sir Anthony Colman. It found the Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago's powers over the insurance industry fundamentally deficient, tracing that to the narrow scope of the Insurance Act, and said Clico and CL Financial management largely ignored the limited tools the Inspector of financial institutions did have. It blamed no named central bank official.
n:Commission of Enquiry into CL Financia: This inquiry in Trinidad and Tobago examined the collapse of CL Financial and the Hindu Credit Union. Sole commissioner Sir Anthony Colman sat from March 2011 to May 2013, at a cost of 36.2 million dollars. He found the Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago's powers over insurance fundamentally deficient, and blamed no named official. On 6 December 2012 Queen's Counsel Peter Carter put it to former governor Ewart Williams that intervening in 2006 would have spared over 10 billion Trinidad and Tobago dollars; that was cross-examination, not a finding.
n:DRT Bağımsız Denetim ve Serbest Muhase: This is an accounting firm in Istanbul, Turkiye, and a member of Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Limited. It is the outside auditor of the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkiye, which means it checks the central bank's accounts and reports on them independently of the bank's own staff. It audited those accounts for the 2024 financial year, as recorded in the central bank's annual report for that year.
n:Farijala Hussein: Farijala Hussein is a businessman in Tanzania who took money from the Bank of Tanzania, the country's central bank. The Kisutu Resident Magistrate's Court in Dar es Salaam found him and fellow businessman Rajabu Maranda guilty of offences related to financial impropriety, forgery and obtaining credit under false pretences, sentenced each to five years in prison, and ordered them to return the money they had taken. A report published on 27 May 2011 described these as the first court cases heard after the 2008 Bank of Tanzania corruption scandal.
n:Heller Financial: Heller Financial was a company in Chicago, United States, and one stop in the career of a Federal Reserve official. Dennis P. Lockhart worked at Citibank from 1971 to 1988, at Heller Financial from 1988 to 2001 as president of Heller International Group, and then at the private equity firm Zephyr Management from 2001 to 2003. He went on to serve as President and Chief Executive of the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta from 1 March 2007 to 28 February 2017. The move itself carries no accusation.
KPMG Cardenas Dosal is an accounting firm in Mexico City, Mexico. It serves as the outside auditor of the Bank of Mexico, the country's central bank, which means it checks the bank's accounts and reports on them independently of the bank's own staff. It audited those accounts for the financial year running from 1 January to 31 December 2024.
n:Manqoba Khumalo: Manqoba Khumalo is Eswatini's commerce minister, and he helped overturn a decision of the Central Bank of Eswatini. The bank refused Farmers Bank a commercial banking licence in 2017, then issued one in September 2018 after a royal command from King Mswati III, and revoked it on 5 October 2020 because the source of the bank's seed capital was unexplained. Khumalo ruled in December 2020 that it should keep the licence, and an appeal he chaired reinstated it in January 2021.
n:Ministerio Publico: The Ministerio Publico is the public prosecution service in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. Its anti-corruption unit brought four former Central Bank of the Dominican Republic officials to court, among them former governor Jose Lois Malkun, on unproven charges including breach of trust and criminal association over the disappearance of 18 promissory notes worth 10,663 million Dominican pesos, said to have been handed fraudulently to former banker Manuel Arturo Pellerano. The central bank neither complained nor joined the case, and said it was negotiating the notes' return with Pellerano.
n:New Patriotic Party: The New Patriotic Party is a political party based in Accra, Ghana, that won the 2016 election. Bank of Ghana governor Abdul Nashiru Issahaku came under scrutiny after that win, and party figure Anthony Akoto Osei held that he should step down voluntarily. Issahaku resigned, effective after 1 April 2017, telling Joy Business he was leaving for personal reasons, and the decision followed an agreement reached with the government earlier that month. A governor's four-year term is protected by Article 183(4)(d) of Ghana's 1992 constitution.
n:Office of the President of The Gambia: This is the Gambian presidency, in Banjul, and it held accounts at the Central Bank of The Gambia. Appearing before the Janneh Commission on 19 September 2017, former central bank governor Amadou Colley said accounts controlled by the Office of the President were opened at the bank. He said the sand mining account was opened at the request of the presidential office, which he called irregular, and that withdrawals from it followed instructions from an individual in that office without the approval of the account's signatory.
n:Prudential Financial: Prudential Financial is an insurance company based in Newark, New Jersey, United States, and it hired a Federal Reserve official after her time in office. Sandra Pianalto was President and Chief Executive of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland from February 2003 until May 2014. Prudential elected her to its board of directors as an independent director, effective 1 July 2015. That is a career move, and no wrongdoing is alleged in it.
n:Sejm of the Republic of Poland: The Sejm is the lower house of Poland's parliament, in Warsaw, and it was asked to put the country's central bank chief on trial. The ruling coalition accused National Bank of Poland governor Glapinski of breaking several laws and of failing to uphold the bank's political independence, and in March 2024 moved to bring him before the State Tribunal. On 20 August 2024 the Constitutional Tribunal ruled that law unconstitutional. It had already held, on 12 January 2024, that 276 of the 460 seats were needed; the coalition had 241.
n:Storting Standing Committee on Finance: This is the finance committee of Norway's parliament, in Oslo, and its conflict-of-interest concerns changed the terms on which Nicolai Tangen was hired to run NBIM, Norges Bank's fund arm. In August 2020 the bank's Executive Board had him give up his holding in AKO Capital, transfer it and its dividend rights to the charitable AKO Foundation in perpetuity, and hold his personal fund assets as bank deposits. Supervisory Board chair Julie Brodtkorb said guidelines, regulations and laws had been breached in the appointment. Tangen took office on 1 September.
n:Tioulong Saumura: Tioulong Saumura is a former deputy governor of the National Bank of Cambodia. The Cambodia Daily reported on 28 November 2013 that Chea Serey, daughter of governor Chea Chanto, had been promoted from deputy director-general for banking supervision to director-general, replacing Nguon Sokha. Saumura said that being the governor's daughter should have excluded her, calling it nepotism and a conflict of interest. Nguon Sokha said Serey was a skilled technocrat fit to run the central bank. The claim was not confirmed, and no investigation or finding followed.
n:Wael Bualai: Wael Bualai is Bahrain's attorney general, and he announced the outcome of a money-laundering prosecution against the Central Bank of the Islamic Republic of Iran. Bahrain's Supreme Court of Appeal upheld convictions of that bank, other Iranian banks, Future Bank and six of its officials. Each convicted party was fined one million Bahraini dinars; five Future Bank officials got ten-year prison terms and a sixth five years. Confiscation of remittances put at 184 million US dollars, 967 million euros, 53 million dirhams and 235 billion Iranian riyals was also upheld.
n:Marfin Investment Group: Marfin Investment Group is a company based in Athens, Greece. Cypriot prosecutors charged Christodoulos Christodoulou, a former governor of the Central Bank of Cyprus, with agreeing to take 1 million euros from the group and from Andreas Vgenopoulos between February and November 2006, so that he would overlook Vgenopoulos taking control of Laiki Bank. The charges are unproven; Christodoulou said the money was an advance for ten years of consultancy work.
n:Andreas Vgenopoulos: Andreas Vgenopoulos is a businessman in Greece. Christodoulos Christodoulou, a former governor of the Central Bank of Cyprus, faced 29 charges over a 1 million euro payment said to have been made so that he would overlook Vgenopoulos buying a controlling stake in Laiki Bank, which failed in 2013. The first charge alleges he agreed to take that money from Vgenopoulos and Marfin Investment Group in 2006. It is unproven, and Christodoulou said the money was a consultancy advance.
n:Laiki Bank: Laiki Bank was a bank in Nicosia, Cyprus, and it failed in 2013. Christodoulos Christodoulou, a former governor of the Central Bank of Cyprus, faced 29 charges over a 1 million euro payment said to have been made so he would overlook Andreas Vgenopoulos taking a controlling stake in it, and over failing to look into whether Marfin Investment Group could control Laiki after buying shares on 6 February 2006 without central bank approval. The charges are unproven.
n:Nicosia criminal court: The Nicosia criminal court is a court in Nicosia, Cyprus. A case against Christodoulos Christodoulou, a former governor of the Central Bank of Cyprus, and co-defendants was expected to come before it at the end of September 2016. They faced 29 charges over a 1 million euro payment alleged to have been made so he would overlook Andreas Vgenopoulos taking control of Laiki Bank. The charges are unproven; Christodoulou said the money was a consultancy advance.
n:MediaWorks New Zealand: MediaWorks New Zealand is a broadcaster based in Auckland. Deloitte, brought in by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand on 11 March 2016, reported on 12 April 2016 that a Mediaworks employee was the source of a leak of the 10 March 2016 decision on the Official Cash Rate, the interest rate the bank sets. A journalist emailed a draft story out of the media lock-up without approval, and another employee emailed Michael Reddell at 8.04am, before the 9am announcement. Mediaworks reported itself on 5 April 2016.
n:Michael Reddell: Michael Reddell is a person in New Zealand who received leaked information from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. Deloitte found that the 10 March 2016 decision on the Official Cash Rate, the interest rate the bank sets, leaked from a media lock-up: a Mediaworks employee who overheard colleagues discussing the rate cut emailed Reddell at 8.04am, before the 9am announcement, and Reddell did not tell the bank until 9.08am.
n:Rana Investment Company: An investment firm based in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Fahad Al-Mubarak was its general manager from 1992 to 1999, before he became governor of the Saudi Central Bank, a post he held from 2011 to 2016 and again from January 2021.
n:Siam Commercial Bank: A commercial bank based in Bangkok, Thailand. Sethaput Suthiwartnarueput was executive vice president and chief economist of the Siam Commercial Bank Group before he became governor of the Bank of Thailand on 1 October 2020.
n:SCB Asset Management: A firm in Bangkok, Thailand that invests money for clients, part of the Siam Commercial Bank group. Sethaput Suthiwartnarueput was its president from 2008 to 2009, nine years before he became governor of the Bank of Thailand on 1 October 2020.
n:SCB Securities: A securities firm in Bangkok, Thailand, part of the Siam Commercial Bank group, which buys and sells shares and publishes research on them. Sethaput Suthiwartnarueput was its managing director and head of research, with no years given, before he became governor of the Bank of Thailand on 1 October 2020.
n:TMB Bank: A commercial bank based in Bangkok, Thailand. Sethaput Suthiwartnarueput was one of its directors from 2011 to 2012, and became governor of the Bank of Thailand on 1 October 2020.
n:Philippine Commercial Industrial Bank: A commercial bank based in Manila, Philippines. Rafael Buenaventura was its chief executive, the last post of his private banking career, before he was appointed governor of Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas in 1999. He served until 2005.
n:James Capel & Company: A securities firm based in London, United Kingdom. Zsigmond Jarai was its director for East Europe from 1990 to 1993, at the start of a career that ran through private banks in London and Budapest and later led the Magyar Nemzeti Bank.
n:Samuel Montagu & Co: A merchant bank based in London, United Kingdom, meaning a bank that arranges finance for companies rather than taking deposits from the public. Zsigmond Jarai was its managing director from 1993 to 1995, before he returned to Hungarian banking and later led the Magyar Nemzeti Bank.
n:Hungarian Credit Bank: A bank based in Budapest, Hungary, known there as MHB. Zsigmond Jarai was its chief executive from 1995 to 1997, before he moved to ABN-AMRO's Hungarian bank and later led the Magyar Nemzeti Bank.
n:CIG Pannonia Life Insurance: A life insurer based in Budapest, Hungary. Zsigmond Jarai joined its supervisory board, the body that oversees the managers, in early 2008, after leading the Magyar Nemzeti Bank.
n:Board of Audit and Inspection of Korea: The state body in Seoul that audits South Korean public institutions. The Bank of Korea Act requires it to audit the Bank of Korea's accounts, so the bank's books are checked by a government auditor rather than only by a private accounting firm.
n:Auditor of the Bank of Korea (appointe: An auditor inside the Bank of Korea in Seoul whose job the Bank of Korea Act creates. The President of South Korea appoints the person who holds it, and the Act gives them the task of auditing the bank's accounts.
n:First Abu Dhabi Bank: A commercial bank based in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. Abdulhamid Saeed was a board member and group chief executive there before a federal decree made him Governor of the Central Bank of the UAE on 2 April 2020.
n:Alpha Bank: A commercial bank based in Athens, Greece. Georgios Provopoulos was its economic adviser from 1993, at the start of a career in Greek private banking that ended with the governorship of the Bank of Greece in June 2008.
n:Emporiki Bank: A bank based in Athens, Greece. Georgios Provopoulos took a management role there in 2004 and oversaw its sale to the French bank Credit Agricole, before he became Governor of the Bank of Greece in June 2008.
n:Piraeus Bank: A commercial bank based in Athens, Greece. Georgios Provopoulos was its vice president and chief executive from 2006 to 2008, the post he left to become Governor of the Bank of Greece.
n:ING Bank: A bank based in Amsterdam, Netherlands. Valeria Gontareva worked there before she became Governor of the National Bank of Ukraine in 2014, though the source naming the firm gives no role or years.
n:Investment Capital Ukraine: A financial services group based in Kyiv, Ukraine, known as ICU. Valeria Gontareva worked there before she became Governor of the National Bank of Ukraine in 2014, though the source naming the firm gives no role or years.
n:Erste Bank Hungary: A commercial bank based in Budapest, Hungary, part of the Austrian Erste group. It named Radovan Jelasic, a former Governor of the National Bank of Serbia, its chairman and chief executive on 10 May 2011, to join the management on 1 June 2011 once the Hungarian market regulators approved.
n:First Chicago Corporation: A bank holding company in Chicago, United States, and the parent of the First National Bank of Chicago. William J. McDonough spent about 22 years there before joining the Federal Reserve Bank of New York in 1992 and becoming its president in 1993.
n:Morgan Grenfell & Co: A merchant bank in London, United Kingdom, meaning a bank that arranges finance for companies rather than taking deposits from the public. Tom Dechaene was an assistant director there from 1991 to 1998, before Deutsche Bank and, later, a seat on the board of the National Bank of Belgium.
n:Bank Brussel Lambert: A bank based in Brussels, Belgium. Tom Dechaene was an executive there from 1986 to 1990, at the start of a banking career that ended with his appointment as a Director of the National Bank of Belgium in December 2014.
n:Realkredit Danmark: A mortgage bank based in Copenhagen, Denmark, meaning a lender that funds home loans by issuing bonds. Lars Rohde was its fund director from 1989 to 1992, a director from 1992 to 1997 and deputy managing director from 1997 to 1998, long before he chaired Danmarks Nationalbank's Board of Governors.
n:Nordea: A bank based in Helsinki, Finland, operating across the Nordic countries. Lars Rohde joined its board of directors in 2024, the year after he finished ten years chairing the Board of Governors of Danmarks Nationalbank.
n:Bank Pekao: A commercial bank based in Warsaw, Poland. Dariusz Filar was its chief economist from March 1999 until the day he was appointed to the Monetary Policy Council of the National Bank of Poland.
n:MKS (Switzerland): A firm based in Geneva, Switzerland. Jean-Pierre Roth sits on its board; he chaired the Swiss National Bank's Governing Board from 2001 to 2009. The source naming the seat gives no years for it.
n:DSK Bank: A commercial bank based in Sofia, Bulgaria. Kalin Hristov, a long-standing member of the Bulgarian National Bank's Governing Council and Deputy Governor of its Issue Department, joined the bank's Supervisory Board in August 2025.
n:TAGES Holding: An asset management holding company based in Milan, Italy. Lorenzo Bini Smaghi was a director from 2014 to 2019, between leaving the European Central Bank's Executive Board in December 2011 and chairing the board of Societe Generale from 2015.
n:SG Securities: Part of Societe Generale, based in Singapore. Arjuna Mahendran was its head of economic research for ASEAN and South Asia after resigning from the Central Bank of Sri Lanka in 1995, and returned to that bank as Governor in January 2015.
n:Emirates NBD: A bank based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Arjuna Mahendran was a managing director and chief investment officer with it and with HSBC Private Bank, before becoming Governor of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka in January 2015. Which of the two banks held which title is not stated.
n:United Overseas Bank: A commercial bank based in Singapore. It appointed Ong Chong Tee, a former Deputy Managing Director of the Monetary Authority of Singapore, a director on 1 January 2023. He chairs its audit committee and sits on its board risk management and executive committees.
n:AIA Group: An insurance group based in Hong Kong. Ong Chong Tee, a former Deputy Managing Director of the Monetary Authority of Singapore, is one of its directors.
n:Financiera Confianza: A lender based in Lima, Peru. Eduardo Torres-Llosa sat on its board after leaving BBVA in Peru in June 2019 and before becoming general manager of the Central Reserve Bank of Peru in March 2022.
n:Cosapi: An engineering and construction firm based in Lima, Peru. Eduardo Torres-Llosa chaired its board after leaving BBVA in Peru in June 2019 and before becoming general manager of the Central Reserve Bank of Peru in March 2022.
n:Troika Dialog: An investment bank based in Moscow, Russia. Oleg Vyugin, a First Deputy Chairman of the Bank of Russia, was its executive vice president. The CV that lists both roles gives no dates, so the order is not established.
n:MDM Bank: A commercial bank based in Moscow, Russia. Oleg Vyugin, a First Deputy Chairman of the Bank of Russia, chaired its board of directors. The CV that lists both roles gives no dates.
n:Binbank: A commercial bank based in Moscow, Russia. Oleg Vyugin, a First Deputy Chairman of the Bank of Russia, sat on its board of directors. The CV that lists both roles gives no dates.
n:Safmar Financial Investments: A financial holding company based in Moscow, Russia. Oleg Vyugin, a First Deputy Chairman of the Bank of Russia, chairs its board of directors. The CV that lists both roles gives no dates.
n:Sagicor Jamaica: A financial group based in Kingston, Jamaica. Richard Byles was its chief executive from 2004 until he retired in 2017 and then its non-executive chairman, before becoming Governor of the Bank of Jamaica on 19 August 2019.
n:Pan Jam: A conglomerate based in Kingston, Jamaica. Richard Byles led it as chief executive from 1991 for thirteen years, before Sagicor Jamaica and the Bank of Jamaica governorship.
n:Pan Caribbean Merchant Bank: A merchant bank based in Kingston, Jamaica. Richard Byles was its managing director from 1988, the first of the private posts he held before becoming Governor of the Bank of Jamaica in 2019.
n:Red Stripe: A brewer based in Kingston, Jamaica. Richard Byles has chaired it; the announcement of his appointment as Governor of the Bank of Jamaica names the role without dates.
n:HODA Holdings: House of Duffuor Assets (HODA) Holdings, based in Accra, Ghana. Kwabena Duffuor, Governor of the Bank of Ghana from 1997 to 2001, is its founder, president and adviser. It houses more than fifteen companies across industries including real estate, insurance and banking.
n:uniBank Ghana: A commercial bank in Accra, Ghana, described as the largest holding of Kwabena Duffuor, who was Governor of the Bank of Ghana from 1997 to 2001. In February 2020 the Attorney-General charged Duffuor and seven others over the bank's collapse; on 22 July 2025 the Attorney-General ended that case.
n:Star Assurance: An insurance company in Accra, Ghana, and one of the companies of HODA Holdings, founded by Kwabena Duffuor, Governor of the Bank of Ghana from 1997 to 2001.
n:Banca Comerciala Romana: A commercial bank based in Bucharest, Romania. Nicolae Danila was its chief executive from 1999 to 2008, and joined the National Bank of Romania's Board of Administration in October 2009.
n:First Bank SA: A commercial bank based in Bucharest, Romania. Nicolae Danila chaired its Board of Administration from July 2018 to July 2020, after five years on the National Bank of Romania's board.
n:TRANSFOND: The technical operator of Romania's electronic payment system, based in Bucharest; its shareholders are the National Bank of Romania and Romanian banks. Nicolae Danila, a former member of the National Bank's Board of Administration, chaired it from August 2015 to July 2019.
n:Chase Manhattan Bank: A bank in New York. Paul Volcker worked there as a financial economist from about 1957 and returned as vice president and director of forward planning from 1965, between spells at the Treasury, before becoming president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York on 1 August 1975.
n:Pittsburgh National Bank: A bank in Pittsburgh, United States. Jerry L. Jordan was its senior vice president and economist from 1975 to 1980, after eight years at the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis and before the Cleveland Fed presidency.
n:Interstate Bancorp: A bank holding company in Los Angeles. Jerry L. Jordan was its senior vice president and chief economist from 1985 to 1992, and became president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland in March 1992.
n:Security Pacific National Bank: A bank in Los Angeles. Robert T. Parry joined it as a vice president in 1970 from the Federal Reserve Board and rose to executive vice president and chief economist of the bank and of Security Pacific Corporation, before becoming president of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco on 4 February 1986.
n:Mellon Bank: A bank in Pittsburgh, United States. Silas Keehn worked there from 1957 in its credit, international and national departments, became its vice chairman, and left in 1980; he became president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago on 1 July 1981. John J. Balles was its senior vice president over economic and corporate planning from 1959, having left the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland that year, and became president of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco in September 1972.
A manufacturer in Chicago. Silas Keehn chaired its board of directors in 1980, between leaving the vice chairmanship of Mellon Bank and becoming president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago in July 1981.
n:American Stock Exchange: A stock exchange in New York. Richard F. Syron became its chairman and chief executive in 1994, the year he left the presidency of the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston.
n:Freddie Mac: The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation, a shareholder-owned mortgage company in McLean, United States. Richard F. Syron was its chairman and chief executive from 2003 to 2008, having been president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston from 1989 to 1994.
n:Federal Home Loan Bank of Boston: One of the Federal Home Loan Banks, owned by its member lenders. Richard F. Syron was its president from January 1986 until he became president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston on 1 January 1989.
n:First Nationwide Financial Corp: A savings and loan holding company in San Francisco. William F. Ford became its president on 1 October 1983, the day he left the presidency of the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta.
A bank holding company. Karen N. Horn became its chair and chief executive in Cleveland in 1987, the year she resigned as president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland.
n:First National Bank of Boston: A bank in Boston. Karen N. Horn was an economist and then a vice president there, between a spell as a senior economist at the Federal Reserve Board and the Cleveland Fed presidency she took up in 1982.
n:Bell Telephone Company of Pennsylvania: A telephone company in Philadelphia. Karen N. Horn was its treasurer from 1978, before becoming president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland on 1 May 1982.
n:Diamond State Telephone Company: A telephone company. Karen N. Horn was its treasurer at the same time as she was treasurer of the Bell Telephone Company of Pennsylvania, before the Cleveland Fed presidency.
A bank holding company in Pittsburgh. W. Lee Hoskins was its chief economist and senior vice president for economics and corporate affairs from 1980 to 1987, and became president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland on 8 October 1987.
n:Huntington National Bank: A commercial bank in Columbus, United States. W. Lee Hoskins resigned as president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland on 15 November 1991 to become its president and chief executive.
An investment firm in Boston. Frank E. Morris was a vice president there from 1963, and became president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston in August 1968.
n:Investment Bankers Association: A trade body for investment banks, in Washington. Frank E. Morris was its research director from 1955 to 1961, before the Treasury and then the Boston Fed presidency.
n:Leigh Fisher and Associates: A consulting firm. Frank E. Morris worked there on airport planning and management from 1948 to 1951, the earliest job listed before his Federal Reserve career.
n:Amerisure Companies: Amerisure Companies is an insurer in the United States. Martha R. Seger held a seat on its board, with no dates given. She was a financial economist at the Federal Reserve Board of Governors from 1964, chief economist at Detroit Bank and Trust, then a vice president at the Bank of the Commonwealth in Detroit from 1974, and Michigan's Commissioner of Financial Institutions from 1981 to 1982. She served as a Federal Reserve governor from 2 July 1984 to 3 March 1991. No ethics finding is recorded.
n:BDO & Co, Chartered Accountants: BDO & Co, Chartered Accountants is an accountancy firm in Port Louis, Mauritius. It is the external auditor of the Bank of Mauritius, the central bank of Mauritius, which means it is the outside firm brought in to check the bank's accounts and say whether they give a true picture. It audited the accounts for the year ended 30 June 2025.
n:Bank of the Commonwealth: The Bank of the Commonwealth was a bank in Detroit, United States. Martha R. Seger worked there before she joined the Federal Reserve. She came to the Fed from Detroit Bank and Trust and the Bank of the Commonwealth, served as a governor on the Board of Governors from 2 July 1984 to 3 March 1991, and then left for her own firm, M.R. Seger & Associates. Moving between a bank and the body that oversees banking is a career move, not an accusation.
n:Beal Bank: Beal Bank is a bank in the United States. Robert D. McTeer Jr. joined its board after leaving the Federal Reserve. He was president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, one of the twelve regional banks that make up the Federal Reserve System, from 1 February 1991 to 4 November 2004, and from there took board seats at Westwood Holdings Group and at Beal Bank.
n:Chicago Board Options Exchange: The Chicago Board Options Exchange is a financial exchange in Chicago, United States. Susan M. Phillips joined its board after her time at the Federal Reserve. She came from the chairmanship of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, was sworn in as a governor of the Federal Reserve Board on 2 December 1991 and left on 20 June 1998, and afterwards took board seats at the Chicago Board Options Exchange, the Chicago Futures Exchange and State Farm Insurance.
n:Colina Holdings Ltd: Colina Holdings Ltd is an insurer in Nassau, Bahamas. Its investment arm is CFAL, which describes itself as an independent investment management and advisory firm offering pension administration, brokerage and private wealth services. James H. Smith, CBE, was Governor of the Central Bank of The Bahamas from 1987 to 1997 and is Chairman of CFAL, with no dates given for that post. He was also Senator and Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance from 2002 to 2007.
n:DongA Bank: DongA Bank is a joint-stock commercial bank in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, meaning a bank owned by shareholders rather than by the state. Cao Si Kiem, who was Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam, the country's central bank, from 1989 to 1997, became an independent member of DongA Bank's board in March 2012 and chaired its management board from 26 April 2014 to 2015.
n:Fair Isaac Corporation: Fair Isaac Corporation is a firm in the United States. H. Robert Heller worked there after his time at the Federal Reserve. He came to the Fed from Bank of America, served as a governor on the Board of Governors from 19 August 1986 to 31 July 1989, then became chief executive of Visa U.S.A. and after that went to Fair Isaac Corporation.
n:Harris Trust and Savings Bank: Harris Trust and Savings Bank is a bank in Chicago, United States. Theodore H. Roberts worked there both before and after running a part of the Federal Reserve. He went from Harris Trust and Savings Bank to the presidency of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, which he held from 1 February 1983 to 31 December 1984, then returned to Harris Bank and later moved to Talman Home Federal Savings and Loan and LaSalle National Bank.
n:Islamic International Arab Bank: Islamic International Arab Bank is a bank in Amman, Jordan. Mohammed Said Mohammed Shahin has been its Chairman since 31 March 2017. Before that he was Deputy Governor and then Governor and Chairman of the Central Bank of Jordan, the body that issues the country's money and oversees its banks. His move from the central bank to the chairmanship of a bank it supervises is a career move, with nothing improper attached to it.
n:Liberty Mutual Insurance Company: Liberty Mutual Insurance Company is an insurer in Boston, United States. John P. LaWare was one of its directors, with no dates given. He began in finance in 1953, rose through Chemical Bank & Trust Co. in New York and later worked at Shawmut Bank in Boston, where he sat on the Federal Reserve's Federal Advisory Council from 1986 to 1988. He was a governor of the Federal Reserve Board from 15 August 1988 until he resigned on 30 April 1995. No ethics finding is recorded.
n:Northern Trust Company: The Northern Trust Company is a bank in Chicago, United States. J. Charles Partee worked there before joining the Federal Reserve. He went from Northern Trust Company of Chicago to the Fed's staff and then to a seat on its Board of Governors, which he held from 5 January 1976 to 7 February 1986. After that he joined the board of State Farm Insurance and took a mutual fund trusteeship.
n:Schultz Investments: Schultz Investments is a firm in the United States, set up by Frederick H. Schultz. He came to the Federal Reserve from the chairmanship of Barnett Investment Services and from his own firm, and served as Vice Chair of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors, taking office on 27 July 1979 and resigning on 11 February 1982.
n:Sovran Bank: Sovran Bank is a bank in Nashville, United States, the successor to Commerce Union Bank. J. Dewey Daane joined it after his time at the Federal Reserve. He came from the United States Treasury, served as a governor on the Federal Reserve Board from 29 November 1963 to 8 March 1974, and then became vice chairman of Commerce Union Bank and of Sovran Bank after it took the bank over.
n:Sun Insurance Company Ltd: Sun Insurance Company Ltd is an insurer in Suva, Fiji. Inia Naiyaga moved there in stages after leaving the Reserve Bank of Fiji, the country's central bank, where he was Deputy Governor until he retired in May 2014. He became a consultant to the SUN Insurance board in 2016, an independent director in April 2018, and Managing Director from 6 June 2018.
n:Visa: Visa is a payments firm based in San Francisco, United States. H. Robert Heller ran its United States arm after leaving the Federal Reserve. He came to the Fed from Bank of America, served as a governor on the Board of Governors from 19 August 1986 to 31 July 1989, then became chief executive of Visa U.S.A. and later moved to Fair Isaac Corporation.
n:Apex Group (Mauritius): Apex Group (Mauritius) is a fund administration firm, a business that handles the paperwork and accounts of investment funds, based in Mauritius. Dr Rama Krishna Sithanen was its independent chairperson and director from 2023 until 15 November 2024, and became Governor of the Bank of Mauritius the next day, 16 November 2024. He had earlier chaired International Financial Services from 2011 to 2016 and Sanne Mauritius from 2017 to 2022.
n:Bank South Pacific: Bank South Pacific is a commercial bank based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea. Two of its kind of senior banker have moved onto the board of the country's central bank, the Bank of Papua New Guinea: Sir Robin Fleming, formerly chief executive officer of Bank South Pacific, whose appointment was announced in April 2024, and Mark Baker, formerly country head of the commercial bank ANZ, appointed to the same board.
n:Barnett Banks of Florida: Barnett Banks of Florida was a banking group based in Jacksonville, in the United States. Frederick H. Schultz joined Barnett National Bank of Jacksonville in 1956, opened his own firm Schultz Investments in 1957, and was chairman of the board of Barnett Investment Services and a director of Barnett Banks of Florida when he became Vice Chair of the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors on 27 July 1979. He resigned on 11 February 1982, returned to Florida, and founded The Schultz Center for Teaching and Leadership in Jacksonville in 1997. No ethics finding against him is recorded.
Bear Stearns & Co., Inc. was an investment bank in New York. Wayne D. Angell taught economics at Ottawa University in Kansas from 1956 to 1985, sat in the Kansas House of Representatives from 1960 to 1966, and was an officer and director of several banks in Kansas and Missouri from 1971 to 1985. He was a Governor of the Federal Reserve Board from 7 February 1986 until he retired on 2 February 1994, after which he became chief economist at Bear Stearns.
n:Chicago Board of Trade: The Chicago Board of Trade is a market in Chicago where contracts on future prices are traded. J. Dewey Daane sat on it as a public director from 1979 to 1982, a few years after leaving the Federal Reserve. He had headed research at the Richmond Fed, moved to the Minneapolis Fed in May 1960 and then to the Treasury, and was a Governor of the Federal Reserve Board from 29 November 1963 to 8 March 1974. Afterwards he taught banking at Vanderbilt University and was vice chairman of Commerce Union Bank.
n:Commerce Union Bank: Commerce Union Bank was a commercial bank in Nashville, in the United States. J. Dewey Daane went from the Treasury to a seat on the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors, which he held from 29 November 1963 to 8 March 1974, and afterwards became a senior official and vice chairman of the board at Commerce Union Bank and at its successor, Sovran Bank, in Nashville. No dates are given for that later work.
n:ERNST & YOUNG (HELLAS) Certified Audit: Ernst & Young (Hellas) Certified Auditors-Accountants S.A. is an accounting firm in Maroussi, in the Athens area of Greece. It checks the books of the Bank of Greece, the country's central bank, and signs off on whether the figures are accurate. It was first appointed to that work on 7 April 2022, and on 8 April 2025 its appointment was renewed for the year ending 31 December 2025.
n:Farmers Savings & Loan: Farmers Savings & Loan was a savings and loan institution in the United States, the kind of lender that takes deposits and writes home loans. Sherman J. Maisel came from the University of California, Berkeley to a seat on the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors, which he held from 30 April 1965 to 31 May 1972, and afterwards became chairman of the board of Farmers Savings & Loan and ran his own firm, Sherman J. Maisel & Associates.
n:International Financial Services: International Financial Services is a financial firm based in Mauritius. Dr Rama Krishna Sithanen was its chairperson and director from 2011 to 2016. He then chaired Sanne Mauritius from 2017 to 2022 and was independent chairperson and director of the fund administration firm Apex Group (Mauritius) from 2023 until 15 November 2024, moving from that post straight into the governorship of the Bank of Mauritius, the country's central bank, on 16 November 2024.
Johnson Smick International, Inc. is an investment and consulting firm in Washington, in the United States. Manuel H. Johnson came to the Federal Reserve from the Treasury, becoming a Governor on 7 February 1986 and Vice Chair of the Board on 22 August 1986. He left the Federal Reserve on 3 August 1990 and went to Johnson Smick International.
n:Long-Term Capital Management: Long-Term Capital Management was an investment firm based in Greenwich, in the United States. David W. Mullins Jr. came to the Federal Reserve from the Treasury, becoming a Governor on 21 May 1990 and Vice Chair of the Board on 24 July 1991. His resignation took effect on 14 February 1994, and he joined Long-Term Capital Management.
PMI Mortgage Insurance Co. is a United States insurer covering home loans, so that the lender is paid if a borrower stops paying. Preston Martin came from private banking and savings-and-loan ventures to be Vice Chair of the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors from 31 March 1982 to 30 April 1986. After leaving, he founded PMI Mortgage Insurance Co. and a partnership that took over failing thrifts and banks.
n:Shawmut Bank: Shawmut Bank was a commercial bank in Boston, in the United States. John P. LaWare came from Chemical Bank & Trust and Shawmut Bank to a seat on the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors, which he held from 15 August 1988 to 30 April 1995. He left the Federal Reserve for Stewart Information Services Corp.
n:State Audit of Vietnam: The State Audit of Vietnam is the country's government audit body. It checks the books of the State Bank of Vietnam, the central bank, confirming whether its accounts are accurate. This is not a one-off engagement but a standing arrangement written into the law governing the central bank, as set out in the 2022 consolidated text of that law.
n:Talman Home Federal Savings and Loan: Talman Home Federal Savings and Loan was a savings and loan institution in Chicago, the kind of lender that takes deposits and writes home loans. Theodore H. Roberts came from Harris Trust and Savings Bank to be president of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis from 1 February 1983 to 31 December 1984. From there he went back to Harris Bank, and then on to Talman Home Federal Savings and Loan and LaSalle National Bank.
n:West Belt National Bank: West Belt National Bank was a commercial bank in the United States. Edward W. Kelley Jr. was one of its founding directors, as he was of Southern National Bank and Westwood Commerce Bank, and he also sat on the board of Promontory Interfinancial Network. He came to the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors from the chairmanship of Investment Advisors, Inc., was sworn in on 26 May 1987, reappointed on 20 April 1990, and retired on 31 December 2001.
n:Arab Bank plc: Arab Bank plc is a commercial bank based in Amman, Jordan. It is tied to the Central Bank of Jordan through one man. Mohammed Said Mohammed Shahin, born 1948, is a former Governor and Chairman of the Central Bank of Jordan, a former Deputy Governor of it, and a former Chairman and Chief Executive of the state-run Jordan Deposit Insurance Corporation. He joined the board of the Islamic International Arab Bank on 31 March 2017 and chairs it. Several other directors of that bank are serving executives of Arab Bank plc, including its vice chairman, who is Executive Vice President and Head of Consumer Banking at Arab Bank plc.
n:Bank of Fort Valley: The Bank of Fort Valley is a bank in Fort Valley, Georgia, in the United States, and M. Monroe Kimbrel was its chairman. He had worked in the lumber business in Thomson, Georgia and as a credit examiner for the Farm Credit Administration, joined the First National Bank of Thomson in 1946 and later ran it as president and chairman. He sat on the board of the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta from 1960 to 1965, became its senior vice president on 1 June 1965, and was its president and chief executive from 1 February 1968 to 31 March 1980. He then became vice chairman of the First Railroad and Banking Co. of Georgia.
Barnett Investment Services, Inc. is an investment firm in the United States. Frederick H. Schultz was chairman of its board when he was appointed to the Federal Reserve, the United States central bank, and he served as Vice Chair of its Board of Governors from 27 July 1979 until he resigned on 11 February 1982. He had joined Barnett National Bank of Jacksonville in 1956, opened his own firm, Schultz Investments, in 1957, and was a director of Barnett Banks of Florida. Afterwards he returned to Florida and founded The Schultz Center for Teaching and Leadership in Jacksonville in 1997. He died in 2009.
n:CFAL: CFAL is an asset manager in Nassau, the Bahamas. Its chairman is James H. Smith, who was Governor of the Central Bank of The Bahamas from 1987 to 1997 and took the CFAL chairmanship afterwards; the source gives no dates for it. Moving between a country's central bank and a firm that manages money is what this map records as a revolving door. It is a career move, not an accusation of wrongdoing.
n:Chicago Futures Exchange: The Chicago Futures Exchange is a firm in Chicago, in the United States. Susan M. Phillips joined its board after serving at the Federal Reserve, the United States central bank. She came to the Fed from the chairmanship of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the federal futures regulator, was sworn in as a Governor of its Board of Governors on 2 December 1991, and left on 20 June 1998. She then took seats on the boards of the Chicago Board Options Exchange, the Chicago Futures Exchange and State Farm Insurance.
n:Commission on Audit: The Commission on Audit is the state auditor of the Philippines. It audits the accounts of Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, the Philippine central bank, which means it checks the bank's own financial statements and reports on whether they are accurate. This is not a one-off engagement: the arrangement is written into Section 47 of Republic Act No. 7653, the New Central Bank Act of 1993, and has stood since then.
Ernst & Young Kft. is an accounting firm in Budapest, Hungary. It audits the accounts of Magyar Nemzeti Bank, the Hungarian central bank, for the year ended 31 December 2025. An external audit means an outside firm checks the bank's own financial statements and reports on whether they are accurate, so the firm doing it sees the bank's books from the inside.
n:First National Bank of Thomson: The First National Bank of Thomson is a bank in Thomson, Georgia, in the United States, and M. Monroe Kimbrel was its president and chairman. He left that bank for the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, part of the Federal Reserve System, the United States central bank, and was its president and chief executive from 1 February 1968 to 31 March 1980. From there he went to the vice chairmanship of the First Railroad and Banking Co. of Georgia.
Investment Advisors, Inc. is an asset manager in the United States, and Edward W. Kelley Jr. was its chairman before he joined the Federal Reserve, the United States central bank. He was sworn in as a Governor of its Board of Governors on 26 May 1987, sworn in again for a second term on 20 April 1990, and retired on 31 December 2001.
