He was also a founding director of Southern National Bank, Westwood Commerce Bank and West Belt National Bank and a director of Promontory Interfinancial Network.
KPMG ehf. is an accounting firm in Reykjavik, Iceland. It audited the accounts of the Central Bank of Iceland for the year ended 31 December 2022. An external audit means an outside firm checks the bank's own financial statements and reports on whether they are accurate, so the firm doing it sees the bank's books from the inside.
n:M.R. Seger & Associates: M.R. Seger & Associates is a firm in the United States run by Martha R. Seger. She came to the Federal Reserve, the United States central bank, from the commercial banks Detroit Bank and Trust and the Bank of the Commonwealth, served as a Governor of its Board of Governors from 2 July 1984 to 3 March 1991, and left the Fed for her own firm.
n:Promontory Interfinancial Network, LLC: Promontory Interfinancial Network, LLC is a financial firm in Arlington, in the United States, and Edward W. Kelley Jr. is one of its directors. He had run Kelley Manufacturing Company, the firm his father established in 1937, returning to Houston after earning his MBA in 1959, and expanded it into a holding company. He sold the company in 1981 and became chairman of Investment Advisors, Inc. that same year. He was sworn in as a Governor of the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors on 26 May 1987, began a second term on 20 April 1990 and retired on 31 December 2001. He was also a founding director of three banks and a trustee of the Financial Accounting Foundation Inc.
Sherman J. Maisel & Associates Inc. is a firm in the United States, and Sherman J. Maisel was its president from 1986 to 2010. He had been a research economist at the Federal Reserve Board of Governors in Washington from 1939 to 1941, served in the US Army from 1941 and reached captain by 1945, spent a year in the US Foreign Service in Brussels, and taught at the Haas School of Business at the University of California, Berkeley from 1948 until 1965. He was a Governor of the Federal Reserve from 30 April 1965 to 31 May 1972, then returned to Haas until 1986 and chaired the board of Farmers Savings & Loan from 1986 to 1988.
n:State Farm Insurance: State Farm Insurance is an insurer based in Bloomington, in the United States, and two former Federal Reserve governors have sat on its board. Susan M. Phillips came to the Federal Reserve, the United States central bank, from the chairmanship of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the federal futures regulator, was sworn in as a Governor on 2 December 1991 and left on 20 June 1998, after which she took board seats at State Farm, the Chicago Board Options Exchange and the Chicago Futures Exchange. J. Charles Partee came from the Northern Trust Company of Chicago to the Fed staff and then a governorship from 5 January 1976 to 7 February 1986, and went on to the State Farm board and a mutual fund trusteeship.
n:The National Bank of Washington: The National Bank of Washington is a bank in Washington, in the United States. Emmett J. Rice was its senior vice president, and he left that job for the Federal Reserve, the United States central bank, serving as a Governor of its Board of Governors from 20 June 1979 to 31 December 1986.
n:Westwood Commerce Bank: Westwood Commerce Bank is a bank in the United States, and Edward W. Kelley Jr. was one of its founding directors. He came to the Federal Reserve, the United States central bank, from the chairmanship of the asset manager Investment Advisors, Inc., was sworn in as a Governor of its Board of Governors on 26 May 1987, began a second term on 20 April 1990 and retired on 31 December 2001. He was also a founding director of Southern National Bank and West Belt National Bank and a director of Promontory Interfinancial Network.
n:Australia and New Zealand Banking Grou: The Australia and New Zealand Banking Group is a commercial bank based in Melbourne. Its link to a central bank is a person. Mark Baker, its former country head, was named to the board of the Bank of Papua New Guinea in an announcement made in April 2024, at the same time as Sir Robin Fleming, the former chief executive of another commercial bank, Bank South Pacific. Two men who had run commercial banks thus took seats on the body that governs the country's central bank.
n:Bank of Marin: Bank of Marin is a bank in the United States. Its tie to the Federal Reserve, the American central bank, is H. Robert Heller, who sat on the Fed's Board of Governors from 19 August 1986 to 31 July 1989. He came from Bank of America in San Francisco, where he directed international economic research, and before that headed the financial studies division of the International Monetary Fund. He left the Fed for Visa U.S.A., running it from 1991 for two years, then Fair Isaac Corporation until 2001, and now holds board seats at Bank of Marin and Bank of Marin Bancorp. No ethics finding is recorded.
n:Barnett National Bank of Jacksonville: Barnett National Bank of Jacksonville is a bank in Florida that Frederick H. Schultz joined in 1956, a year before opening his own firm, Schultz Investments. He was chairman of Barnett Investment Services and a director of Barnett Banks of Florida when he was made Vice Chair of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve, the American central bank, a post he held from 27 July 1979 until he resigned on 11 February 1982. He then returned to Florida and founded a teaching centre in Jacksonville in 1997. He died in 2009. No ethics finding is recorded.
Chemical Bank & Trust Co. is a New York bank where John P. LaWare rose through the ranks after starting in finance in 1953. He moved on to Shawmut Bank in Boston, served on the Federal Reserve's Federal Advisory Council from 1986 to 1988 and was a director of its Boston regional bank in 1988, then became a Governor of the Federal Reserve, the American central bank, from 15 August 1988 until he resigned on 30 April 1995. He left for Stewart Information Services Corp. No ethics finding is recorded.
n:Coldwell Financial Consultants: Coldwell Financial Consultants is a firm in Washington. Philip E. Coldwell went to it after a long run inside the Federal Reserve, the American central bank: he was president of its Dallas regional bank from 1 February 1968 to 28 October 1974, and then a member of the Fed's Board of Governors, which sets national policy, from 29 October 1974 to 29 February 1980.
n:Detroit Bank and Trust: Detroit Bank and Trust is a bank in Detroit. Martha R. Seger worked there and at the Bank of the Commonwealth before joining the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve, the American central bank, where she served from 2 July 1984 to 3 March 1991. On leaving she set up her own firm, M.R. Seger & Associates.
n:Ernst & Young Professional Services: Ernst & Young Professional Services is an audit firm based in Riyadh. It audits the accounts of the Saudi Central Bank, meaning it checks the central bank's own books and signs off on them. It did the audit for the financial year that ended on 30 June 2023, the year covered by the bank's sixtieth annual report.
n:First Railroad and Banking Co. of Geor: First Railroad and Banking Co. of Georgia is a bank in the United States. M. Monroe Kimbrel became its vice chairman after running the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, one of the regional banks of the American central bank, as president and chief executive from 1 February 1968 to 31 March 1980. He had come to that post from the presidency and chairmanship of the First National Bank of Thomson.
n:Irving Trust Company: Irving Trust Company is a New York bank where Sir Courtney Blackman worked as an economist from 1968 to 1971. He left it to become the founding Governor of the Central Bank of Barbados, which he led from 1972 to 1987. After leaving the central bank he took directorships at financial institutions that are not named.
n:LaSalle National Bank: LaSalle National Bank is a bank in Chicago, and the last stop in a career that ran in and out of the Federal Reserve, the American central bank. Theodore H. Roberts came from Harris Trust and Savings Bank to the presidency of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, which he held from 1 February 1983 to 31 December 1984. He then went back to Harris Bank, on to Talman Home Federal Savings and Loan, and then to LaSalle National Bank.
n:National Futures Association: The National Futures Association is a Chicago body on whose board J. Dewey Daane sat as a public director from 1987 to 2002. Daane rose from statistician to head of research at the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond, advised the Treasury Secretary on debt management from 1960, and was appointed by President Kennedy to the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors, serving from 29 November 1963 to 8 March 1974. He then taught banking at Vanderbilt University and was vice chairman of Commerce Union Bank and its successor Sovran Bank. No ethics finding is recorded.
n:Sanne Mauritius: Sanne Mauritius is a firm in Mauritius that Dr Rama Krishna Sithanen chaired, and was a director of, from 2017 to 2022. Before that he chaired International Financial Services from 2011 to 2016, and after it he was independent chairperson and director of Apex Group (Mauritius), a firm that administers investment funds, from 2023 until 15 November 2024. The next day, 16 November 2024, he became Governor of the Bank of Mauritius.
n:Southern National Bank: Southern National Bank is a bank in the United States that Edward W. Kelley Jr. helped start as a founding director, as he did Westwood Commerce Bank and West Belt National Bank. He was chairman of Investment Advisors, Inc. before being sworn in as a Governor of the Federal Reserve, the American central bank, on 26 May 1987. He was reappointed on 20 April 1990 and retired on 31 December 2001. He was also a director of Promontory Interfinancial Network.
Stewart Information Services Corp. is an insurer in Houston. John P. LaWare joined it after leaving the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve, the American central bank, where he was a Governor from 15 August 1988 to 30 April 1995. He had reached that post from two commercial banks, Chemical Bank & Trust and Shawmut Bank.
n:Travelers Real Estate Investors Trust: Travelers Real Estate Investors Trust is a United States asset manager on which John P. LaWare served as a trustee, with no dates given. He had risen through Chemical Bank & Trust Co. in New York and then Shawmut Bank in Boston, was a director of the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston in 1988, and was a Governor of the Federal Reserve, the American central bank, from 15 August 1988 until he resigned on 30 April 1995. He then became an advisory director of Stewart Information Services Corp. and a director of Liberty Mutual Insurance Company. No ethics finding is recorded.
n:Westwood Holdings Group: Westwood Holdings Group is an asset manager in Dallas. Robert D. McTeer Jr. took a seat on its board, and on that of Beal Bank, after running the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, one of the regional banks of the American central bank, as president from 1 February 1991 to 4 November 2004.
n:AXA Affin General Insurance Berhad: AXA Affin General Insurance Berhad is an insurer in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, tied to Bank Negara Malaysia through one person. Dato' Dr. Nirmala Menon was appointed to the central bank's board on 16 March 2020 as an independent non-executive member and chairs its Board Risk Committee. The bank's own board page lists, among her earlier roles and without years, chief executive of ING Malaysia Berhad, executive vice president at MetLife Asia Pacific Limited, and a board seat at AXA Affin General Insurance Berhad. A board seat is not an accusation.
n:Caisse Interprofessionnelle Marocaine: The Caisse Interprofessionnelle Marocaine de Retraites, or CIMR, is a pension body in Casablanca, Morocco, which the insurance regulator ACAPS describes as a private-sector employers' pension fund. It is tied to Bank Al-Maghrib through one person: Abdellatif Jouahri, who was president of the CIMR and went straight from that job into the Wali, or governorship, of Bank Al-Maghrib in 2003. Before the CIMR he was president of BMCE until 1995. A career move is not an accusation.
n:Continental Illinois National Bank and: Continental Illinois National Bank and Trust Company is a bank in Chicago, United States, tied to the Federal Reserve System through one person. Robert P. Mayo worked at Continental Illinois in Chicago, then went into federal service and on to the presidency of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, which he held from 1970 to 1981. That is a career move, not an accusation, and nothing improper is recorded.
n:East Caribbean Financial Holding Co. L: East Caribbean Financial Holding Co. Ltd is a financial holding company in Castries, St. Lucia, tied to the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank through one person. Trevor Brathwaite held a seat on the company's board, and his career ran into the central bank: he was Saint Lucia's representative on its board of directors from October 2002 to March 2006, then its deputy governor from April 2006 to September 2021. A board seat is not wrongdoing.
n:First National Bank of St. Louis: First National Bank of St. Louis is a bank in St. Louis, United States, tied to the Federal Reserve System through one person. Lawrence K. Roos went from First National Bank of St. Louis to the presidency of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, which he held from 1976 to 1983, and afterwards to the firm Bear, Stearns and Company. Those are career moves, not accusations, and no wrongdoing is recorded.
n:KPMG Peat Marwick: KPMG Peat Marwick is an accounting firm in St. Lucia. It is tied to the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank through one person: Trevor Brathwaite, an accountant who worked for KPMG Peat Marwick in Saint Lucia, New Zealand and Barbados early in a career that later ran about fourteen years in Saint Lucia's government, including Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Finance from 2002 to 2006. He was the central bank's deputy governor from April 2006 to September 2021. No wrongdoing is recorded.
n:Merchants Bank (Fort Smith, Arkansas): Merchants Bank is a bank in Fort Smith, United States, tied to the Federal Reserve System through one person. Darryl R. Francis began at the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis in 1944 as an agricultural economist, worked as a commercial banker in Memphis, rejoined the St. Louis Fed in 1953 and was its president from 17 January 1966 until he retired on 29 February 1976. Before retiring he also served as chairman of Merchants Bank in Fort Smith, Arkansas. No ethics finding is recorded.
n:National City Bank: National City Bank is a bank in New York, United States, tied to the Federal Reserve System through one person. Alfred Hayes worked in the bond department of the National City Bank, having begun in banking in 1933 at the City Bank Farmers Trust Company, and joined the New York Trust Company in 1942. He was named president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York on 1 August 1956; he retired on 1 August 1975 and joined Morgan Stanley International Inc. as chairman that November. No ethics finding is recorded.
n:SIA Ernst & Young Baltic: SIA Ernst & Young Baltic is a firm in Latvia. Its one tie to a central bank is an audit job: it audits the accounts of the Bank of Latvia, the Latvijas Banka, for the years 2020 to 2024. The appointment appears in the European Central Bank's decision of 7 October 1999 on the external auditors of the national central banks, as consolidated on 26 October 2021.
n:U.S. Bancorp: U.S. Bancorp is a bank in the United States. It is tied to the Federal Reserve System through one person: Mark W. Olson, who joined First Bank System, now US Bancorp, and was named an officer there in 1969, then in 1976 became president and chief executive of Security State Bank in Fergus Falls, Minnesota. He was sworn in as a member of the Board of Governors on 7 December 2001 and left on 30 June 2006. No ethics finding is recorded.
n:Auditor General: The Auditor General is Uganda's public audit office. It is tied to one central bank, the Bank of Uganda, whose accounts it audits, meaning it examines the bank's books and reports on them. This is not a one-off job but a standing arrangement written into the law that governs the bank, the Bank of Uganda Act, Statute 5 of 1993, at section 43, and it was still in place in the text of that law as in force on 31 December 2023.
n:Charles Schwab Corporation: The Charles Schwab Corporation is a brokerage, a firm that buys and sells investments for clients, in Washington, DC, in the United States. It is tied to one central bank, the Federal Reserve System, by a single career move. Lyle E. Gramley sat as a governor on the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors from 1980 to 1985, and went from that seat to the Schwab Washington Research Group and to Soleil Securities Corporation.
n:Controller and Auditor General: The Controller and Auditor General is Tanzania's public audit office. It is tied to one central bank, the Bank of Tanzania, whose accounts it audits, meaning it checks the bank's books and reports on what it finds. The job is a standing one, set out in the law that governs the bank, the Bank of Tanzania Act 2006, at section 20(6), and dating from that year.
n:Ernst & Young Baltic AS: Ernst & Young Baltic AS is an accounting firm in Estonia. It is tied to one central bank, the Bank of Estonia, known in Estonian as Eesti Pank, as its external auditor, the outside firm that checks the bank's accounts rather than its own staff doing so. It held that role from 2021 to 2025. The appointment runs through a European Central Bank decision of 7 October 1999 on the external auditors of the national central banks, in the consolidated text of 26 October 2021.
n:ING Asia Pacific Limited: ING Asia Pacific Limited is an insurer based in Hong Kong. It is tied to one central bank, Bank Negara Malaysia, through one person. Dato' Dr. Nirmala Menon was Head of South Asia at ING Asia Pacific Limited and, among her other past roles, President and Chief Executive Officer of ING Malaysia Berhad; the central bank's own page for its directors lists those jobs without giving the years. She joined the Bank Negara Malaysia board on 16 March 2020 as an independent non-executive member and chairs its Board Risk Committee.
n:MCG Capital Corporation: MCG Capital Corporation is an asset manager, a firm that invests money on behalf of others, in the United States. It is tied to one central bank, the Federal Reserve System, through one person. Jeffrey M. Bucher was senior vice president of the 1st Interstate Bank of California before being appointed a governor of the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors on 5 June 1972, and resigned on 2 January 1976. From 2001 to 2009 he sat on MCG Capital Corporation's board, as chairman from 2007 to 2009.
n:MetLife Asia Pacific Limited: MetLife Asia Pacific Limited is an insurer based in Hong Kong. It is tied to one central bank, Bank Negara Malaysia, through one person. Dato' Dr. Nirmala Menon was Executive Vice President at MetLife Asia Pacific Limited, one of several insurance jobs listed on the central bank's own page for its directors, which gives no start or end dates for any of them. She joined the Bank Negara Malaysia board on 16 March 2020 as an independent non-executive member and chairs its Board Risk Committee.
n:National Shawmut Bank: The National Shawmut Bank is a bank in Boston, in the United States. It is tied to one central bank, the Federal Reserve System, by a single career move. Joseph A. Erickson was an executive vice president of the National Shawmut Bank before he became president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston, part of the Federal Reserve System, a post he held from 1948 to 1961.
n:Security State Bank (Fergus Falls): Security State Bank is a bank in Fergus Falls, in the United States. It is tied to one central bank, the Federal Reserve System, through one person. Mark W. Olson was named its president and chief executive officer in 1976; his father had been the lead organizer in chartering the bank in 1957. Olson was later sworn in as a member of the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors on 7 December 2001 and left on 30 June 2006. He died in 2018.
n:UAB Ernst & Young Baltic: UAB Ernst & Young Baltic is an accounting firm in Lithuania. It is tied to one central bank, the Bank of Lithuania, as its external auditor, the outside firm brought in to check the bank's accounts. It held that role from 2018 to 2021. The appointment runs through a European Central Bank decision of 7 October 1999 on the external auditors of the national central banks, in the consolidated text of 26 October 2021.
n:Bear Stearns: Bear Stearns is a bank in the United States, tied to the Federal Reserve System through one person. Lawrence K. Roos was president of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis from 1976 to 1983. He came to that job from the First National Bank of St. Louis, and when he left the St. Louis Fed he went on to Bear, Stearns and Company.
n:City Bank Farmers Trust Company: City Bank Farmers Trust Company is a bank in New York. Alfred Hayes began his banking career there in 1933 as an analyst in its investment department, and joined the New York Trust Company in 1942, running its foreign division as vice president from 1949 to 1956. He came from there to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, was named its president on 1 August 1956, retired on 1 August 1975, and became chairman of Morgan Stanley International Inc. that November.
n:Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank of California: Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank of California is a bank in the United States. Jeffrey M. Bucher worked for the 1st Interstate Bank of California from 1957, as its senior vice president from 1969, until he was appointed to the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors on 5 June 1972. He served as a governor until he resigned on 2 January 1976, and afterwards sat on the board of directors of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank of California. No ethics finding is recorded.
n:First Interstate Bank of California: First Interstate Bank of California is a bank in the United States. It is tied to the Federal Reserve System through one person: Jeffrey M. Bucher, who went from the 1st Interstate Bank of California to the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors, served as a governor there from 1972 to 1976, and then moved on to bank boards and chairmanships, among them the chairmanship of First Interstate Bank of Washington.
n:ING Group: ING Group is a bank, marked in the United States. Robert P. Forrestal became president and chief executive officer of the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta on 7 December 1983 and served until 1 January 1996. After retiring from the bank he worked with the Atlanta law firm Smith, Gambrell & Russell and sat on several corporate boards, among them ING North America Co. and the ING Advisory Council in the Netherlands, as well as Equifax Inc. and Genuine Parts Co. He died in 2004. No ethics finding is recorded.
n:Manufacturers Bank: Manufacturers Bank is a bank in Los Angeles. Jeffrey M. Bucher worked for the 1st Interstate Bank of California from 1957, as its senior vice president from 1969, until his appointment to the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors on 5 June 1972, and he served as a governor until he resigned on 2 January 1976. He was a director of Manufacturers Bank from 1978 to 1980, and later chairman of First Interstate Bank of Washington from 1983 to 1987. No ethics finding is recorded.
n:Mizuho Corporate Bank of California: Mizuho Corporate Bank of California is a bank in the United States. Jeffrey M. Bucher was appointed to the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors on 5 June 1972, coming from the 1st Interstate Bank of California, where he had worked since 1957 and been senior vice president from 1969, and he served as a governor until he resigned on 2 January 1976. He later sat on the board of directors of Mizuho Corporate Bank of California. No ethics finding is recorded.
n:New York Life Insurance Company: New York Life Insurance Company is an insurer in New York. It is tied to the Federal Reserve System through one person: W. Braddock Hickman, who went from the insurance company into the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland and was its president from 1963 to 1970.
n:Singlife Holdings Private Limited: Singlife Holdings Private Limited is an insurer in Singapore. Dato' Dr. Nirmala Menon, who holds a seat on its board, was appointed an independent non-executive member of the board of directors of Bank Negara Malaysia, Malaysia's central bank, on 16 March 2020, and chairs that board's risk committee. Her earlier jobs include president and chief executive officer of ING Malaysia Berhad, head of South Asia at ING Asia Pacific Limited, and executive vice president at MetLife Asia Pacific Limited.
n:Boatmen's National Bank: Boatmen's National Bank is a bank in St. Louis, in the United States, and it is linked to the Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States, through a person who moved between the two. Darryl R. Francis came from Boatmen's National Bank and commercial banking in Memphis to become president of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, a post he held from 1966 to 1976. He was also chairman of Merchants Bank in Fort Smith. Moving between jobs is not an accusation of wrongdoing.
n:Commonwealth Bank Limited: Commonwealth Bank Limited is a bank in Nassau, in the Bahamas. Its link to the Central Bank of The Bahamas runs through T. Baswell Donaldson, CBE, who was that central bank's first governor and board chairman from 1 June 1974 to May 1980 and afterwards became chairman of Commonwealth Bank, a commercial bank. Who owns the commercial bank is not stated. Taking a job in private banking after public office is a tie, not an allegation of anything improper.
Deloitte Audit s.r.o. is an accounting firm in Slovakia. Its tie to the National Bank of Slovakia is an audit: it checks the central bank's accounts, that is, it goes through the books and reports whether they are accurate. It was named as that bank's external auditor for 2021 under a European Central Bank decision of 7 October 1999 on the external auditors of national central banks, in the version consolidated on 26 October 2021. Auditing a central bank is ordinary paid work, not a finding against anyone.
n:First Interstate Bank of Washington: First Interstate Bank of Washington is a bank in the United States. It is tied to the Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States, through Jeffrey M. Bucher, who sat on the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors, its top decision-making body, from 1972 to 1976. He came to the board from the 1st Interstate Bank of California and went on afterwards to bank boards and chairmanships, among them First Interstate Bank of Washington. The move itself is not an allegation of wrongdoing.
n:ING Malaysia Berhad: ING Malaysia Berhad is an insurer in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Its tie to Bank Negara Malaysia, the country's central bank, is Dato' Dr. Nirmala Menon, appointed to the central bank's board on 16 March 2020 as an independent non-executive member and chair of its board risk committee. Her earlier roles include president and chief executive of ING Malaysia Berhad, head of South Asia at ING Asia Pacific Limited and executive vice president at MetLife Asia Pacific Limited. No years are given for those jobs, and no wrongdoing is reported.
Mazars, druzba za revizijo, d.o.o. is an accounting firm in Slovenia. Its tie to the Bank of Slovenia is an audit: it checks the central bank's accounts, going through the books and reporting whether they are accurate. It holds that role for the years 2024 to 2026, under Council Decision (EU) 2023/2797 on the external auditors of Banka Slovenije. Being the auditor is paid work, not a finding against the bank or the firm.
n:Mortgage and Realty Trust: Mortgage and Realty Trust is an asset manager in Philadelphia, in the United States, meaning it invests money on behalf of others. Its tie to the Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States, is Jeffrey M. Bucher, who worked for the 1st Interstate Bank of California from 1957 to 1972, was appointed to the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors on 5 June 1972 and resigned on 2 January 1976. Afterwards he was a trustee of Mortgage and Realty Trust and held other bank directorships and chairmanships. No ethics finding is recorded.
n:New York Trust Company: New York Trust Company is a bank in New York, in the United States. It is tied to the Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States, through Alfred Hayes, who came from New York Trust Company to be president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York from 1956 to 1975, and then left the Federal Reserve to become chairman of Morgan Stanley International. Nothing improper is reported; the tie is the career path itself.
n:Soleil Securities Corporation: Soleil Securities Corporation is a brokerage in the United States, a firm that buys and sells securities for clients. Its tie to the Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States, is Lyle E. Gramley, who sat on the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors from 1980 to 1985 and afterwards went to the Schwab Washington Research Group and to Soleil Securities Corporation. No wrongdoing is reported; what is recorded is the move from the central bank into private finance.
n:AIA Group Limited: AIA Group Limited is a publicly listed pan-Asian life insurance group based in Hong Kong. It is linked to one central bank, Bank Negara Malaysia, through a person who worked for both. Tan Sri Mohamed Azman Yahya was an independent non-executive director of the insurer from 24 February 2014 to 28 May 2020, and joined Bank Negara Malaysia's Board of Directors on 1 June 2020, four days after leaving.
n:Banknote Printing House, Central Bank: The Banknote Printing House is a state printing works run by the Central Bank of Egypt itself, in the New Administrative Capital outside Cairo, and it prints Egypt's banknotes. It handles the whole job, from designing a note to delivering it to the bank's Cash Centre. Its output covers what Egypt needs at home, with capacity that could also supply other countries in the region, though no capacity figures are given. A West African delegation from the BCEAO toured the plant on 10 March 2025.
n:Dar As-Sikkah: Dar As-Sikkah, in Rabat, is the industrial unit of Morocco's central bank, Bank Al-Maghrib, and it is where the country's money is made: it prints Morocco's banknotes and mints its coins, and it also produces the national passport and other security documents. The bank says it was founded in 1987 and inaugurated by King Hassan II on 5 March 1987. A second banknote production line was added in 1992, it has printed banknotes for other countries since 1995, and its equipment began to be modernised in 2008.
n:Fábrica Nacional de Moneda y Timbre: The Fábrica Nacional de Moneda y Timbre is Spain's state printing works, in Madrid, and it has printed banknotes used in Argentina. Argentina's own state mint, Casa de Moneda, had sent production of the 2,000-peso note out to the Spanish works, and the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic is to receive only a small share of those notes. The same report says Argentina's 20,000-peso notes were imported from China, without naming who made them.
n:Landqart AG: Landqart AG is a firm in Landquart, Switzerland, that makes the material banknotes are printed on rather than the notes themselves. It supplies the National Bank of Kazakhstan: the 20,000 tenge note issued for the 30th anniversary of independence is printed on Landqart's Durasafe composite substrate, the layered sheet the design sits on, and Landqart says it is the second note the bank has issued on that material. The firm describes a partnership with the central bank's own Banknote Factory.
n:Polska Wytwórnia Papierów Wartościowyc: Polska Wytwórnia Papierów Wartościowych, or PWPW, is a firm in Warsaw, Poland, that prints banknotes for the Bank of Guatemala. It signed an agreement with Banco de Guatemala, the country's central bank, on 20 August 2018 to produce 5- and 10-quetzal notes on a printing material containing synthetic fibres, with production due to begin later that year. PWPW's president called it the largest order in the firm's work with the Guatemalan central bank up to then. No contract value is stated.
n:Al-Aiban, Al-Osaimi & Partners of Erns: These are two accounting firms in Kuwait City, Kuwait, which together check the books of the Central Bank of Kuwait and sign off on them. They are named as the auditors of the central bank's accounts for the fiscal year that ended on 31 March 2013, as reported in the central bank's Annual Report 2012/2013. That is the one central bank they are tied to here, and nothing else is recorded about them.
n:Bulgarian National Audit Office: The Bulgarian National Audit Office is a state body in Sofia, Bulgaria, that checks the books of public institutions. It audits the accounts of the Bulgarian National Bank, the country's central bank, and it does so under a continuing duty written into law rather than a contract for particular years; no starting year is stated. That is the one central bank it is tied to, and no case or dispute is recorded about the work.
n:Deloitte Cote d'Ivoire: Deloitte Cote d'Ivoire is a private accounting firm in Abidjan, Cote d'Ivoire. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of West African States, the BCEAO, which issues the shared currency of eight countries and is based in Senegal. Its audit covers the financial year that ended on 31 December 2025, and it signed the bank's financial statements for that year. That is the one central bank it is tied to here.
n:Fábrica de Billetes del Banco de Méxic: This is the Bank of Mexico's own state printing works, which makes the country's banknotes. The central bank prints every denomination itself at two factories, one in Mexico City and one in El Salto, Jalisco. It did not always do so: the first notes it put into circulation, in 1925, were made by the American Bank Note Company of New York, and printing moved to the central bank's own factory in Mexico in 1969. The marker is placed at the country rather than either plant.
n:Louisenthal (Papierfabrik Louisenthal): Louisenthal, also called Papierfabrik Louisenthal, is a firm in Gmund am Tegernsee, Germany, that makes the special paper banknotes are printed on. It says it supplied the security features embedded in the paper of the Bulgarian National Bank's 100-lev note — the thread, the foil and the watermark — though it names no particular paper product. That note became legal tender on 28 December 2018 and won the High Security Printing EMEA award in Malta in March 2019.
n:PricewaterhouseCoopers Limited: PricewaterhouseCoopers Limited is a private accounting firm in Nicosia, Cyprus. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Cyprus, and its approved term covered the financial years 2018 to 2022. Auditors of national central banks in the European Union are approved by a formal decision of the Council of the EU, Council Decision 1999/70/EC, the consolidated version of which dates from 26 October 2021. That is the one central bank it is tied to here.
n:Banco de la República (Imprenta de Bil: The Imprenta de Billetes is the banknote printing works of Banco de la República in Bogota, Colombia. It prints the banknotes of the Bank of the Republic, Colombia's central bank. The bank says it carries out the production, issuance, supply, exchange and destruction of Colombia's banknotes and coins itself, and its site places the printing works under its cash division, with its coin plant at Ibague, Tolima. No location is given for the printing works.
n:Casa de Moneda (Sociedad del Estado, A: Casa de Moneda is Argentina's state mint, in Buenos Aires. It printed 1,000- and 2,000-peso banknotes for the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic under three contracts dated November 2021, September 2022 and February 2023. The central bank then partially cancelled those contracts, and the mint stopped printing banknotes at 10pm on 28 October 2024, with the government announcing that 2,000-peso notes would no longer be printed.
n:Ernst & Young Mongolia Audit LLC: Ernst & Young Mongolia Audit LLC is a firm in Mongolia. It is the external auditor of the Bank of Mongolia, the country's central bank, meaning it is the outside accountant that checks the bank's books: it audited the accounts for the 2020 financial year.
n:Institute for Manufacturing Banknotes: The Institute for Manufacturing Banknotes and Coins at Topcider, in Belgrade, Serbia, prints the banknotes of the National Bank of Serbia. The bank says the Institute makes the banknotes and coins it issues, and also makes products for foreign countries. The Institute was built from 1927 and began operating in December 1929 as the Institute for Manufacturing Banknotes of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, with a mint added in 1937.
n:National Banknote Printing Factory (Vi: The National Banknote Printing Factory, in Hanoi, prints the banknotes of the State Bank of Vietnam, the country's central bank. It is reported to be a one-member limited liability company whose charter capital is held entirely by the state, and to be responsible for printing banknotes, with its board chairman appointed by the Governor of the State Bank and its production plans assigned by the Governor. Nguyen Duc Cuong was appointed chairman for a five-year term, succeeding Le Thai Nam, who had led it since September 2019.
n:SinoPac Financial Holdings Company Lim: SinoPac Financial Holdings Company Limited is a bank based in Taipei, Taiwan. Its chairman, Chen Szu-kuan, who also chairs SinoPac Securities Investment Trust Company Limited, sits at the same time on the board of the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) as a director of its 21st Board of Directors, for a term running from 27 January 2025 to 26 January 2030. Holding both posts is a tie, not a finding of wrongdoing.
n:Banknote Factory of the National Bank: The Banknote Factory of the National Bank of Kazakhstan is the state printing works that makes Kazakhstan's banknotes. The National Bank of Kazakhstan lists it among its subsidiaries and says its main activity is producing banknotes, along with other security printing such as passports, identity documents and payment cards. The factory has released three series of tenge banknotes and eight commemorative or jubilee banknotes. It is tied to one central bank, the National Bank of Kazakhstan, whose money it prints.
n:Central Engraving and Printing Plant: The Central Engraving and Printing Plant is the state printing works in Taiwan that prints banknotes for the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan). That is the only central bank it is tied to. A central bank press release on the NT$200 banknote says that "the new banknotes are printed by China Engraving & Printing Works".
n:Ernst & Young SA: Ernst & Young SA, in Luxembourg, is the outside auditor of the Central Bank of Luxembourg, meaning it checks the central bank's accounts. It is the only central bank it is tied to. Under the European Union decision on the external auditors of national central banks, in its text consolidated on 26 October 2021, the firm was approved to audit those accounts for the financial years 2019 to 2023.
n:Korea Minting and Security Printing Co: The Korea Minting and Security Printing Corporation, known as KOMSCO, is based in Daejeon, South Korea, and prints the banknotes of the Bank of Korea, the one central bank it is tied to. The Korea Times describes KOMSCO as the state-run mint and "the country's sole manufacturer of banknotes and coins", and says it keeps a close partnership with the Bank of Korea.
n:Oberthur Fiduciaire AD: Oberthur Fiduciaire AD prints the banknotes of the Bulgarian National Bank, the one central bank it is tied to. Louisenthal states that Oberthur Fiduciaire AD has handled Bulgarian National Bank banknote production since 2014. Nothing else is reported about it.
n:SinoPac Securities Investment Trust Co: SinoPac Securities Investment Trust Company Limited, in Taipei, manages money for investors and is tied to one central bank through a shared person. Chen Szu-kuan (陳思寬) is a director of the 21st Board of Directors of the Central Bank of the Republic of China, for a term running from 27 January 2025 to 26 January 2030, while serving as chairman of SinoPac Financial Holdings Company Limited and chairman of SinoPac Securities Investment Trust Company Limited. Holding both roles at once is a tie, not a finding of wrongdoing.
n:BDO Austria GmbH Wirtschaftsprufungs-: BDO Austria GmbH Wirtschaftsprufungs- und Steuerberatungsgesellschaft is an accounting firm in Austria. It is the outside auditor of the Oesterreichische Nationalbank, Austria's central bank, meaning it checks the bank's accounts from outside the institution. Its approved term runs from 2023 to 2027, set under the European Union Council decision that names the external auditors of national central banks, in the version of 27 June 2024.
n:Banknote Paper Mill (Malyn): The Banknote Paper Mill at Malyn, in Ukraine, makes the paper that Ukraine's hryvnia banknotes are printed on, supplying the National Bank of Ukraine. The bank's own account of the currency, given by Vasyl Ishchenko, places the paper's making at Malyn and describes the notes as carrying sophisticated security features and lasting well in circulation.
n:Crown Agents Investment Management: Crown Agents Investment Management is a money manager based in London. It runs part of the foreign currency savings of the Central Bank of Seychelles: an externally managed portfolio of bonds and similar fixed income holdings, divided evenly between US dollars and Chinese renminbi. The job began in 2014 with 25.0 million US dollars, and a further 25.0 million US dollars was added in April 2022. This is actual management of the bank's assets, not only advice.
Ernst & Young d.o.o. is an accounting firm in Croatia. It is the outside auditor of the Croatian National Bank, the body that checks the central bank's accounts from outside it, for the financial years 2025 to 2027. The appointment was made by the Council of the European Union, which amended its 1999 decision naming the external auditors of national central banks to record it.
n:Hungarian Banknote Printing Company: The Hungarian Banknote Printing Company, in Budapest, prints the forint notes that Hungarians carry. The Magyar Nemzeti Bank, Hungary's central bank, says the printer is an enterprise it owns outright, so the bank that issues the money also owns the works that makes it.
n:Mazars Niger: Mazars Niger is an accounting firm in Niger. It was selected to audit the accounts of the Central Bank of West African States, known by its French initials BCEAO, which issues the shared currency of a group of West African countries. Its term covers the financial years 2024 to 2029, and the selection was announced by the BCEAO itself.
n:Perum Peruri: Perum Peruri, in Jakarta, is described as Indonesia's state banknote printing firm. Bank Indonesia, the central bank, gave it the job of printing the country's new banknotes, and the work was done at Peruri's plant at Karawang in West Java. Peruri denied that a private firm in Central Java had printed any of the notes.
n:South African Bank Note Company: The South African Bank Note Company, formally the South African Bank Note Company (RF) Proprietary Limited, is in Pretoria and prints South Africa's banknotes. The South African Reserve Bank, the country's central bank, says the printer is one of its own subsidiaries, so the bank that issues the money owns the company that produces it.
Valora S.A., at Carregado in Portugal, is the banknote printer owned by the Banco de Portugal, and it prints notes for that central bank. A Banque de France press release names it as the bank's printer. It is the only central bank tied to the firm.
n:BNP Paribas Asset Management: BNP Paribas Asset Management is a firm based in Paris, France. Chile's Ministry of Finance says it is the sole outside manager of the US agency mortgage-backed securities portfolio of Chile's sovereign wealth funds, the state's savings pots, and that the Banco Central de Chile runs the selection of outside managers, handles the sovereign fixed income share of the funds itself, and supervises outside managers holding instruments that qualify for the country's international reserves. This is management of money, not advice.
n:Mellon Investments Corporation: Mellon Investments Corporation is a firm based in Boston, United States. Chile's Ministry of Finance says it manages part of the share portfolio of Chile's sovereign wealth funds, the state's savings pots. The Banco Central de Chile runs the process that picks these outside managers and supervises those holding instruments that qualify for the country's international reserves. Mellon is handling money, not giving advice.
n:Banknote Printing and Minting Works of: The Banknote Printing and Minting Works of the National Bank of Ukraine is a state printing works in Kyiv. It prints the hryvnia, Ukraine's banknotes, and the National Bank of Ukraine says the works is part of the bank itself. So the country's cash is made in-house rather than ordered from an outside printer.
n:De La Rue Lanka Currency and Security: De La Rue Lanka Currency and Security Print (Pvt) Ltd is a firm at Biyagama, Sri Lanka. The Central Bank of Sri Lanka says in its own question-and-answer page on currency that this company prints the country's currency notes at Biyagama. The job of making a country's cash therefore sits with a company outside the central bank.
Grant Thornton Audit, s.r.o. is a firm in Slovakia. It checks the books of the National Bank of Slovakia as that bank's outside auditor, an appointment approved for the financial years 2024 to 2027 under the European Union decision that names the external auditors of the national central banks, in the version of 27 June 2024.
n:Imprenta de Billetes S.A. (IMBISA): Imprenta de Billetes S.A., known as IMBISA, is a state printing works in Madrid, Spain, 80 per cent owned by the Banco de España. It prints the euro banknotes allotted to Spain, which the Banco de España puts at roughly 12 per cent of all euro banknote production, so the Spanish central bank owns most of the plant that makes a sizeable share of the shared currency's cash.
n:PriceWaterhouseCoopers & Associados -: PriceWaterhouseCoopers & Associados - Sociedade de Revisores Oficiais de Contas Lda is a firm in Portugal. It checks the books of the Bank of Portugal as that bank's outside auditor, an appointment approved for the financial years 2022 to 2026 under the European Union decision naming the external auditors of the national central banks, in the version of 27 June 2024.
n:Tribunal de Cuentas: The Tribunal de Cuentas is a state body in Montevideo, Uruguay. It checks the books of the Central Bank of Uruguay. That duty is not a contract the bank can end but a standing requirement written into the bank's founding law, Ley 16.696 of 1995, which remains in force, so the auditing is done by the state itself rather than by a hired accounting firm.
n:World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory a: The Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership, RAMP, is run by the World Bank's treasury department in Washington, DC, and offers member central banks three things: advice, training for senior staff, and the actual handling of money. Fourteen central banks are tied to it, and what each gets differs. Guatemala, Trinidad and Tobago, Cambodia and Bulgaria are listed only as members, Bulgaria also co-hosting a RAMP forum. Ecuador, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Cape Verde, Liberia, Libya and Zimbabwe signed up for advice, technical assistance or capacity building. Armenia rejoined for advice and training, after membership from 2006 to 2014. Paraguay joined in 2017 and used RAMP advice to rewrite its own investment policy, still running its reserves itself. Only in Seychelles does RAMP run money: a portfolio of international reserves first funded with 100 million US dollars in 2019 and still held at the end of 2025.
n:Baker Tilly Klitou and Partners Limite: Baker Tilly Klitou and Partners Limited is a private firm in Cyprus. It is the external auditor of the Central Bank of Cyprus, meaning the outside accountants who check the bank's books and sign off on its accounts. Its approved term runs from 2023 to 2027, set out in a Council of the European Union decision amending Decision 1999/70/EC on the external auditors of national central banks, document 11852/24. That is the only central bank tied to the firm.
n:Contraloria General de la Republica: The Contraloria General de la Republica is a state body in San Jose, Costa Rica. It audits the accounts of two central banks, meaning it checks their books from outside the banks themselves. It audits the Central Bank of Costa Rica under a 1995 law that is still in force, the Ley Organica del Banco Central de Costa Rica, Ley No. 7558. It also audits the Central Bank of Bolivia, again under a 1995 law in force, Ley No. 1670, the law of the Central Bank of Bolivia.
n:Deloitte Audit Ltd: Deloitte Audit Ltd is a private firm in Malta. It is the external auditor of the Central Bank of Malta, the outside accountants who check the bank's books and sign off on its accounts, under an approved term covering 2023 to 2027. That term was set by Council Decision (EU) 2023/1196 of 16 June 2023, published in the Official Journal of the European Union. It is the only central bank tied to the firm.
n:Grant Thornton Ireland: Grant Thornton Ireland is a private firm in Ireland. It is the external auditor of the Central Bank of Ireland, meaning the outside accountants who check the bank's books rather than bank staff doing it themselves. Its approved term covers 2023 to 2027, recorded in the consolidated text of Council Decision 1999/70/EC on the external auditors of national central banks, in the version of 27 June 2024. That is the only central bank tied to the firm.
KPMG Audit S.a r.l. is a private firm in Luxembourg. It is the external auditor of the Central Bank of Luxembourg, the outside accountants who check the bank's books and sign off on its accounts. Its approved term runs from 2024 to 2028, set by Council Decision (EU) 2024/864 of 12 March 2024, published in the Official Journal of the European Union. It is the only central bank tied to the firm.
n:Oesterreichische Banknoten- und Sicher: Oesterreichische Banknoten- und Sicherheitsdruck GmbH, or OeBS, is a state printing works in Vienna, Austria. It prints the banknotes for the Oesterreichische Nationalbank, Austria's central bank, which owns it. A joint press release from the Banque de France names OeBS as one of three printers owned by central banks that are strengthening their cooperation on banknote production. Austria's central bank is the only one tied to it.
n:Security Printing Corporation (Banglad: The Security Printing Corporation (Bangladesh) Ltd is a state printing works in Gazipur, Bangladesh. It prints the banknotes for Bangladesh Bank, the country's central bank. The Business Standard reports that Bangladesh's taka notes are printed there, at a site known locally as Takshal that covers about 66 acres and has been in operation since 1989. Bangladesh Bank is the only central bank tied to it.
n:UAB ROSK Consulting: UAB ROSK Consulting is a private firm in Lithuania. It is the external auditor of the Bank of Lithuania, meaning the outside accountants who check the bank's books, under an approved term covering 2022 to 2024. That term is set out in the consolidated text of Council Decision 1999/70/EC on the external auditors of national central banks, in the version of 27 June 2024. It is the only central bank tied to the firm.
Baker Tilly Nicaragua, S.A. is a private firm based in Managua, Nicaragua. It acts as the outside auditor of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, meaning it checks the bank's books from outside the bank and reports on whether the figures hold up. Its work appears in the central bank's financial statements for 2024, published by the Banco Central de Nicaragua.
n:Corte de Cuentas de la Republica: The Corte de Cuentas de la Republica is a state body in San Salvador, El Salvador. It audits the accounts of the Central Reserve Bank of El Salvador, which means checking the bank's books from outside and reporting on them. This is not a contract with an end date but a duty written into the law that governs the central bank, and that law is in force.
n:Diósgyőr Papermill: The Diósgyőr Papermill in Miskolc, Hungary, is a state printing works and a wholly owned subsidiary of the Hungarian Banknote Printing Company. It does not print money itself; it makes the special paper the notes are printed on. The Magyar Nemzeti Bank, Hungary's central bank, states that the paper for forint banknotes is made at this mill.
n:Horwath Central America: Horwath Central America is a private firm in Honduras. It is the outside auditor of the Central Bank of Honduras, checking the bank's books and reporting on them rather than keeping them. It audited the central bank's financial statements as at 31 December 2023, which were published through Honduras's single transparency portal.
n:KPMG Bedrijfsrevisoren / KPMG Reviseur: KPMG Bedrijfsrevisoren / KPMG Reviseurs d'Entreprises BV/SRL is a private firm in Belgium. It audits the accounts of the National Bank of Belgium, that is, it checks the bank's books from outside and reports on them. The appointment covers the years 2023 to 2028 and is recorded in a Council decision of the European Union on the outside auditors of national central banks.
n:Orell Füssli Security Printing Ltd: Orell Füssli Security Printing Ltd is a private firm in Zurich, Switzerland. It prints banknotes for the Swiss National Bank, Switzerland's central bank, which states that this company prints the ninth series of Swiss franc notes. So the notes the central bank issues are physically made by a separate company.
n:Security Printing and Minting Organiza: The Security Printing and Minting Organization, in Tehran, is a state printing works and has been a subsidiary of the Central Bank of Iran since 1962. It handles the design, production and destruction of Iran's banknotes and coins. Until 1982 Iran's banknotes were printed abroad; since then they have come from this organization.
n:UBS Asset Management: UBS Asset Management is a private firm based in Zurich, Switzerland, and it handles money for two central banks. For the Central Bank of Seychelles it runs a money market fund holding part of the country's reserves, funded with 10.0 million US dollars in 2017 and still held at the end of 2025, and it has invited bank staff to its annual reserves management seminar. For Chile, UBS Asset Management Inc manages part of the corporate bond portfolio and part of the equity portfolio of the sovereign wealth funds, with the Banco Central de Chile selecting and supervising the outside managers.
n:\"Ernst&Young Montenegro\" Ltd Podgori: "Ernst&Young Montenegro" Ltd Podgorica is a firm based in Podgorica, Montenegro. It is tied to one central bank: it audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Montenegro, meaning it checks from outside that the bank's books are accurate. Its most recent audit covered the 2025 accounts, as recorded in the central bank's summary of its audit committee report for that year.
n:Davlat Belgisi: Davlat Belgisi is a state printing operation in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, and it prints the banknotes of the Central Bank of Uzbekistan. The central bank lists it among its own subordinate organisations, as a state production association set up as a limited liability company under the bank and made up of the Tashkent Printing Factory, the Tashkent Paper Factory and the Tashkent Mint. Its core business is given as making banknote and other security papers, banknotes and passports.
n:Northern Trust: Northern Trust is a firm based in Chicago, United States, with ties to two central banks. For the Bank of Botswana it reports on how investments have performed and why, and trains bank staff on benchmarks and bond investing. For the Bank of Uganda it does compliance, performance and risk analysis, helped build a dashboard for watching the bank's outside asset managers, and supported a redesign of how the bank plans its investments. In both cases Central Banking's award profile describes services, training and advice, not management of the money.
n:State Street Global Advisors: State Street Global Advisors is a firm based in Boston, United States, and it manages money for one central bank. Central Banking's award profile reports that it holds a mandate to invest shares for the Czech National Bank, raised to 7.5 billion US dollars, and that the Czech bank's executive director of risk management says it has kept that mandate with the firm since 2007. The firm also gives the bank its views when it weighs alternatives to its current approach to reserves.
n:Amundi: Amundi is a firm based in Paris, France, tied to three central banks. In 2023 the Bank of the Republic (Colombia) chose it as one of eight outside managers, and it runs an active fixed income programme covering 1.7 billion US dollars of Treasuries, mortgage-backed securities and G10 currencies. With the Latin American Reserve Fund it also built a fixed-income exchange-traded fund for central banks, a pooled product rather than a mandate to run reserves; the Central Bank of Uruguay and the Bank of Mexico are named as clients.
n:Ernst & Young Statutory Auditors, Bran: Ernst & Young Statutory Auditors, Branch in Albania is a firm based in Tirana, Albania. It is tied to one central bank: it audits the accounts of the Bank of Albania, meaning it checks the bank's books from outside and signs off on them. The Bank of Albania's own financial statements record it as the auditor for 2023.
n:Orell Fuessli: Orell Fuessli is a firm based in Zurich, Switzerland, tied to one central bank. It prints banknotes for the Central Bank of Nicaragua. LexLatin reported on 27 March 2024 that the firm had been partially awarded a tender to print and supply the bank's notes, meaning it took part of the work rather than all of it. No value or quantity is given.
n:Sudanese Company for Currency Printing: The Sudanese Company for Currency Printing is a printing works in Khartoum, Sudan, tied to one central bank. It prints banknotes for the Central Bank of Sudan. Dabanga reported in February 2019 that Sudan's new 200-pound note went into production there, at a domestic press the prime minister visited that week. Who owns the company is not stated.
n:BDO Assurance NV: BDO Assurance NV is a firm in Suriname that audits accounts, meaning it checks another organisation's books and says whether the figures are right. One central bank is tied to it: it audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Suriname. The audit on record covers that bank's 2020 accounts, published in its annual financial statements for that year.
n:KPMG Moldova SRL: KPMG Moldova SRL is a firm in Moldova that audits accounts, meaning it examines another organisation's books and states whether the figures are right. One central bank is tied to it: it audits the accounts of the National Bank of Moldova. The audits on record cover 2024 and 2023, as set out in that bank's financial statements for 2024.
n:Oumolat Security Printing: Oumolat Security Printing is a banknote printer in Abu Dhabi, in the United Arab Emirates. Currency News reported on 31 March 2025 that the Central Bank of the UAE had issued a new 100 dirham polymer banknote printed by Oumolat. A 2023 profile in the same publication says the firm began operations in 2016, was owned and started by the Emirates Investment Authority, and was then transferred to the Central Bank of the UAE, so the bank whose money it prints is also its owner.
n:West African Monetary Institute: The West African Monetary Institute is an international body in Accra, Ghana. It manages a shared fund that one central bank, the Bank of Sierra Leone, pays into. That bank's audited financial statements for 2024 list its contribution to the Stabilization and Cooperation Fund, 63.59 million leones, among its foreign assets, and say the institute manages the fund, with the balance held at the Bank of Ghana. What it runs is the pooled fund, not the central bank's own reserves.
n:DWS Group: DWS Group is a firm based in Frankfurt, Germany. It is one of the outside managers that invest part of the foreign reserves of the Bank of Papua New Guinea on the bank's behalf, measured against the FTSE Russell Government Bond Index 1-3 Years USD Hedged. The bank's Annual Report 2024 says DWS and BlackRock delivered the strongest results for the year, while Pictet recorded the weakest relative performance.
n:Pictet Asset Management: Pictet Asset Management is a firm based in Geneva, Switzerland. It is one of the outside managers that invest part of the foreign reserves of the Bank of Papua New Guinea on the bank's behalf, measured against the FTSE Russell Government Bond Index 1-3 Years USD Hedged. In the bank's Annual Report 2024, Pictet recorded the weakest relative performance for the year, while DWS and BlackRock delivered the strongest results.
n:Latin American Reserve Fund (FLAR): The Latin American Reserve Fund, known as FLAR, is an international body based in Bogota, Colombia. Central Banking's announcement of its 2026 awards gave the partner initiative award to Amundi and FLAR for a fixed-income exchange-traded fund they developed together for central banks, built around environmental, social and governance standards, and named the Central Bank of Uruguay and the Bank of Mexico among the clients. This is a fund those banks put money into, not a mandate to manage their reserves.
n:World Bank Reserves Advisory and Manag: The Reserves Advisory and Management Partnership, or RAMP, is run by the World Bank from Washington, D.C., in the United States. The Central Bank of Somalia says it joined RAMP at the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, gaining technical support and advisory services. The National Bank of Georgia describes a RAMP mission helping update its reserves investment strategy and gold policy, with its governor thanking the team for technical assistance. In both cases RAMP advises; it does not invest the money itself.
n:Statni tiskarna cenin: Statni tiskarna cenin is a state printing works in Prague, Czechia, tied to one central bank, the Czech National Bank. It printed some of that bank's banknotes: the bank says the reverse of its commemorative note marking the establishment of the Czechoslovak currency carries, in tiny letters near the lower edge, the inscription "STATNI TISKARNA CENIN, STATNI PODNIK, PRAHA". No printing date is given; the note was issued in 2022 and entered circulation on 30 March 2022. Who prints the bank's circulating notes is not stated.
n:Auditor General of the Cayman Islands: The Auditor General of the Cayman Islands, Patrick O. Smith, a certified public accountant and certified fraud examiner, heads the government audit office there. The office is tied to one central bank: it audits the accounts of the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority, and its audit for 2025 appears in that authority's annual report, tabled in the Cayman Islands Parliament.
n:Moteane, Quashie & Associates and Sizw: Moteane, Quashie & Associates and SizweNtsalubaGobodo Grant Thornton Inc. are accounting firms working together from Maseru, Lesotho. They are tied to one central bank: they audit the accounts of the Central Bank of Lesotho, and signed its annual financial statements for the year ended 2023.
n:Deloitte Namibia and Grand Namibia: Deloitte Namibia and Grand Namibia are accounting firms based in Windhoek, Namibia. They are tied to one central bank: they are the external auditors of the Bank of Namibia and audit its accounts.
n:Hong Kong Note Printing Limited: Hong Kong Note Printing Limited is a firm in Hong Kong that prints banknotes. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's page on Hong Kong notes says the notes issued by the note-issuing banks are printed in Hong Kong by the company. The same page says the government keeps management control and a majority stake in it, with the chief executive of the Monetary Authority as the company's chairman. That is the one central bank it is tied to.
n:Bureau of Engraving and Printing: The Bureau of Engraving and Printing is a United States government works that prints banknotes for the Federal Reserve System, the country's central bank. Its own About page says it prints billions of dollars each year, in notes called Federal Reserve notes. The page gives no location for the agency, so it is marked at the country rather than at the office. That is the one central bank it is tied to.
n:Auditor-General of Papua New Guinea (A: The Auditor-General of Papua New Guinea, also called the Auditor General's Office, is based in Port Moresby. It audits the accounts of the Bank of Papua New Guinea, the country's central bank, meaning it checks the bank's books from outside. The tie is recorded for 2024, from the central bank's annual report for that year. That is the one central bank it is tied to.
n:Auditor General (of Nepal): The Auditor General of Nepal, based in Kathmandu, audits the accounts of Nepal Rastra Bank, the country's central bank: it checks the bank's books from outside the bank. The duty comes from section 92 of the Nepal Rastra Bank Act, dated 2002 in the numbering used there. That is the one central bank it is tied to.
n:World Bank Treasury: The World Bank Treasury is based in Washington, D.C., in the United States, and one central bank is tied to it. Financial Afrik reports that the governor of the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie, Sid'Ahmed Ould Raiss, and the World Bank's vice-president and treasurer Madelyn Antoncic signed a cooperation agreement on foreign exchange reserve management at the IMF-World Bank spring meetings, under which the treasury department would train reserve staff, organise the relevant structures and eventually set up a trading room. That is technical assistance, not management of the money itself.
n:Auditor General of Seychelles, audit r: The Auditor General of Seychelles, in Victoria, Seychelles, audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Seychelles, the one central bank tied to it, with the audit review carried out by Grant Thornton Audit and Accounting Limited in Abu Dhabi. Auditing means checking the bank's books and reporting whether they give an accurate picture. The audit covers 2025 and appears in the central bank's annual report for that year, which was tabled in the National Assembly.
n:PricewaterhouseCoopers Eastern Caribbe: PricewaterhouseCoopers Eastern Caribbean is an accounting firm at Bird Rock in Basseterre, St. Kitts & Nevis. It audits the accounts of the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, the one central bank tied to it, which means it checks the bank's books and reports whether they give an accurate picture. The audit covers 2025 and is published with the central bank's financial statements as an independent auditors' report.
n:Baker Tilly SL, Chartered Accountants: Baker Tilly SL, Chartered Accountants is an accounting firm in Freetown, Sierra Leone. It audits the accounts of the Bank of Sierra Leone, the one central bank tied to it, which means it checks the bank's books and reports whether they give an accurate picture. The audit covers 2024 and appears in the bank's published financial statements for that year.
n:DELOITTE COTE D'IVOIRE (titulaire), MA: These are two accounting firms in Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire, appointed together as a pair: Deloitte Côte d'Ivoire is the titulaire, the firm that actually does the audit, and Mazars Côte d'Ivoire the suppléant, the stand-in held in reserve. They audit the accounts of the Côte d'Ivoire arm of the Central Bank of West African States, the shared central bank known as the BCEAO, under a 2023 selection whose results the bank published in Dakar on 12 January 2024.
n:MAZARS SENEGAL (titulaire), FICAO GRAN: These are two accounting firms appointed together as a pair, based in Dakar, Senegal: Mazars Senegal is the titulaire, the firm that actually does the audit, and FICAO Grant Thornton Togo the suppléant, the stand-in held in reserve. They audit the accounts of the Senegal arm of the Central Bank of West African States, the shared central bank known as the BCEAO, under a 2023 selection whose results the bank published in Dakar on 12 January 2024.
n:Banque d'Algerie banknote printing wor: This is the Bank of Algeria's own banknote printing operation, placed in Algiers, Algeria, and it prints the banknotes of the Bank of Algeria. The news outlet Tunisie Numérique lists Algeria among the Arab countries that print their money at home, writing that the Bank of Algeria prints its notes locally. The article names no separate printing company and gives no location or print volumes for the works.
n:Ernst & Young Audit & Associados – SRO: This is the Portuguese audit arm of Ernst & Young, one of the large international accounting networks, based in Lisbon, Portugal. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Timor-Leste, and signed off that bank's accounts for 2023, which appear in the bank's annual report for that year. It is tied to that one central bank.
n:KPMG, a Fiji partnership, Chartered Ac: This is the Fiji partnership of KPMG, one of the large international accounting networks, based in Suva and made up of chartered accountants. It audits the accounts of the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu, the central bank of neighbouring Vanuatu, and signed that bank's financial statements for 2019. It is tied to that one central bank.
n:Mazars Fivoarana: This is an accounting firm in Antananarivo, Madagascar, part of the Mazars network. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of the Comoros, the central bank of the neighbouring Comoros islands, and produced the auditors' report on that bank's 2024 accounts. It is tied to that one central bank.
n:Groupement PKF BAGE SARL et MAZARS BEN: This is a pair of accounting firms based in Lomé, Togo, appointed together to audit a central bank: PKF BAGE SARL with Mazars Benin does the work as the appointed auditor, the titulaire, and Deloitte Togo stands in as the suppléant. They audit the 2023 accounts of the Togo arm of the Central Bank of West African States, the BCEAO. The appointment was published by the bank in Dakar on 12 January 2024, in the results of its calls for proposals for outside auditors.
n:Saudi Central Bank Printing Works: The Saudi Central Bank Printing Works is a state printing operation in Saudi Arabia; the exact location of the office is not given. It prints the banknotes of the Saudi Central Bank. Tunisie Numérique lists Saudi Arabia among the Arab countries that print their money at home, names the printing works, and describes this as giving the kingdom strong monetary sovereignty. The article gives no founding date, no location and no production figures.
n:Deloitte Cote d'Ivoire (titulaire), Ma: Two accounting firms appointed together to audit a central bank, based in Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire: Deloitte Côte d'Ivoire does the audit as the appointed firm, the titulaire, and Mazars Senegal is the stand-in, the suppléant. They audit the accounts of the Central Bank of West African States, the BCEAO, for 2023 and for 2024 to 2029. The appointment was published by the bank in Dakar on 12 January 2024, in the results of its calls for proposals for outside auditors.
n:Ernst & Young Ford Rhodes Sidat Hyder,: Ernst & Young Ford Rhodes Sidat Hyder, Chartered Accountants, is an accounting firm in Kabul, Afghanistan. It audits the accounts of Da Afghanistan Bank, the country's central bank. Its name appears on the bank's financial statements signed on 21 December 2018.
KPMG S.A. is an accounting firm based at Paris la Défense in France; the marker sits on the country rather than the exact office. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of the Republic of Guinea, and its name appears on that bank's 2023 report drawn up under international financial reporting standards.
n:Groupement PKF BAGE SARL et CROWE TG I: This is a pair of audit firms based in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, appointed together in 2023 to check the accounts of the Burkina Faso arm of the Central Bank of West African States. Such appointments come in pairs: the titulaire, here the grouping of PKF BAGE SARL and Crowe TG ICAAF, does the audit, and the suppleant, Deloitte Cote d'Ivoire, is the stand-in. The central bank published the selection results in Dakar on 12 January 2024.
n:MAZARS SENEGAL (titulaire), GRANT THOR: These are two audit firms in Dakar, Senegal, appointed together in 2023 to check the accounts of the Guinea-Bissau arm of the Central Bank of West African States. The appointment is a pair: the titulaire, Mazars Senegal, does the audit, and the suppleant, Grant Thornton Senegal, is the stand-in. The central bank published the selection results in Dakar on 12 January 2024.
n:DELOITTE BENIN (titulaire), MAZARS BEN: These are two audit firms in Cotonou, Benin, appointed together in 2023 to check the accounts of the Benin arm of the Central Bank of West African States. They were picked as a pair: the titulaire, Deloitte Benin, does the audit, and the suppleant, Mazars Benin, is the stand-in. The central bank published the selection results in Dakar on 12 January 2024.
n:KRESTON AUDIT SERVICES ECUADOR CIA. LT: Kreston Audit Services Ecuador Cia. Ltda. is an audit firm in Ecuador; the map places its marker on the country rather than the exact office. It audited the accounts of the Central Bank of Ecuador for 2021. A resolution numbered JPRM-2022-016-G approved the bank's audited financial statements as at 31 December 2021.
n:Deloitte & Touche, Certified Public Ac: Deloitte & Touche, certified public accountants, is based in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. It is tied to one central bank on this map: it audited the accounts of the Central Bank of Somalia for 2024, and is named as the auditor in that bank's annual report for the year.
n:Board of Supreme Audit: The Board of Supreme Audit is Iraq's state audit body; the map places its marker on the country rather than the exact office. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Iraq, a role set out in the central bank law issued as Coalition Provisional Authority Order Number 56 in 2004.
n:GRANT THORNTON SENEGAL (titulaire), Gr: A pair of accounting firms in Dakar, Senegal, appointed together: Grant Thornton Senegal as titulaire, the firm that does the audit, and a grouping of PKF BAGE SARL and Crowe TG ICAAF as suppléant, the stand-in. The pair audits the accounts of the Central Bank of West African States, the BCEAO, in Mali, for 2023, under the bank's notice of results of its calls for proposals, published in Dakar on 12 January 2024.
n:Deloitte & Touche (Chartered Accountan: Two accounting firms working together, Deloitte & Touche, chartered accountants in Accra, and Baker Tilly Liberia, certified public accountants in Monrovia, with the marker placed at the country rather than an exact office. They audit the accounts of the Central Bank of Liberia. The work covers 2024 and appears in that bank's management letter, the private letter auditors send a client about what they found, signed on 19 May 2025.
n:Central Bank of Jordan national bankno: A state printing works in Amman, Jordan, that prints banknotes for the Central Bank of Jordan. Tunisie Numerique lists Jordan among the Arab countries that print their banknotes domestically, saying the Central Bank of Jordan has a national printing works for notes. The article gives the facility no separate corporate name, and states nothing about its size or output.
n:Auditor General's Office: The Auditor General's Office in Honiara is the Solomon Islands' own public auditor. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Solomon Islands, work listed for 2019 among that office's financial audits of statutory authorities, the bodies set up by law that it is required to audit.
n:BDO CHARTERED ACCOUNTANTS: BDO Chartered Accountants is an accounting firm in Apia, Samoa. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Samoa, signing off that bank's financial statements for the year ended 30 June 2025, so the figures the central bank publishes for that year carry this firm's name.
n:Bank of Canada: The Bank of Canada is Canada's central bank, in Ottawa, and two other central banks keep gold in its vaults. Sveriges Riksbank's notice of 28 October 2013, listing where its 125.7 tonnes of gold are stored, puts 33.2 tonnes, 26.4 per cent, at the Bank of Canada. The Swiss National Bank says roughly 10 per cent of its gold is stored there, with about 70 per cent in Switzerland and some 20 per cent at the Bank of England. Both are custody of gold, not management of anyone's money.
n:Oesterreichische Nationalbank: The Oesterreichische Nationalbank is Austria's central bank, in Vienna. It shares the management of some reserves with Latvia's central bank, Latvijas Banka. Latvijas Banka's 2024 annual report says that together with the Oesterreichische Nationalbank it manages their share in Japanese yen, describing this as a shared arrangement for the European Central Bank's foreign reserve assets allocated to the two national central banks. No split between them is given.
n:Sveriges Riksbank: Sveriges Riksbank is Sweden's central bank, in Stockholm. One other central bank keeps gold with it. A Bank of Finland press release of 30 October 2013, setting out where its gold reserves are held in custody, puts 20 per cent of them in Sweden, at the Riksbank. That is storage of the gold: the Riksbank holds it, and does not manage Finland's money.
n:KPMG Armenia LLC: KPMG Armenia LLC is an accounting firm based in Yerevan, Armenia. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Armenia, meaning it checks the bank's books from outside, and its work covers the bank's 2022 annual consolidated financial statements. That is the one central bank it is tied to.
n:Swiss National Bank: The Swiss National Bank is Switzerland's central bank, based in Bern. Two other central banks store gold with it, which is custody rather than management of their money. The Bank of Finland said on 30 October 2013 that 7 per cent of its gold reserves were held in custody in Switzerland, at the Swiss National Bank. Sveriges Riksbank, Sweden's central bank, said on 28 October 2013 that of its 125.7 tonnes of gold, 2.8 tonnes, or 2.2 per cent, were stored at the Swiss National Bank.
n:Standard Chartered Bank: Standard Chartered Bank is a bank based in London. It stores gold for Bangladesh Bank, the central bank of Bangladesh: reporting of 8 September 2026 on where those reserves sit said that as of June Standard Chartered held 92,739 troy ounces of Bangladesh Bank's gold, worth around 45.66 billion taka, in the United Kingdom. That is custody of a reserve asset, not management of the bank's money.
n:Castillo Sanchez & Burrell, LLP, Chart: Castillo Sanchez & Burrell, LLP, Chartered Accountants is a firm of chartered accountants in Belize. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Belize, the country's central bank, and its work appears in the financial statements section of that bank's annual report for 2013. No other tie to a central bank is listed.
n:KPMG Audit SRL: KPMG Audit SRL is an accounting firm based in Bucharest, Romania. It audits the accounts of the National Bank of Romania, Romania's central bank, and did so for that bank's 2019 annual report. No other central bank is tied to it.
