n:US Federal Reserve: The US Federal Reserve, the central bank of the United States, is based in Washington, D.C. One central bank is tied to it here: it stores gold belonging to the Bank of Ghana. A report of 30 September 2021, drawing on the Bank of Ghana's 2020 annual report and financial statements, said that bank's gold held with “the Central Bank of England and US Federal Reserve” came to 2.05 billion Ghanaian cedis between the two, which the source does not split; no particular Reserve Bank is named. This is storage of gold, not management of money.
n:Banque de France: The Banque de France is France's central bank, based in Paris. One central bank is tied to it here: it stores gold belonging to the Deutsche Bundesbank, Germany's central bank. In a press release of 27 January 2016 the Bundesbank listed where its gold reserves sat as at 31 December 2015, and 196.4 tonnes, 5.8 per cent of its 3,381.0-tonne total, were at the Banque de France in Paris. That is storage of gold, not management of the Bundesbank's money.
n:KPMG Audit Azerbaijan LLC: KPMG Audit Azerbaijan LLC is an accounting firm based in Baku, Azerbaijan. It audits the accounts of one central bank, the Central Bank of the Republic of Azerbaijan, checking and reporting on its financial statements; the work recorded here is that bank's 2025 consolidated financial statements and independent auditors' report.
n:Gaveglio Aparicio y Asociados Sociedad: Gaveglio Aparicio y Asociados Sociedad Civil de Responsabilidad Limitada is an accounting firm in Lima, Peru, and a member firm of PricewaterhouseCoopers International Limited. It is tied to one central bank: it audits the accounts of the Central Reserve Bank of Peru, checking and reporting on its financial statements. Its report on the 2024 accounts appears as the independent auditors' chapter of that bank's annual report for the year.
Arevalo Perez, Iralda y Asociados, S. C. is an accounting firm in Guatemala City, Guatemala, and a member firm of PKF International Limited. It is tied to one central bank: it audits the accounts of the Bank of Guatemala, meaning it checks and reports on that bank's financial statements. Its work covers the Bank of Guatemala's financial statements for 2025.
n:Royal Canadian Mint: The Royal Canadian Mint is a state body in Ottawa, Canada. It is tied to one central bank: it holds gold reserves belonging to De Nederlandsche Bank, the Dutch central bank, whose own page on its gold says "another 18.5% at the Royal Canadian Mint in Ottawa". This is storage of gold, not management of money or investments; the gold remains the Dutch bank's.
n:Banca d'Italia: Banca d'Italia is Italy's central bank, based in Rome. The one tie recorded for it is to itself: it stores its own gold. Its gold-reserves page says the metal is kept in the vaults of the Bank of Italy and of major central banks, and that the Italian-held share, 1,100 tonnes or 44.86 per cent of the 2,452-tonne stock, sits in the security rooms at Via Nazionale. That is storage, not management of the holding. The shares in the United Kingdom, Switzerland and the United States are given by country, with no institution named.
n:Czech National Bank: The Czech National Bank is Czechia's central bank, based in Prague. The one tie recorded for it is to itself: it stores part of its own gold. Its page on its gold says some of the metal is kept at its headquarters in Prague, in what it calls the bank's high security vault, mostly for making the bank's own gold coins. That is storage, not management of the holding. The page says most of the reserve is held in London but does not name the London institution.
n:PKF Gambia and PKF Nigeria: PKF Gambia and PKF Nigeria is an accountancy firm based in Bijilo, Gambia. It is tied to one central bank: it audits the accounts of the Central Bank of The Gambia, checking the figures the bank publishes. The audit on record is for 2021, the bank's annual report and financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2021.
n:Royal Joh. Enschedé: Royal Joh. Enschede is a printing firm in Haarlem, in the Netherlands, tied to one central bank. The Banco Central de Sao Tome e Principe's own announcement of its 50-dobra commemorative note, marking 50 years of independence, says production was handled by Royal Joh. Enschede in the Netherlands. That was the commemorative note, not the notes in everyday circulation.
n:Banco de Portugal: Banco de Portugal is the state central bank in Lisbon, and the tie recorded here is to its own gold. Note 2 of its 2023 annual report, on gold and gold receivables, introduces a table of the institutions in which the gold was held and assigns 5,549,238 fine ounces, about 45 per cent of the 12,302,063-ounce total, to the line "In the country - Banco de Portugal". The reserve is 382.6 tonnes. The note says where the gold sits, not who manages it.
n:EY, Firm of Chartered Accountants: EY, Firm of Chartered Accountants is an accountancy firm in Gaborone, Botswana, tied to one central bank. It audits the accounts of the Bank of Botswana, and signed the independent auditor's report in that bank's annual report for 2025. Auditing the accounts means checking and reporting on the figures; it is not managing the bank's money.
n:Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiy: The Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye is a state body in Ankara, Türkiye, and it appears here as the keeper of its own gold. Its 2025 annual report records 34,015,944 grams, about 34 tonnes, of internationally standard gold held in the bank's own vaults, and states that gold which is not of international standard belongs to the bank and is held entirely in its vaults. That is safekeeping of bars, not the management of money.
n:Baker Tilly Bishkek LLC: Baker Tilly Bishkek LLC is an accounting firm based in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. It is tied to one central bank: it audits the accounts of the National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic, signing the independent auditor's report on the consolidated financial statements in that bank's annual report for 2025. Auditing the books is checking them, not running the bank's money.
n:Central Asian Secure Printing Typograp: Central Asian Secure Printing Typography LLC is a banknote printing firm in Kyrgyzstan. It began printing Kyrgyz som banknotes in September 2026, and the domestically printed 20- and 50-som notes entered circulation on 27 October; the Cabinet added the company to Kyrgyzstan's list of strategic facilities. Larger denominations are not yet produced inside the country. The National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic named De La Rue and Oberthur Fiduciaire as manufacturers in 2022 and Crane Currency in 2024. An earlier attempt by Uchkun OJSC in March 2025 produced 10-som notes that never circulated.
n:Borsa İstanbul: Borsa İstanbul is the Turkish exchange company, based in Istanbul. It is one of the three places where the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye keeps its gold, with 382,926,774 grams, about 382.9 tonnes, of internationally standard gold assigned to it. The central bank's 2025 annual report notes describe this as safekeeping rather than management of the holding, so the gold stays the central bank's.
n:Grant Thornton d.o.o. Banja Luka: Grant Thornton d.o.o. Banja Luka is an accounting firm based in Banja Luka, Bosnia. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and signed the independent auditors' report on that bank's financial statements for 2016. Auditing the accounts means checking the books, not holding or steering the bank's money.
n:Security Printing Works, Wazi (Central: Security Printing Works at Wazi is the Central Bank of Myanmar's own banknote plant, in Myanmar. It prints some of that bank's notes. Myanmar's new 20,000-kyat note, introduced on 31 July 2023, was printed there; that note is a commemorative issue, made to mark an occasion, rather than part of the everyday circulating series.
n:M/s P.K. Mitra & Company: M/s P.K. Mitra & Company is a firm based in Kolkata, India. It audits the accounts of the Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan, Bhutan's central bank, meaning it checks the authority's financial statements from outside rather than keeping them. Its audit of those accounts for 2003 and 2004 appears in the authority's annual report for that year.
n:Sudan Currency Printing Press: The Sudan Currency Printing Press is Sudan's state currency printing works, in Khartoum. One central bank is tied to it: the Central Bank of Somalia, whose new 2,000-shilling note is printed there. That is a circulating note, not a commemorative one, so Somalia's money is printed in Sudan rather than at home.
n:Ernst & Young d.o.o. Beograd: Ernst & Young d.o.o. Beograd is an accounting firm in Belgrade, Serbia. One central bank is tied to it: the National Bank of Serbia, whose accounts it audits. It signed the independent auditor's report on the bank's financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2025. Auditing the accounts is checking and reporting on them, not running the bank's money.
n:Banka Slovenije: Banka Slovenije is Slovenia's central bank, based in Ljubljana, and it keeps part of its own gold on its own premises. The gold note in its audited financial statements for 2024 separates the stock of gold held at Banka Slovenije from the remainder, described only as gold in foreign bank accounts; it names no foreign institution and gives no split by weight or value between the two locations. Total holdings at 31 December 2024 were 102,216 fine troy ounces, valued at 256,671 thousand euros.
n:Societe FMBZ - KPMG Tunisie and Societ: Societe FMBZ - KPMG Tunisie and Societe Cabinet C.M.C are accountancy firms in Tunis that together audit the accounts of the Central Bank of Tunisia, meaning they check its financial statements and sign off on them. They did so for 2025, and their joint auditors' report is published with the central bank's financial statements in its annual report for that year.
n:Deloitte Partners, Male': Deloitte Partners is an accountancy firm in Male, the capital of the Maldives. It audits the accounts of the Maldives Monetary Authority, the country's central bank, checking its financial statements and signing off on them. Its independent auditor's report for 2024 appears in the authority's annual report for that year.
n:Banco de Guatemala: Banco de Guatemala is the central bank of Guatemala, based in Guatemala City. It keeps much of its gold itself rather than abroad: its 2024 accounts record coined gold worth 2,431.2 million quetzales, or 315.5 million US dollars at 31 December 2024, in its own reserve vaults, out of total monetary gold of 4,458.9 million quetzales, 578.6 million US dollars. That is more than half the value of its monetary gold stored in its own vaults. No weight is given.
n:PricewaterhouseCoopers Services: PricewaterhouseCoopers Services is an accounting firm based in Bandar Seri Begawan, Brunei. It audits the accounts of the Brunei Darussalam Central Bank, which means it examines the bank's financial statements and signs a report on whether they give a true picture of its finances. It signed that report for the bank's 2025 annual accounts.
n:Uchkun: Uchkun is an open joint stock company based in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. It has printed some banknotes for the National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic: the Times of Central Asia reported on 25 March 2025 that new notes were being produced by Uchkun, after the National Bank's chairman announced that domestic production had begun with small denominations. The article reports the production without stating who owns the company.
n:Union Auditor General Office: The Union Auditor General Office, based in Nay Pyi Taw, Myanmar, is the government body that checks public accounts. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Myanmar, a duty set out in the Central Bank of Myanmar Law of 2013, passed by the Pyidaungsu Hluttaw as Law No. 16/2013. That is its one documented tie to a central bank, and it is an audit role, not an accusation.
n:Banco Central de Bolivia: Banco Central de Bolivia is the Bolivian state's central bank, in La Paz, and it stores part of its own gold. Its quarterly report on gold operations says that at 31 December 2024 about 2.62 tonnes sat in the bank's own vaults. The other 19.91 tonnes were deposited and invested in gold accounts at institutions in London - the Bank for International Settlements 0.27 tonnes, Bank of Montreal 1.00, BNP Paribas 3.89, JPMorgan Chase 2.77, Toronto-Dominion 5.50 and UBS 6.48 - which earns a return rather than being storage.
n:Crane NXT: Crane NXT is a firm based in Boston, in the United States, and it prints banknotes for Norges Bank, Norway's central bank. Norges Bank's own page on the notes says the 2016 to 2019 banknotes were printed by Oberthur Fiduciaire in France, and that from 2020 the printing is carried out by Crane NXT in Malta, while the banknote paper is produced in Sweden. The work takes place at the company's Malta plant.
n:BDO T&T: BDO T&T is an accounting firm in Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago, the country's central bank, and did so for 2024. The report of this comes from the Trinidad and Tobago Guardian, under the heading that the Auditor General declined to audit the central bank.
n:KPMG Georgia LLC: KPMG Georgia LLC is an accounting and auditing firm based in Tbilisi, Georgia. It audited the accounts of the National Bank of Georgia for the year ended 31 December 2020. The Independent Auditors' Report in the bank's 2020 annual report is dated 23 April 2021 at Tbilisi, with Karen Safaryan as engagement partner.
n:Deloitte & Touche with BDO (joint audi: This is a joint appointment of two accounting firms, Deloitte & Touche and BDO, auditing together as one engagement. The pair audited the accounts of the Central Bank of The Bahamas for 2011. The Independent Auditors' Report in that year's annual report carries both signature blocks, each signed as Chartered Accountants at Nassau on 16 April 2012, and names no individual partner. The bank's later annual reports print the auditors' report as a scanned image, so 2011 is the most recent year whose auditor can be read as text.
n:Coopers & Lybrand: Coopers & Lybrand was an accounting and auditing firm; its practice merged into PricewaterhouseCoopers in 1998. From its Suva office in Fiji it audited the accounts of the National Reserve Bank of Tonga for the year ended 30 June 1993. The Tonga Government Gazette published those accounts together with the auditor's report, signed at Suva on 21 September 1993. The auditor was a private firm rather than Tonga's Auditor General.
n:Ernst & Young Chartered Accountants: Ernst & Young Chartered Accountants is the Jamaican practice of the accounting and auditing firm Ernst & Young, at 8 Olivier Road, Kingston 8. It audits the accounts of the Bank of Jamaica. Its Independent Auditor's Report to the bank's Board of Directors, in the Annual Report 2025, is signed at Kingston on 4 March 2026 for the year ended 31 December 2025.
n:KPMG Afrique Centrale with Mazars Came: This is a joint appointment of two accounting firms, KPMG Afrique Centrale and Mazars Cameroun, auditing together as the commissaires aux comptes of the Banque des Etats de l'Afrique Centrale, the central bank shared by Cameroon, the Central African Republic, Chad, Congo-Brazzaville, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon. Their general report on the 2018 accounts is signed at Yaounde on 29 March 2019, by Odile Ndzana for KPMG Afrique Centrale and Jules Alain Njall Bikok for Mazars Cameroun, each as Associe. The document is a scan with no text layer, and the names were read off the rendered page.
n:PricewaterhouseCoopers SRL: PricewaterhouseCoopers SRL is the Barbadian practice of the accounting and auditing firm PricewaterhouseCoopers, at The Financial Services Centre, Bishop's Court Hill. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Barbados, which means it examines the bank's financial statements and signs a report saying whether they give a fair picture of its finances. Its report sits at pages 61 to 64 of the bank's Annual Report 2025 and is dated at Bridgetown on 27 March 2026, for the year ended 31 December 2025. The report says it is made to the board of directors under section 67 of the Central Bank of Barbados Act, 2020.
n:KPMG Fakhro: KPMG Fakhro is the Bahraini practice of the accounting and auditing firm KPMG, at the 12th floor of Fakhro Tower in Manama. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Bahrain. Its report on the bank's financial statements for the period ended 31 December 2023 is signed on 10 March 2024 under partner registration number 213, and says the statements are prepared in line with the basis of accounting the bank sets out in note 2 to those statements rather than with a general accounting standard.
n:SNG Grant Thornton Chartered Accountan: SNG Grant Thornton Chartered Accountants (Eswatini) is an accounting firm at Lot 195 Kal Grant Street, Mbabane, and part of the Grant Thornton network. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Eswatini. Its report on the bank's financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2026 is signed on 26 August 2026, and the directors' report in the same document names the firm as the bank's external auditor.
n:Forvis Mazars Cameroun SA: Forvis Mazars Cameroun SA is the Cameroonian practice of the accounting and auditing firm Forvis Mazars. It audits the accounts of the Bank of the Republic of Burundi. Its report on the bank's financial statements for the year ended 30 June 2023 is signed at Bujumbura on 6 August 2026 by the partner Jules Alain Njall Bikok, and the signature block gives the firm's CEMAC approval number SEC 034 and its ONECCA approval number SEC 017. The same partner signed the 2018 statutory auditors' report for the Bank of Central African States, which issues the currency used by six countries to Burundi's west.
n:Howladar Yunus & Co. and ACNABIN, Char: Howladar Yunus & Co. and ACNABIN are two firms of chartered accountants in Dhaka that audit Bangladesh Bank's accounts together, each signing the same report. Their Independent Auditors' Report on the bank's accounts for 2024-2025 is signed at Dhaka on 26 August 2025, by Muhammad Farooq FCA for Howladar Yunus & Co. and Abu Sayed Mohammed Nayeem FCA for ACNABIN, both managing partners. It is addressed not to the bank's board but to the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, which the Bangladesh Bank Order 1972 requires to publish the bank's certified accounts. The report also records that the previous year's statements were audited by Howladar Yunus & Co. with a different second firm, Hoda Vasi Chowdhury & Co.
n:KPMG S.A. and Merove-Pierre - Cabinet: KPMG S.A., the French firm in the KPMG network, and Merove-Pierre - Cabinet d'Experts-Comptables, an accounting firm at 7 rue Lechaud, Bourdon, Port-au-Prince, audit the accounts of the Bank of the Republic of Haiti together. Their report on the year ended 30 September 2021 is signed at Paris La Defense and Port-au-Prince on 30 June 2022, by the KPMG partner Valery Fousse and by Mireille Merove-Pierre, managing partner of the Haitian firm. The bank publishes the report on its own site, along with the report for the previous year and a public call for firms to bid for the work.
Solution S.r.l. is an accounting firm at Via XXVIII Luglio 212 in Borgo Maggiore, San Marino, entered in the republic's register of companies in March 2007 and at number 11 of its register of statutory auditors. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of the Republic of San Marino under article 23(3) of Law 96 of 29 June 2005, the bank's statute, and reports to the bank's shareholders rather than to its board. Its report on the accounts for the year ended 31 December 2025 is signed at San Marino on 5 May 2026 and gives an unqualified opinion. It belongs to no international accounting network, which makes San Marino one of the few central banks audited by a purely local firm.
n:Ernst & Young RDC: Ernst & Young RDC is the Congolese practice of the accounting and auditing firm Ernst & Young, at Immeuble Onze Treize, 110 Boulevard du 30 juin, Gombe, Kinshasa. It audits the accounts of the Banque Centrale du Congo and reports to the bank's Conseil. Its report on the year ended 31 December 2024 gives an unqualified opinion and says the audit followed international standards on auditing under OHADA Regulation 01/2017, the accounting and audit rules shared by seventeen African countries. The governor's own foreword to the same annual report states that the bank's accounts were audited and certified without reserve by the firm.
